1→import React, {
     2→  createContext,
     3→  useState,
     4→  useContext,
     5→  ReactNode,
     6→  useEffect,
     7→  useMemo
     8→} from 'react';
     9→import { supabase } from '@/integrations/supabase/client';
    10→import type { Session } from '@supabase/supabase-js';
    11→
    12→interface AuthContextType {
    13→  /** Current authenticated user ID, null if not logged in */
    14→  userId: string | null;
    15→  /** Whether the user is authenticated */
    16→  isAuthenticated: boolean;
    17→  /** Whether the initial auth check is still in progress */
    18→  isLoading: boolean;
    19→}
    20→
    21→const AuthContext = createContext<AuthContextType | undefined>(undefined);
    22→
    23→/**
    24→ * AuthProvider handles authentication state and event debouncing.
    25→ *
    26→ * Features:
    27→ * - [AuthDebounce] Debounces duplicate auth events to prevent cascading updates
    28→ * - [MobileStallFix] Resets loading states on meaningful auth transitions
    29→ * - [FastResume] Provides immediate auth state for fast tab resume
    30→ */
    31→export const AuthProvider = ({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) => {
    32→  const [userId, setUserId] = useState<string | undefined>(undefined);
    33→  const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(true);
    34→
    35→  // [MobileStallFix] Enhanced auth state tracking with mobile recovery
    36→  // [AuthDebounce] Prevent cascading updates from duplicate auth events
    37→  useEffect(() => {
    38→    let authStateChangeCount = 0;
    39→    let debounceTimeout: NodeJS.Timeout | null = null;
    40→    let lastProcessedState: { event: string; userId: string | undefined } | null = null;
    41→    let pendingAuthState: { event: string; session: Session | null } | null = null;
    42→
    43→    const processAuthChange = (event: string, session: Session | null) => {
    44→      const currentUserId = session?.user?.id;
    45→
    46→      // Check if this is a meaningful state transition
    47→      const isDuplicateEvent = lastProcessedState &&
    48→        lastProcessedState.event === event &&
    49→        lastProcessedState.userId === currentUserId;
    50→
    51→      if (isDuplicateEvent) {
    52→        return;
    53→      }
    54→
    55→      // Update user ID
    56→      setUserId(currentUserId);
    57→
    58→      // Track the processed state
    59→      lastProcessedState = { event, userId: currentUserId };
    60→    };
    61→
    62→    const handleAuthStateChange = (event: string, session: Session | null) => {
    63→      authStateChangeCount++;
    64→
    65→      // Store the latest auth state
    66→      pendingAuthState = { event, session };
    67→
    68→      // Clear existing debounce timer
    69→      if (debounceTimeout) {
    70→        clearTimeout(debounceTimeout);
    71→      }
    72→
    73→      // [AuthDebounce] Wait 150ms for additional auth events before processing
    74→      debounceTimeout = setTimeout(() => {
    75→        if (pendingAuthState) {
    76→          const { event: pendingEvent, session: pendingSession } = pendingAuthState;
    77→          React.startTransition(() => {
    78→            processAuthChange(pendingEvent, pendingSession);
    79→          });
    80→          pendingAuthState = null;
    81→        }
    82→        debounceTimeout = null;
    83→      }, 150);
    84→    };
    85→
    86→    supabase.auth.getSession().then(({ data: { session } }) => {
    87→      setUserId(session?.user?.id);
    88→      setIsLoading(false);
    89→      lastProcessedState = { event: 'INITIAL_SESSION', userId: session?.user?.id };
    90→    });
    91→
    92→    // Use centralized auth manager instead of direct listener
    93→    const authManager = window.__AUTH_MANAGER__;
    94→    let unsubscribe: (() => void) | null = null;
    95→
    96→    if (authManager) {
    97→      unsubscribe = authManager.subscribe('AuthContext', handleAuthStateChange);
    98→    } else {
    99→      // Fallback to direct listener if auth manager not available
   100→      const { data: listener } = supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange(handleAuthStateChange);
   101→      unsubscribe = () => listener.subscription.unsubscribe();
   102→    }
   103→
   104→    return () => {
   105→      if (unsubscribe) unsubscribe();
   106→      if (debounceTimeout) {
   107→        clearTimeout(debounceTimeout);
   108→        // Process final pending state on cleanup if needed
   109→        if (pendingAuthState) {
   110→          processAuthChange(pendingAuthState.event, pendingAuthState.session);
   111→        }
   112→      }
   113→    };
   114→  }, []);
   115→
   116→  const contextValue = useMemo(
   117→    () => ({
   118→      userId: userId ?? null,
   119→      isAuthenticated: !!userId,
   120→      isLoading,
   121→    }),
   122→    [userId, isLoading]
   123→  );
   124→
   125→  return (
   126→    <AuthContext.Provider value={contextValue}>
   127→      {children}
   128→    </AuthContext.Provider>
   129→  );
   130→};
   131→
   132→/**
   133→ * Hook to access authentication state.
   134→ *
   135→ * @returns { userId, isAuthenticated }
   136→ */
   137→export const useAuth = () => {
   138→  const context = useContext(AuthContext);
   139→  if (context === undefined) {
   140→    const errorMessage = 'useAuth must be used within an AuthProvider. ' +
   141→      'Make sure the component is rendered inside the AuthProvider tree.';
   142→    console.error('[AuthContext]', errorMessage, {
   143→      stack: new Error().stack,
   144→    });
   145→    throw new Error(errorMessage);
   146→  }
   147→  return context;
   148→};
   149→

1→import { createContext, useContext, ReactNode, useEffect, useMemo } from 'react';
     2→import { Project } from '@/types/project';
     3→import { useAuth } from './AuthContext';
     4→import { useUserSettings } from './UserSettingsContext';
     5→import { useProjectSelection } from '@/shared/hooks/useProjectSelection';
     6→import { useProjectCRUD } from '@/shared/hooks/useProjectCRUD';
     7→import { useProjectDefaults } from '@/shared/hooks/useProjectDefaults';
     8→
     9→// Type for updating projects (re-exported for consumers that may need it)
    10→interface ProjectUpdate {
    11→  name?: string;
    12→  aspectRatio?: string;
    13→}
    14→
    15→interface ProjectContextType {
    16→  projects: Project[];
    17→  selectedProjectId: string | null;
    18→  setSelectedProjectId: (projectId: string | null) => void;
    19→  isLoadingProjects: boolean;
    20→  fetchProjects: () => Promise<void>;
    21→  addNewProject: (projectData: { name: string; aspectRatio: string }) => Promise<Project | null>;
    22→  isCreatingProject: boolean;
    23→  updateProject: (projectId: string, updates: ProjectUpdate) => Promise<boolean>;
    24→  isUpdatingProject: boolean;
    25→  deleteProject: (projectId: string) => Promise<boolean>;
    26→  isDeletingProject: boolean;
    27→  /** Current authenticated user ID, null if not logged in */
    28→  userId: string | null;
    29→}
    30→
    31→const ProjectContext = createContext<ProjectContextType | undefined>(undefined);
    32→
    33→export const ProjectProvider = ({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) => {
    34→  const { userId } = useAuth();
    35→  const { userSettings: userPreferences, isLoadingSettings: isLoadingPreferences, updateUserSettings } = useUserSettings();
    36→
    37→  // ── Selection: owns selectedProjectId, localStorage persistence, cross-device sync ──
    38→  const selection = useProjectSelection({
    39→    userId: userId ?? null,
    40→    userPreferences,
    41→    isLoadingPreferences,
    42→    updateUserSettings,
    43→  });
    44→
    45→  // ── CRUD: owns projects list, loading flags, fetch/create/update/delete ──
    46→  const crud = useProjectCRUD({
    47→    selectedProjectId: selection.selectedProjectId,
    48→    onProjectsLoaded: selection.handleProjectsLoaded,
    49→    onProjectCreated: selection.handleProjectCreated,
    50→    onProjectDeleted: selection.handleProjectDeleted,
    51→    updateUserSettings,
    52→  });
    53→
    54→  // ── Side effects: fetch trigger, cross-device sync, prefetch, mobile fallback ──
    55→  useProjectDefaults({
    56→    userId: userId ?? null,
    57→    selectedProjectId: selection.selectedProjectId,
    58→    isLoadingProjects: crud.isLoadingProjects,
    59→    isLoadingPreferences,
    60→    projects: crud.projects,
    61→    fetchProjects: crud.fetchProjects,
    62→    applyCrossDeviceSync: selection.applyCrossDeviceSync,
    63→  });
    64→
    65→  // ── Expose context snapshot for hooks that need project ID outside React context ──
    66→  // This is a [structural] global (not debug-only) — consumed by useProjectGenerations,
    67→  // useTasks, and ImageGenerationToolPage as a fallback when projectId isn't passed as a prop.
    68→  useEffect(() => {
    69→    if (typeof window !== 'undefined') {
    70→      window.__PROJECT_CONTEXT__ = {
    71→        selectedProjectId: selection.selectedProjectId,
    72→        projects: crud.projects,
    73→      };
    74→    }
    75→  }, [selection.selectedProjectId, crud.projects]);
    76→
    77→  // ── Build context value ──
    78→  const contextValue = useMemo(
    79→    (): ProjectContextType => ({
    80→      projects: crud.projects || [],
    81→      selectedProjectId: selection.selectedProjectId,
    82→      setSelectedProjectId: selection.setSelectedProjectId,
    83→      isLoadingProjects: crud.isLoadingProjects,
    84→      fetchProjects: crud.fetchProjects,
    85→      addNewProject: crud.addNewProject,
    86→      isCreatingProject: crud.isCreatingProject,
    87→      updateProject: crud.updateProject,
    88→      isUpdatingProject: crud.isUpdatingProject,
    89→      deleteProject: crud.deleteProject,
    90→      isDeletingProject: crud.isDeletingProject,
    91→      userId: userId ?? null,
    92→    }),
    93→    [
    94→      crud.projects,
    95→      selection.selectedProjectId,
    96→      selection.setSelectedProjectId,
    97→      crud.isLoadingProjects,
    98→      crud.fetchProjects,
    99→      crud.addNewProject,
   100→      crud.isCreatingProject,
   101→      crud.updateProject,
   102→      crud.isUpdatingProject,
   103→      crud.deleteProject,
   104→      crud.isDeletingProject,
   105→      userId,
   106→    ]
   107→  );
   108→
   109→  return (
   110→    <ProjectContext.Provider value={contextValue}>
   111→      {children}
   112→    </ProjectContext.Provider>
   113→  );
   114→};
   115→
   116→export const useProject = () => {
   117→  const context = useContext(ProjectContext);
   118→  if (context === undefined) {
   119→    const errorMessage = 'useProject must be used within a ProjectProvider. ' +
   120→      'Make sure the component is rendered inside the ProjectProvider tree. ' +
   121→      'Check that the component is not being rendered outside of App.tsx or in an error boundary that is outside the provider.';

   127→  }

   120→  child_order?: number | null;
   121→  // FK reference to shot_generations for video-to-timeline slot matching
   122→  // When the referenced shot_generation is deleted, this becomes null (ON DELETE SET NULL)
   123→  pair_shot_generation_id?: string | null;
   124→  // FK to the primary variant record (generation_variants.id)
   125→  primary_variant_id?: string | null;
   126→}
   127→
   128→/**
   129→ * Type for timeline-specific images that guarantees required fields
   130→ * Use this type when you need to read pair prompts or timeline positions
   131→ * 
   132→ * @example
   133→ * ```typescript
   134→ * const timelineImages = images.filter(isTimelineGeneration);
   135→ * // Now TypeScript knows timelineImages[0].metadata exists
   136→ * const pairPrompt = timelineImages[0].metadata.pair_prompt;
   137→ * ```
   138→ */
   139→interface TimelineGenerationRow extends GenerationRow {
   140→  timeline_frame: number; // Required for timeline positioning
   141→  metadata: GenerationMetadata; // Required for pair prompts and timeline metadata
   142→}
   143→
   144→export interface Shot {
   145→  id: string;
   146→  name: string;
   147→  images: GenerationRow[]; // This will be populated by joining data
   148→  created_at?: string; // Optional, matches the DB schema
   149→  updated_at?: string | null; // Optional, matches the DB schema
   150→  project_id?: string; // Add project_id here
   151→  aspect_ratio?: string | null; // Aspect ratio for shot video generation
   152→  position: number; // Position for manual ordering
   153→  
   154→  // Pre-computed stats (computed in useListShots, used to avoid reactive flicker)
   155→  imageCount?: number;
   156→  positionedImageCount?: number;
   157→  unpositionedImageCount?: number;
   158→  hasUnpositionedImages?: boolean;
   159→}
   160→
   161→interface ShotImage {
   162→  shot_id: string;
   163→  generation_id: string; // Assuming generation_id is a string. If it's BIGINT, this might be number.
   164→  timeline_frame?: number;
   165→}

## Testing Patterns in Reigh

### 1. **Vitest Import & Setup**

**Explicit imports** (NOT using global mode):
```typescript
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
```

However, the `vitest.config.ts` has `globals: true` enabled:
```typescript
export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    globals: true,        // Global test functions available
    environment: 'jsdom',
    include: ['src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}'],
  },
});
```

This means while globals are available, the codebase **explicitly imports** `describe`, `it`, `expect` anyway (best practice for clarity).

---

### 2. **Mock Setup Patterns**

**Simple global mocks** (NetworkStatusManager.test.ts):
```typescript
const mockNavigator = {
  onLine: true,
  connection: {
    effectiveType: '4g',
    addEventListener: vi.fn(),
    removeEventListener: vi.fn(),
  }
};

Object.defineProperty(global, 'navigator', {
  value: mockNavigator,
  writable: true
});
```

**Lifecycle hooks** (beforeEach):
```typescript
beforeEach(() => {
  vi.clearAllMocks();
  manager = new NetworkStatusManager();
});
```

**Mock functions** with `vi.fn()`:
- Used to track calls: `expect(mockWindow.addEventListener).toHaveBeenCalledWith(...)`
- Supports: `toHaveBeenCalled()`, `toHaveBeenCalledTimes()`, `toHaveBeenCalledWith()`

---

### 3. **Test Structure Patterns**

**Nested describes** for organizing related tests:
```typescript
describe('NetworkStatusManager', () => {
  describe('initialization', () => {
    it('should initialize with current network status', () => { ... });
    it('should set up event listeners when initialized', () => { ... });
  });
  
  describe('network status detection', () => {
    it('should detect slow connections', () => { ... });
  });
});
```

**Simple function tests** (no mocking):
```typescript
describe('deepEqual', () => {
  it('returns true for identical primitives', () => {
    expect(deepEqual(1, 1)).toBe(true);
  });
});
```

---

### 4. **Assertion Patterns**

Common matchers used:
- `.toBe()` - strict equality
- `.toEqual()` - deep equality
- `.toBeNull()` / `.toBeUndefined()`
- `.toHaveBeenCalledWith()` - mock verification
- `.toHaveBeenCalledTimes()`
- `.toBeInstanceOf()`
- `.not.toBe()` / `.not.toHaveBeenCalled()`

---

### 5. **Test Utilities**

No custom test utility files observed. Tests use:
- **Standard vitest functions**: `describe`, `it`, `expect`, `beforeEach`
- **Vitest mock API**: `vi.fn()`, `vi.clearAllMocks()`
- **Object.defineProperty** for global mocks
- **Direct instantiation** of classes being tested

---

### Key Takeaways:
1. Tests live in `__tests__` directories with `.test.ts` suffix
2. Simple, readable tests with minimal setup
3. Explicit imports preferred even with globals enabled
4. Mocks handled via `vi.fn()` and `Object.defineProperty`
5. Organized with nested `describe` blocks
6. No custom test utilities or fixtures library (simple inline mocks)

## Exported Types & Context Shapes

### 1. **AuthContext.tsx**

**Exported Interface:**
```typescript
interface AuthContextType {
  /** Current authenticated user ID, null if not logged in */
  userId: string | null;
  /** Whether the user is authenticated */
  isAuthenticated: boolean;
  /** Whether the initial auth check is still in progress */
  isLoading: boolean;
}
```

**Export:**
- `AuthProvider` - Context provider component
- `useAuth()` - Hook to access auth context

---

### 2. **ProjectContext.tsx**

**Exported Interface:**
```typescript
interface ProjectContextType {
  projects: Project[];
  selectedProjectId: string | null;
  setSelectedProjectId: (projectId: string | null) => void;
  isLoadingProjects: boolean;
  fetchProjects: () => Promise<void>;
  addNewProject: (projectData: { name: string; aspectRatio: string }) => Promise<Project | null>;
  isCreatingProject: boolean;
  updateProject: (projectId: string, updates: ProjectUpdate) => Promise<boolean>;
  isUpdatingProject: boolean;
  deleteProject: (projectId: string) => Promise<boolean>;
  isDeletingProject: boolean;
  /** Current authenticated user ID, null if not logged in */
  userId: string | null;
}

interface ProjectUpdate {
  name?: string;
  aspectRatio?: string;
}
```

**Related Type:**
```typescript
interface Project {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  user_id: string;
  aspectRatio?: string;
  createdAt?: string;
}
```

**Exports:**
- `ProjectProvider` - Context provider component
- `useProject()` - Hook to access project context

---

### 3. **Supabase Client** (`src/integrations/supabase/client.ts`)

**Export:**
```typescript
export const supabase = getOrCreateSupabaseClient();
// Type: ReturnType<typeof createClient<Database>>
```

**Key Details:**
- Singleton pattern using `window.__supabase_client__`
- Typed with `Database` from `@/integrations/supabase/types`
- Configured with auth, realtime, and custom fetch handling
- Initializes:
  - `ReconnectScheduler`
  - `AuthStateManager` (exposes `window.__AUTH_MANAGER__`)
  - Realtime instrumentation
  - Dev auto-login (dev-only)

**Window globals for context fallback:**
- `window.__PROJECT_CONTEXT__` - { selectedProjectId, projects }
- `window.__AUTH_MANAGER__` - Auth event subscription manager
- `window.__supabase_client__` - Direct supabase client reference

---

## Mock Factory Recommendations

For your mock factories, you'll want:

1. **AuthContextType mock**: Simple values for `userId`, `isAuthenticated`, `isLoading`
2. **ProjectContextType mock**: Arrays for `projects`, functions that return resolved Promises, loading flags
3. **Supabase client mock**: You'll likely need to mock the specific methods you use (e.g., `auth.getSession()`, `from()` queries)
4. **Window globals**: Set up `__PROJECT_CONTEXT__`, `__AUTH_MANAGER__` if your tests need them

All three contexts use `useMemo` to stabilize values, so reference equality matters if you're testing context consumers.

// ===== SINGLE-ITEM VARIANT CREATION =====

/**
 * Create variant on parent for single-item cases
 */
export async function createSingleItemVariant(
  ctx: HandlerContext,
  parentGenerationId: string
): Promise<any | null> {
  const { supabase, taskId, taskData, publicUrl, thumbnailUrl, childOrder } = ctx;

  // Check if this is first variant on parent
  const { count: existingVariantCount } = await supabase
    .from('generation_variants')
    .select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true })
    .eq('generation_id', parentGenerationId);
  const isFirstVariant = (existingVariantCount || 0) === 0;

  const toolType = taskData.params?.full_orchestrator_payload?.tool_type ||
                   taskData.params?.tool_type ||
                   taskData.tool_type;

  const variantType = taskData.variant_type || VARIANT_TYPE_DEFAULT;

  const result = await createVariantOnParent(
    supabase, parentGenerationId, publicUrl, thumbnailUrl, taskData, taskId,
    variantType,
    {
      tool_type: toolType,
      created_from: 'single_item_completion',
      is_single_item: true,
      child_order: childOrder ?? 0,
    },
    null,
    isFirstVariant
  );

  return result;
}

 * Find existing generation at a position (for variant creation)

  supabase: any,

    52→        } else {
    53→          pathValid = false;

    55→        }
    56→      }

   171→/**
   172→ * Set thumbnail URL in params at the correct location based on task_type
   173→ * @returns Updated params object (does not mutate original)
   174→ */
   175→export function setThumbnailInParams(
   176→  params: Record<string, any>,
   177→  taskType: string,
   178→  thumbnailUrl: string
   179→): Record<string, any> {
   180→  const config = THUMBNAIL_PATH_CONFIG[taskType] || THUMBNAIL_PATH_CONFIG.default;
   181→  const updatedParams = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(params || {})); // Deep clone
   182→
   183→  // Navigate to parent path and ensure it exists
   184→  let target = updatedParams;
   185→  for (let i = 0; i < config.path.length - 1; i++) {
   186→    const key = config.path[i];
   187→    if (!target[key]) {
   188→      target[key] = {};
   189→    }
   190→    target = target[key];
   191→  }
   192→
   193→  // Set the thumbnail URL
   194→  const finalKey = config.path[config.path.length - 1];
   195→  target[finalKey] = thumbnailUrl;
   196→
   197→  // Set any extras (e.g., accelerated=false for travel_stitch)
   198→  if (config.extras) {
   199→    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(config.extras)) {
   200→      target[key] = value;
   201→    }
   202→  }
   203→
   204→  return updatedParams;
   205→}

   209→/**
   210→ * Get MIME content type from filename extension
   211→ */
   212→export function getContentType(filename: string): string {
   213→  const ext = filename.toLowerCase().split('.').pop();
   214→  switch (ext) {
   215→    case 'png':
   216→      return 'image/png';
   217→    case 'jpg':
   218→    case 'jpeg':
   219→      return 'image/jpeg';
   220→    case 'gif':
   221→      return 'image/gif';
   222→    case 'webp':
   223→      return 'image/webp';
   224→    case 'mp4':
   225→      return 'video/mp4';
   226→    case 'webm':
   227→      return 'video/webm';
   228→    case 'mov':
   229→      return 'video/quicktime';
   230→    default:
   231→      return 'application/octet-stream';
   232→  }
   233→}
   234→
   235→/**
   236→ * Build generation params starting from normalized task params
   237→ */
   238→export function buildGenerationParams(
   239→  baseParams: any,
   240→  toolType: string,
   241→  contentType?: string,
   242→  shotId?: string,
   243→  thumbnailUrl?: string,
   244→  sourceTaskId?: string
   245→): any {
   246→  let generationParams = { ...baseParams };
   247→
   248→  // Add tool_type to the params JSONB
   249→  generationParams.tool_type = toolType;
   250→
   251→  // Add source_task_id if provided
   252→  // IMPORTANT: This is used by the auto_view_manual_upload_variant trigger
   253→  // to distinguish task-created generations (which should show NEW badge)
   254→  // from manual uploads (which should be auto-marked as viewed)
   255→  if (sourceTaskId) {
   256→    generationParams.source_task_id = sourceTaskId;
   257→  }
   258→
   259→  // Add content_type to params for download/display purposes
   260→  if (contentType) {
   261→    generationParams.content_type = contentType;
   262→  }
   263→
   264→  // Add shot_id if present and valid
   265→  if (shotId) {
   266→    generationParams.shotId = shotId;
   267→  }
   268→
   269→  // Add thumbnail_url to params if available
   270→  if (thumbnailUrl) {
   271→    generationParams.thumbnailUrl = thumbnailUrl;
   272→  }
   273→
   274→  return generationParams;
   275→}
   276→
   277→

}

### Key Invariants for Mock Factories

1. **Generation/Variant relationship**: 
   - `generations` now has `primary_variant_id` pointing to the actual output in `generation_variants`
   - `generation_variants.is_primary` ensures only one primary per generation
   - Variants have their own `location`, `thumbnail_url`, `params`, `variant_type`

2. **Timeline/Shot positioning**:
   - `shot_generations.timeline_frame` is nullable - unpositioned items have `null`
   - `generations.pair_shot_generation_id` is an FK that can cascade to `null`
   - `shot_generations.id` is the actual timeline entry ID (different from `generation_id`)

3. **Generation hierarchy**:
   - `parent_generation_id` + `is_child` + `child_order` = child relationship
   - `based_on` = variant lineage (magic edits, variations)
   - Both can exist on same row

4. **Task params are polymorphic**:
   - Different task types nest critical fields at different paths
   - Path priority: `['field']` → `['orchestrator_details', 'field']` → `['full_orchestrator_payload', 'field']`
   - Always deep clone params when setting values

5. **Status enum**: `'Queued' | 'In Progress' | 'Complete' | 'Failed' | 'Cancelled'`

1→import React, {
     2→  createContext,
     3→  useState,
     4→  useContext,
     5→  ReactNode,
     6→  useEffect,
     7→  useMemo
     8→} from 'react';
     9→import { supabase } from '@/integrations/supabase/client';
    10→import type { Session } from '@supabase/supabase-js';
    11→
    12→interface AuthContextType {
    13→  /** Current authenticated user ID, null if not logged in */
    14→  userId: string | null;
    15→  /** Whether the user is authenticated */
    16→  isAuthenticated: boolean;
    17→  /** Whether the initial auth check is still in progress */
    18→  isLoading: boolean;
    19→}
    20→
    21→const AuthContext = createContext<AuthContextType | undefined>(undefined);
    22→
    23→/**
    24→ * AuthProvider handles authentication state and event debouncing.
    25→ *
    26→ * Features:
    27→ * - [AuthDebounce] Debounces duplicate auth events to prevent cascading updates
    28→ * - [MobileStallFix] Resets loading states on meaningful auth transitions
    29→ * - [FastResume] Provides immediate auth state for fast tab resume
    30→ */
    31→export const AuthProvider = ({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) => {
    32→  const [userId, setUserId] = useState<string | undefined>(undefined);
    33→  const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(true);
    34→
    35→  // [MobileStallFix] Enhanced auth state tracking with mobile recovery
    36→  // [AuthDebounce] Prevent cascading updates from duplicate auth events
    37→  useEffect(() => {
    38→    let authStateChangeCount = 0;
    39→    let debounceTimeout: NodeJS.Timeout | null = null;
    40→    let lastProcessedState: { event: string; userId: string | undefined } | null = null;
    41→    let pendingAuthState: { event: string; session: Session | null } | null = null;
    42→
    43→    const processAuthChange = (event: string, session: Session | null) => {
    44→      const currentUserId = session?.user?.id;
    45→
    46→      // Check if this is a meaningful state transition
    47→      const isDuplicateEvent = lastProcessedState &&
    48→        lastProcessedState.event === event &&
    49→        lastProcessedState.userId === currentUserId;
    50→
    51→      if (isDuplicateEvent) {
    52→        return;
    53→      }
    54→
    55→      // Update user ID
    56→      setUserId(currentUserId);
    57→
    58→      // Track the processed state
    59→      lastProcessedState = { event, userId: currentUserId };
    60→    };
    61→
    62→    const handleAuthStateChange = (event: string, session: Session | null) => {
    63→      authStateChangeCount++;
    64→
    65→      // Store the latest auth state
    66→      pendingAuthState = { event, session };
    67→
    68→      // Clear existing debounce timer
    69→      if (debounceTimeout) {
    70→        clearTimeout(debounceTimeout);
    71→      }
    72→
    73→      // [AuthDebounce] Wait 150ms for additional auth events before processing
    74→      debounceTimeout = setTimeout(() => {
    75→        if (pendingAuthState) {
    76→          const { event: pendingEvent, session: pendingSession } = pendingAuthState;
    77→          React.startTransition(() => {
    78→            processAuthChange(pendingEvent, pendingSession);
    79→          });
    80→          pendingAuthState = null;
    81→        }
    82→        debounceTimeout = null;
    83→      }, 150);
    84→    };
    85→
    86→    supabase.auth.getSession().then(({ data: { session } }) => {
    87→      setUserId(session?.user?.id);
    88→      setIsLoading(false);
    89→      lastProcessedState = { event: 'INITIAL_SESSION', userId: session?.user?.id };
    90→    });
    91→
    92→    // Use centralized auth manager instead of direct listener
    93→    const authManager = window.__AUTH_MANAGER__;
    94→    let unsubscribe: (() => void) | null = null;
    95→
    96→    if (authManager) {
    97→      unsubscribe = authManager.subscribe('AuthContext', handleAuthStateChange);
    98→    } else {
    99→      // Fallback to direct listener if auth manager not available
   100→      const { data: listener } = supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange(handleAuthStateChange);
   101→      unsubscribe = () => listener.subscription.unsubscribe();
   102→    }
   103→
   104→    return () => {
   105→      if (unsubscribe) unsubscribe();
   106→      if (debounceTimeout) {
   107→        clearTimeout(debounceTimeout);
   108→        // Process final pending state on cleanup if needed
   109→        if (pendingAuthState) {
   110→          processAuthChange(pendingAuthState.event, pendingAuthState.session);
   111→        }
   112→      }
   113→    };
   114→  }, []);
   115→
   116→  const contextValue = useMemo(
   117→    () => ({
   118→      userId: userId ?? null,
   119→      isAuthenticated: !!userId,
   120→      isLoading,
   121→    }),
   122→    [userId, isLoading]
   123→  );
   124→
   125→  return (
   126→    <AuthContext.Provider value={contextValue}>
   127→      {children}
   128→    </AuthContext.Provider>
   129→  );
   130→};
   131→
   132→/**
   133→ * Hook to access authentication state.
   134→ *
   135→ * @returns { userId, isAuthenticated }
   136→ */
   137→export const useAuth = () => {
   138→  const context = useContext(AuthContext);
   139→  if (context === undefined) {
   140→    const errorMessage = 'useAuth must be used within an AuthProvider. ' +
   141→      'Make sure the component is rendered inside the AuthProvider tree.';
   142→    console.error('[AuthContext]', errorMessage, {
   143→      stack: new Error().stack,
   144→    });
   145→    throw new Error(errorMessage);
   146→  }
   147→  return context;
   148→};
   149→

     7→import { useProjectDefaults } from '@/shared/hooks/useProjectDefaults';
     8→
     9→// Type for updating projects (re-exported for consumers that may need it)
    10→interface ProjectUpdate {
    11→  name?: string;
    12→  aspectRatio?: string;
    13→}
    14→
    15→interface ProjectContextType {
    16→  projects: Project[];
    17→  selectedProjectId: string | null;
    18→  setSelectedProjectId: (projectId: string | null) => void;
    19→  isLoadingProjects: boolean;
    20→  fetchProjects: () => Promise<void>;
    21→  addNewProject: (projectData: { name: string; aspectRatio: string }) => Promise<Project | null>;
    22→  isCreatingProject: boolean;
    23→  updateProject: (projectId: string, updates: ProjectUpdate) => Promise<boolean>;
    24→  isUpdatingProject: boolean;
    25→  deleteProject: (projectId: string) => Promise<boolean>;
    26→  isDeletingProject: boolean;
    27→  /** Current authenticated user ID, null if not logged in */
    28→  userId: string | null;
    29→}
    30→
    31→const ProjectContext = createContext<ProjectContextType | undefined>(undefined);
    32→
    33→export const ProjectProvider = ({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) => {
    34→  const { userId } = useAuth();
    35→  const { userSettings: userPreferences, isLoadingSettings: isLoadingPreferences, updateUserSettings } = useUserSettings();
    36→
    37→  // ── Selection: owns selectedProjectId, localStorage persistence, cross-device sync ──
    38→  const selection = useProjectSelection({
    39→    userId: userId ?? null,
    40→    userPreferences,
    41→    isLoadingPreferences,
    42→    updateUserSettings,
    43→  });
    44→
    45→  // ── CRUD: owns projects list, loading flags, fetch/create/update/delete ──
    46→  const crud = useProjectCRUD({
    47→    selectedProjectId: selection.selectedProjectId,
    48→    onProjectsLoaded: selection.handleProjectsLoaded,
    49→    onProjectCreated: selection.handleProjectCreated,
    50→    onProjectDeleted: selection.handleProjectDeleted,
    51→    updateUserSettings,
    52→  });
    53→
    54→  // ── Side effects: fetch trigger, cross-device sync, prefetch, mobile fallback ──
    55→  useProjectDefaults({
    56→    userId: userId ?? null,
    57→    selectedProjectId: selection.selectedProjectId,
    58→    isLoadingProjects: crud.isLoadingProjects,
    59→    isLoadingPreferences,
    60→    projects: crud.projects,
    61→    fetchProjects: crud.fetchProjects,
    62→    applyCrossDeviceSync: selection.applyCrossDeviceSync,
    63→  });
    64→
    65→  // ── Expose context snapshot for hooks that need project ID outside React context ──
    66→  // This is a [structural] global (not debug-only) — consumed by useProjectGenerations,
    67→  // useTasks, and ImageGenerationToolPage as a fallback when projectId isn't passed as a prop.
    68→  useEffect(() => {
    69→    if (typeof window !== 'undefined') {
    70→      window.__PROJECT_CONTEXT__ = {
    71→        selectedProjectId: selection.selectedProjectId,
    72→        projects: crud.projects,
    73→      };
    74→    }
    75→  }, [selection.selectedProjectId, crud.projects]);
    76→
    77→  // ── Build context value ──
    78→  const contextValue = useMemo(
    79→    (): ProjectContextType => ({
    80→      projects: crud.projects || [],
    81→      selectedProjectId: selection.selectedProjectId,
    82→      setSelectedProjectId: selection.setSelectedProjectId,
    83→      isLoadingProjects: crud.isLoadingProjects,
    84→      fetchProjects: crud.fetchProjects,
    85→      addNewProject: crud.addNewProject,
    86→      isCreatingProject: crud.isCreatingProject,
    87→      updateProject: crud.updateProject,
    88→      isUpdatingProject: crud.isUpdatingProject,
    89→      deleteProject: crud.deleteProject,
    90→      isDeletingProject: crud.isDeletingProject,
    91→      userId: userId ?? null,
    92→    }),
    93→    [
    94→      crud.projects,
    95→      selection.selectedProjectId,
    96→      selection.setSelectedProjectId,
    97→      crud.isLoadingProjects,
    98→      crud.fetchProjects,
    99→      crud.addNewProject,
   100→      crud.isCreatingProject,
   101→      crud.updateProject,
   102→      crud.isUpdatingProject,
   103→      crud.deleteProject,
   104→      crud.isDeletingProject,
   105→      userId,
   106→    ]
   107→  );
   108→
   109→  return (
   110→    <ProjectContext.Provider value={contextValue}>
   111→      {children}
   112→    </ProjectContext.Provider>
   113→  );
   114→};
   115→
   116→export const useProject = () => {
   117→  const context = useContext(ProjectContext);
   118→  if (context === undefined) {
   119→    const errorMessage = 'useProject must be used within a ProjectProvider. ' +
   120→      'Make sure the component is rendered inside the ProjectProvider tree. ' +
   121→      'Check that the component is not being rendered outside of App.tsx or in an error boundary that is outside the provider.';
   122→    console.error('[ProjectContext]', errorMessage, {

   125→    });
   126→    throw new Error(errorMessage);
   127→  }
   128→  return context;
   129→};

1→import React, { createContext, useContext, ReactNode, useMemo } from 'react';
     2→import { useListShots, useProjectImageStats } from '@/shared/hooks/useShots';
     3→import { useProject } from '@/shared/contexts/ProjectContext';
     4→import { Shot } from '@/types/shots';
     5→
     6→interface ShotsContextType {
     7→  shots: Shot[] | undefined;
     8→  isLoading: boolean;
     9→  error: Error | null;
    10→  refetchShots: () => void;
    11→  // Stats for SHOT_FILTER.ALL and SHOT_FILTER.NO_SHOT filters
    12→  allImagesCount?: number;
    13→  noShotImagesCount?: number;
    14→}
    15→
    16→const ShotsContext = createContext<ShotsContextType | undefined>(undefined);
    17→
    18→interface ShotsProviderProps {
    19→  children: ReactNode;
    20→}
    21→
    22→export const ShotsProvider: React.FC<ShotsProviderProps> = ({ children }) => {
    23→  const { selectedProjectId } = useProject();
    24→
    25→  // Track previous project ID to detect project switches
    26→  const prevProjectIdRef = React.useRef<string | null>(null);
    27→  const [isProjectTransitioning, setIsProjectTransitioning] = React.useState(false);
    28→
    29→  // Detect project switch and set transitioning state
    30→  React.useEffect(() => {
    31→    if (prevProjectIdRef.current !== null && prevProjectIdRef.current !== selectedProjectId) {
    32→      setIsProjectTransitioning(true);
    33→    }
    34→    prevProjectIdRef.current = selectedProjectId;
    35→  }, [selectedProjectId]);
    36→
    37→  // Load all images per shot (0 = unlimited)
    38→  // Previously limited to 2 on mobile for performance, but this broke expand/collapse UI
    39→  const maxImagesPerShot = 0;
    40→
    41→  const { data: shots, isLoading: isShotsLoading, isFetching: isShotsFetching, error: shotsError, refetch } = useListShots(selectedProjectId, { maxImagesPerShot });
    42→
    43→  // Load project-wide image stats
    44→  const { data: projectStats, isLoading: isStatsLoading } = useProjectImageStats(selectedProjectId);
    45→
    46→  // Clear transitioning state when new shots data arrives
    47→  // Use isFetching (not isLoading) because placeholderData keeps isLoading false during refetches
    48→  React.useEffect(() => {
    49→    if (isProjectTransitioning && !isShotsFetching && shots !== undefined) {
    50→      setIsProjectTransitioning(false);
    51→    }
    52→  }, [isProjectTransitioning, isShotsFetching, shots]);
    53→
    54→  // Show loading during transition or actual loading
    55→  const isLoading = isShotsLoading || isStatsLoading || isProjectTransitioning;
    56→  const error = shotsError;
    57→
    58→  // Return undefined for shots during transition to force skeleton display
    59→  // This prevents showing stale data from a previously cached project
    60→  const effectiveShots = isProjectTransitioning ? undefined : shots;
    61→
    62→  // Memoize context value to prevent unnecessary re-renders of consumers
    63→  const value = useMemo<ShotsContextType>(() => ({
    64→    shots: effectiveShots,
    65→    isLoading,
    66→    error,
    67→    refetchShots: refetch,
    68→    allImagesCount: projectStats?.allCount,
    69→    noShotImagesCount: projectStats?.noShotCount,
    70→  }), [effectiveShots, isLoading, error, refetch, projectStats]);
    71→
    72→  return (
    73→    <ShotsContext.Provider value={value}>
    74→      {children}
    75→    </ShotsContext.Provider>
    76→  );
    77→};
    78→
    79→export const useShots = (): ShotsContextType => {
    80→  const context = useContext(ShotsContext);
    81→  if (context === undefined) {
    82→    throw new Error('useShots must be used within a ShotsProvider');
    83→  }
    84→  return context;
    85→};

1→import {
     2→  createContext,
     3→  useState,
     4→  useContext,
     5→  ReactNode,
     6→  useEffect,
     7→  useRef,
     8→  useCallback,
     9→  useMemo
    10→} from 'react';
    11→import { supabase } from '@/integrations/supabase/client';
    12→import { UserPreferences } from '@/shared/settings/userPreferences';
    13→import { updateToolSettingsSupabase } from '@/shared/hooks/useToolSettings';
    14→import { useMobileTimeoutFallback } from '@/shared/hooks/useMobileTimeoutFallback';
    15→import { handleError } from '@/shared/lib/errorHandler';
    16→import { useAuth } from './AuthContext';
    17→
    18→interface UserSettingsContextType {
    19→  /** User settings from the server (cross-device, account-level) */
    20→  userSettings: UserPreferences | undefined;
    21→  /** Whether settings are currently loading */
    22→  isLoadingSettings: boolean;
    23→  /** Fetch user settings from the server */
    24→  fetchUserSettings: () => Promise<void>;
    25→  /** Update user settings (persisted to server, syncs across devices) */
    26→  updateUserSettings: (scope: 'user', patch: Partial<UserPreferences>) => Promise<void>;
    27→}
    28→
    29→const UserSettingsContext = createContext<UserSettingsContextType | undefined>(undefined);
    30→
    31→/**
    32→ * UserSettingsProvider manages server-persisted user settings.
    33→ * These settings sync across devices (stored in users.settings['user-preferences']).
    34→ *
    35→ * Features:
    36→ * - [MobileStallFix] Timeout and recovery handling for settings loading
    37→ * - Optimistic updates for better UX
    38→ * - Depends on AuthContext for userId
    39→ */
    40→export const UserSettingsProvider = ({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) => {
    41→  const { userId } = useAuth();
    42→
    43→  const [userSettings, setUserSettings] = useState<UserPreferences | undefined>(undefined);
    44→  const [isLoadingSettings, setIsLoadingSettings] = useState(false);
    45→  const userSettingsRef = useRef<UserPreferences | undefined>(undefined);
    46→
    47→  // Settings fetching
    48→  const fetchUserSettings = useCallback(async () => {
    49→    if (!userId) return;
    50→
    51→    setIsLoadingSettings(true);
    52→
    53→    try {
    54→      // Read the settings JSON for the current user
    55→      const { data, error } = await supabase
    56→        .from('users')
    57→        .select('settings')
    58→        .eq('id', userId)
    59→        .single();
    60→
    61→      if (error) throw error;
    62→
    63→      const settings = (data?.settings as Record<string, unknown> | null)?.['user-preferences'] as UserPreferences ?? {};
    64→      setUserSettings(settings);
    65→      userSettingsRef.current = settings;
    66→    } catch (error) {
    67→      handleError(error, { context: 'UserSettingsContext', showToast: false });
    68→      // Set empty settings on error instead of leaving undefined
    69→      setUserSettings({});
    70→      userSettingsRef.current = {};
    71→    } finally {
    72→      setIsLoadingSettings(false);
    73→    }
    74→  }, [userId]);
    75→
    76→  // Update user settings directly using the global write queue
    77→  const updateUserSettings = useCallback(async (_scope: 'user', patch: Partial<UserPreferences>) => {
    78→    if (!userId) return;
    79→
    80→    try {
    81→      // Use the global queue - it handles read-modify-write internally
    82→      await updateToolSettingsSupabase({
    83→        scope: 'user',
    84→        id: userId,
    85→        toolId: 'user-preferences',
    86→        patch,
    87→      });
    88→
    89→      // Update local state optimistically
    90→      setUserSettings(prev => {
    91→        const merged = { ...prev, ...patch };
    92→        userSettingsRef.current = merged;
    93→        return merged;
    94→      });
    95→    } catch (error) {
    96→      handleError(error, { context: 'UserSettingsContext', showToast: false });
    97→    }
    98→  }, [userId]);
    99→
   100→  // Fetch settings when user changes
   101→  useEffect(() => {
   102→    if (userId) {
   103→      fetchUserSettings();
   104→    } else {
   105→      setUserSettings(undefined);
   106→      userSettingsRef.current = undefined;
   107→      setIsLoadingSettings(false);
   108→    }
   109→  }, [userId, fetchUserSettings]);
   110→
   111→  // [MobileStallFix] Fallback recovery: set empty defaults if settings loading stalls
   112→  const handleSettingsTimeout = useCallback(() => {
   113→    setIsLoadingSettings(false);
   114→    setUserSettings({});
   115→    userSettingsRef.current = {};
   116→  }, []);
   117→
   118→  useMobileTimeoutFallback({
   119→    isLoading: isLoadingSettings,
   120→    onTimeout: handleSettingsTimeout,
   121→    mobileTimeoutMs: 10000,
   122→    desktopTimeoutMs: 5000,
   123→    enabled: !!userId,
   124→  });
   125→
   126→  const contextValue = useMemo(
   127→    () => ({
   128→      userSettings,
   129→      isLoadingSettings,
   130→      fetchUserSettings,
   131→      updateUserSettings,
   132→    }),
   133→    [userSettings, isLoadingSettings, fetchUserSettings, updateUserSettings]
   134→  );
   135→
   136→  return (
   137→    <UserSettingsContext.Provider value={contextValue}>
   138→      {children}
   139→    </UserSettingsContext.Provider>
   140→  );
   141→};
   142→
   143→/**
   144→ * Hook to access user settings (server-persisted, cross-device).
   145→ *
   146→ * For device-local preferences (like sound on/off), use useLocalPreferences instead.
   147→ *
   148→ * @returns { userSettings, isLoadingSettings, fetchUserSettings, updateUserSettings }
   149→ */
   150→export const useUserSettings = () => {
   151→  const context = useContext(UserSettingsContext);
   152→  if (context === undefined) {
   153→    const errorMessage = 'useUserSettings must be used within a UserSettingsProvider. ' +
   154→      'Make sure the component is rendered inside the UserSettingsProvider tree.';
   155→    console.error('[UserSettingsContext]', errorMessage, {
   156→      stack: new Error().stack,
   157→    });
   158→    throw new Error(errorMessage);
   159→  }
   160→  return context;
   161→};
   162→
   163→

     4→import type { Task } from '@/types/tasks';

     6→
     7→// ================================================================
     8→// GENERATION-TASK INTEGRATION CONTEXT
     9→// ================================================================
    10→// This context provides a centralized way for components to work with
    11→// both generation and task data seamlessly. It handles background
    12→// preloading and cache management automatically.
    13→
    14→interface GenerationTaskContextValue {
    15→  // Methods for working with generation-task relationships
    16→  preloadTaskMappings: (generationIds: string[]) => Promise<void>;
    17→  enhanceWithTaskData: (generations: GenerationRow[]) => (GenerationRow & { taskId?: string | null; taskData?: Task | null })[];
    18→  
    19→  // Configuration
    20→  isPreloadingEnabled: boolean;
    21→  setPreloadingEnabled: (enabled: boolean) => void;
    22→}
    23→
    24→const GenerationTaskContext = createContext<GenerationTaskContextValue | null>(null);
    25→
    26→interface GenerationTaskProviderProps {
    27→  children: React.ReactNode;
    28→  
    29→  // Configuration options
    30→  enableBackgroundPreloading?: boolean;
    31→  preloadBatchSize?: number;
    32→  preloadDelay?: number;
    33→}
    34→
    35→export function GenerationTaskProvider({ 
    36→  children, 
    37→  enableBackgroundPreloading = true,
    38→  preloadBatchSize = 5,
    39→  preloadDelay = 200 
    40→}: GenerationTaskProviderProps) {
    41→  const queryClient = useQueryClient();
    42→  const [isPreloadingEnabled, setPreloadingEnabled] = React.useState(enableBackgroundPreloading);
    43→
    44→  const preloadTaskMappings = React.useCallback(async (generationIds: string[]) => {
    45→    if (!isPreloadingEnabled || generationIds.length === 0) return;
    46→
    47→    try {
    48→      await preloadGenerationTaskMappings(generationIds, queryClient, {
    49→        batchSize: preloadBatchSize,
    50→        delayBetweenBatches: preloadDelay,
    51→        preloadFullTaskData: true, // Preload full task data for better UX
    52→      });
    53→    } catch (error) {
    54→    }
    55→  }, [queryClient, isPreloadingEnabled, preloadBatchSize, preloadDelay]);
    56→
    57→  const enhanceWithTaskData = React.useCallback((generations: GenerationRow[]) => {
    58→    return enhanceGenerationsWithTaskData(generations, queryClient);
    59→  }, [queryClient]);
    60→
    61→  // Memoize context value to prevent unnecessary re-renders of consumers
    62→  const contextValue = useMemo<GenerationTaskContextValue>(() => ({
    63→    preloadTaskMappings,
    64→    enhanceWithTaskData,
    65→    isPreloadingEnabled,
    66→    setPreloadingEnabled,
    67→  }), [preloadTaskMappings, enhanceWithTaskData, isPreloadingEnabled, setPreloadingEnabled]);
    68→
    69→  return (
    70→    <GenerationTaskContext.Provider value={contextValue}>
    71→      {children}
    72→    </GenerationTaskContext.Provider>
    73→  );
    74→}

    77→// HOOKS FOR USING THE CONTEXT
    78→// ================================================================

1→import React, { createContext, useContext, useState, useCallback, useMemo, useEffect } from 'react';
     2→
     3→// Auto-cleanup stale incoming tasks after this many seconds
     4→const STALE_TASK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 60;
     5→
     6→/**
     7→ * Generic incoming task - represents a task that is being prepared/created
     8→ * but hasn't yet appeared in the database. This allows for immediate UI feedback
     9→ * while background operations (like AI prompt generation) complete.
    10→ *
    11→ * Designed to work with any task type, not just image generation.
    12→ */
    13→export interface IncomingTask {
    14→  id: string;
    15→  startedAt: Date;
    16→  taskType: string;       // e.g., 'image_generation', 'travel_video', 'upscale', etc.
    17→  label: string;          // Display text (e.g., "cinematic shot of...", "Travel video")
    18→  expectedCount?: number; // Optional: expected number of tasks to create
    19→  baselineCount?: number; // DB count when placeholder was added (for accurate count calculation)
    20→}
    21→
    22→interface IncomingTasksContextValue {
    23→  /** List of all incoming tasks currently being prepared */
    24→  incomingTasks: IncomingTask[];
    25→
    26→  /** Add a new incoming task. Returns the generated ID for later removal. */
    27→  addIncomingTask: (task: Omit<IncomingTask, 'id' | 'startedAt'>) => string;
    28→
    29→  /** Remove an incoming task by ID (call when real tasks appear or on error) */
    30→  removeIncomingTask: (id: string) => void;
    31→
    32→  /**
    33→   * Complete an incoming task: remove it and update remaining placeholders' baselines.
    34→   * Call this after refetching queries to ensure a clean count swap.
    35→   * @param id - The task to remove
    36→   * @param newBaseline - The current DB count (remaining placeholders will use this as their new baseline)
    37→   */
    38→  completeIncomingTask: (id: string, newBaseline: number) => void;
    39→
    40→  /** Quick check if there are any incoming tasks */
    41→  hasIncomingTasks: boolean;
    42→}
    43→
    44→const IncomingTasksContext = createContext<IncomingTasksContextValue | null>(null);
    45→
    46→let idCounter = 0;
    47→const generateId = () => `incoming-${Date.now()}-${++idCounter}`;
    48→
    49→export const IncomingTasksProvider: React.FC<{ children: React.ReactNode }> = ({ children }) => {
    50→  const [incomingTasks, setIncomingTasks] = useState<IncomingTask[]>([]);
    51→
    52→  const addIncomingTask = useCallback((task: Omit<IncomingTask, 'id' | 'startedAt'>): string => {
    53→    const id = generateId();
    54→    const newTask: IncomingTask = {
    55→      ...task,
    56→      id,
    57→      startedAt: new Date(),
    58→    };
    59→
    60→    setIncomingTasks(prev => [newTask, ...prev]);
    61→    return id;
    62→  }, []);
    63→
    64→  const removeIncomingTask = useCallback((id: string) => {
    65→    setIncomingTasks(prev => prev.filter(task => task.id !== id));
    66→  }, []);
    67→
    68→  const completeIncomingTask = useCallback((id: string, newBaseline: number) => {
    69→    setIncomingTasks(prev =>
    70→      prev
    71→        .filter(task => task.id !== id)  // Remove completed task
    72→        .map(task => ({ ...task, baselineCount: newBaseline }))  // Update remaining baselines
    73→    );
    74→  }, []);
    75→
    76→  const hasIncomingTasks = incomingTasks.length > 0;
    77→
    78→  // Auto-cleanup stale incoming tasks that have been sitting too long
    79→  // This prevents stuck placeholders if completeIncomingTask is never called (e.g., due to errors)
    80→  useEffect(() => {
    81→    if (incomingTasks.length === 0) return;
    82→
    83→    const interval = setInterval(() => {
    84→      const now = new Date();
    85→      setIncomingTasks(prev => {
    86→        const staleTasks = prev.filter(task => {
    87→          const ageSeconds = (now.getTime() - task.startedAt.getTime()) / 1000;
    88→          return ageSeconds > STALE_TASK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS;
    89→        });
    90→
    91→        if (staleTasks.length > 0) {
    92→          return prev.filter(task => {
    93→            const ageSeconds = (now.getTime() - task.startedAt.getTime()) / 1000;
    94→            return ageSeconds <= STALE_TASK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS;
    95→          });
    96→        }
    97→        return prev;
    98→      });
    99→    }, 5000); // Check every 5 seconds
   100→
   101→    return () => clearInterval(interval);
   102→  }, [incomingTasks.length]);
   103→
   104→  const value = useMemo(() => ({
   105→    incomingTasks,
   106→    addIncomingTask,
   107→    removeIncomingTask,
   108→    completeIncomingTask,
   109→    hasIncomingTasks,
   110→  }), [incomingTasks, addIncomingTask, removeIncomingTask, completeIncomingTask, hasIncomingTasks]);
   111→
   112→  return (
   113→    <IncomingTasksContext.Provider value={value}>
   114→      {children}
   115→    </IncomingTasksContext.Provider>
   116→  );
   117→};
   118→
   119→export const useIncomingTasks = (): IncomingTasksContextValue => {
   120→  const context = useContext(IncomingTasksContext);
   121→  if (!context) {
   122→    throw new Error('useIncomingTasks must be used within an IncomingTasksProvider');
   123→  }
   124→  return context;
   125→};
   126→
   127→// NOTE: Default export removed - was not used anywhere.
   128→// The context is accessed via useIncomingTasks() hook.
   129→

     9→interface PanesContextType {

    26→
    27→  // Active task tracking for highlighting
    28→  activeTaskId: string | null;
    29→  setActiveTaskId: (taskId: string | null) => void;
    30→
    31→  // Programmatic tasks pane control (desktop only)
    32→  isTasksPaneOpen: boolean;
    33→  setIsTasksPaneOpen: (isOpen: boolean) => void;
    34→
    35→  // Reset all pane locks (used by ProductTour)
    36→  resetAllPaneLocks: () => void;
    37→}
    38→
    39→const PanesContext = createContext<PanesContextType | undefined>(undefined);
    40→
    41→export const PanesProvider: React.FC<{ children: ReactNode }> = ({ children }) => {
    42→  const isMobile = useIsMobile();
    43→  const isTablet = useIsTablet();
    44→  
    45→  // On tablets, allow locking but only one pane at a time
    46→  // On phones (mobile but not tablet), no locking allowed
    47→  const isSmallMobile = isMobile && !isTablet;
    48→  
    49→  // Load pane locks from user settings (desktop and tablet)
    50→  const { value: paneLocks, update: savePaneLocks, isLoading } = useUserUIState('paneLocks', {
    51→    shots: false,
    52→    tasks: false,
    53→    gens: false,
    54→  });
    55→
    56→  // Local state for lock status (source of truth for UI)
    57→  const [locks, setLocks] = useState(paneLocks);
    58→
    59→  // Pane open states (not persisted, runtime only)
    60→  const [isGenerationsPaneOpenState, setIsGenerationsPaneOpenState] = useState(false);
    61→  const [isTasksPaneOpenState, setIsTasksPaneOpenState] = useState(false);
    62→
    63→  // Pane dimensions (not persisted)
    64→  const [generationsPaneHeight, setGenerationsPaneHeightState] = useState<number>(PANE_CONFIG.dimensions.DEFAULT_HEIGHT);
    65→  const [shotsPaneWidth, setShotsPaneWidthState] = useState<number>(PANE_CONFIG.dimensions.DEFAULT_WIDTH);
    66→  const [tasksPaneWidth, setTasksPaneWidthState] = useState<number>(PANE_CONFIG.dimensions.DEFAULT_WIDTH);
    67→  
    68→  // Active task tracking (not persisted)
    69→  const [activeTaskId, setActiveTaskId] = useState<string | null>(null);
    70→
    71→  // Hydrate local state once when settings load (desktop and tablet)
    72→  useEffect(() => {
    73→    if (isSmallMobile) {
    74→      // On small mobile (phones), always start with unlocked state
    75→      setLocks({
    76→        shots: false,
    77→        tasks: false,
    78→        gens: false,
    79→      });
    80→      return;
    81→    }
    82→
    83→    if (!isLoading) {
    84→      // Hydrating pane locks from server (desktop and tablet)
    85→      // On tablets, only keep one lock if multiple are saved
    86→      let newLocks = paneLocks;
    87→      if (isTablet) {
    88→        const activeLocks = Object.entries(paneLocks).filter(([_, locked]) => locked);
    89→        if (activeLocks.length > 1) {
    90→          // Keep only the first locked pane on tablets
    91→          const firstLocked = activeLocks[0][0] as 'shots' | 'tasks' | 'gens';
    92→          newLocks = {
    93→            shots: firstLocked === 'shots',
    94→            tasks: firstLocked === 'tasks',
    95→            gens: firstLocked === 'gens',
    96→          };
    97→        }
    98→      }
    99→      setLocks(newLocks);
   100→
   101→      // IMPORTANT: Sync isTasksPaneOpen with isTasksPaneLocked on hydration
   102→      // This ensures lightboxes (which read isTasksPaneOpen from context) correctly
   103→      // account for a locked pane even after page refresh
   104→      if (newLocks.tasks) {
   105→        setIsTasksPaneOpenState(true);
   106→      }
   107→    }
   108→  }, [isLoading, paneLocks, isSmallMobile, isTablet]);
   109→
   110→
   111→  // Factory for pane lock setters — each pane follows the same logic:
   112→  // 1. On mobile/tablet + locking: unlock all OTHER panes (exclusive locking)
   113→  // 2. On small phone: skip persistence to DB
   114→  // 3. On desktop: standard toggle
   115→  const createPaneLockSetter = useCallback(
   116→    (lockKey: 'gens' | 'shots' | 'tasks') => (isLocked: boolean) => {
   117→      setLocks(prev => {
   118→        if (prev[lockKey] === isLocked) return prev;
   119→
   120→        // On mobile/tablets, unlock other panes when locking this one (only one pane can be locked at a time)
   121→        const exclusiveLock = (isMobile || isTablet) && isLocked;
   122→        return exclusiveLock
   123→          ? { shots: false, tasks: false, gens: false, [lockKey]: isLocked }
   124→          : { ...prev, [lockKey]: isLocked };
   125→      });
   126→
   127→      // Save to database (desktop and tablet only, not small phones)
   128→      // Kept outside setLocks updater to avoid side effects in state updater functions
   129→      if (!isSmallMobile) {
   130→        const exclusiveLock = (isMobile || isTablet) && isLocked;
   131→        savePaneLocks(exclusiveLock
   132→          ? { shots: false, tasks: false, gens: false, [lockKey]: isLocked }
   133→          : { [lockKey]: isLocked });
   134→      }
   135→
   136→      // IMPORTANT: Sync isTasksPaneOpen with isTasksPaneLocked
   137→      // This ensures lightboxes correctly account for locked pane state
   138→      if (lockKey === 'tasks' && isLocked) {
   139→        setIsTasksPaneOpenState(true);
   140→      }
   141→    },
   142→    [savePaneLocks, isSmallMobile, isMobile, isTablet]
   143→  );
   144→
   145→  const setIsGenerationsPaneLocked = useMemo(() => createPaneLockSetter('gens'), [createPaneLockSetter]);
   146→  const setIsShotsPaneLocked = useMemo(() => createPaneLockSetter('shots'), [createPaneLockSetter]);
   147→  const setIsTasksPaneLocked = useMemo(() => createPaneLockSetter('tasks'), [createPaneLockSetter]);
   148→
   149→  // Open state setters
   150→  const setIsGenerationsPaneOpen = useCallback((isOpen: boolean) => {
   151→    setIsGenerationsPaneOpenState(isOpen);
   152→  }, []);
   153→  
   154→  const setIsTasksPaneOpen = useCallback((isOpen: boolean) => {
   155→    // Works on desktop and tablets - only small phones use hover/tap behavior exclusively
   156→    if (!isSmallMobile) {
   157→      setIsTasksPaneOpenState(isOpen);
   158→    }
   159→  }, [isSmallMobile]);
   160→
   161→  // Reset all pane locks immediately (used by ProductTour)
   162→  // This updates local state, useUserUIState value, and database without debounce
   163→  const resetAllPaneLocks = useCallback(async () => {
   164→    const unlockedState = { shots: false, tasks: false, gens: false };
   165→
   166→    // Update local locks state immediately
   167→    setLocks(unlockedState);
   168→
   169→    // Update the useUserUIState local value (prevents sync effect from restoring old value)
   170→    savePaneLocks(unlockedState);
   171→
   172→    // Also save to database immediately (no debounce) for reliability
   173→    try {
   174→      const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();
   175→      if (user) {

   183→    } catch (error) {
   184→      handleError(error, { context: 'PanesContext', showToast: false });
   185→    }
   186→  }, [savePaneLocks]);
   187→
   188→  // Dimension setters
   189→  const setGenerationsPaneHeight = useCallback((height: number) => {
   190→    setGenerationsPaneHeightState(height);
   191→  }, []);
   192→
   193→  const setShotsPaneWidth = useCallback((width: number) => {

   196→

   198→    setTasksPaneWidthState(width);
   199→  }, []);
   200→
   201→  const value = useMemo(
   202→    () => ({

   204→      isGenerationsPaneLocked: locks.gens,

   206→      isGenerationsPaneOpen: isGenerationsPaneOpenState,
   207→      setIsGenerationsPaneOpen,

   209→      setGenerationsPaneHeight,
   210→      isShotsPaneLocked: locks.shots,
   211→      setIsShotsPaneLocked,
   212→      shotsPaneWidth,
   213→      setShotsPaneWidth,
   214→      isTasksPaneLocked: locks.tasks,
   215→      setIsTasksPaneLocked,

     4→ * This class centralizes all decisions about:

    16→interface DataFreshnessState {

    18→  lastEventTimes: Map<string, number>;

    23→
    24→class DataFreshnessManager {

    36→  private readonly CIRCUIT_BREAKER_RESET_MS = 60_000; // 1 minute to reset failure count

    41→
    42→  /**

    45→  onRealtimeStatusChange(status: RealtimeStatus, _reason?: string) {
    46→    const previousStatus = this.state.realtimeStatus;
    47→    const now = Date.now();
    48→
    49→    // 🎯 KEY FIX: Ignore duplicate status changes to keep lastStatusChange stable
    50→    // This allows the "recently connected" grace period in getPollingInterval to actually expire
    51→    if (previousStatus === status) {
    52→      return; // Don't update state or notify subscribers for duplicates
    53→    }

    55→    // Actual status transition - update state

    63→  /**

    66→  onRealtimeEvent(_eventType: string, affectedQueries: string[][]) {
    67→    const now = Date.now();
    68→
    69→    affectedQueries.forEach(queryKey => {
    70→      const key = JSON.stringify(queryKey);

    82→  getPollingInterval(queryKey: string[]): PollingInterval {
    83→    const key = JSON.stringify(queryKey);
    84→    const lastEvent = this.state.lastEventTimes.get(key);
    85→    const now = Date.now();
    86→    const timeSinceStatusChange = now - this.state.lastStatusChange;
    87→
    88→    // 🎯 If realtime is connected, trust it after it's been stable
    89→    if (this.state.realtimeStatus === 'connected') {
    90→      // If realtime just connected (< 30 seconds), give it time to prove it's stable
    91→      if (timeSinceStatusChange < 30000) {
    92→        return 30000; // 30 seconds - wait for realtime to prove it's stable
    93→      }
    94→
    95→      // ✅ FIXED: If realtime has been stable for >30 seconds, trust it

    98→      if (lastEvent) {

   101→        if (eventAge < 60000) { // Events within 1 minute

   126→    const hasRecentFailures = failureInfo &&

   128→      failureInfo.count >= this.CIRCUIT_BREAKER_THRESHOLD;
   129→
   130→    let pollingInterval: number;
   131→
   132→    if (hasRecentFailures) {
   133→      // Circuit breaker triggered - use much longer interval
   134→      pollingInterval = 60_000; // 60 seconds
   135→    } else if (disconnectedDuration < 30_000) {
   136→      // First 30 seconds: 15s polling (give realtime time to reconnect)
   137→      pollingInterval = 15_000;
   138→    } else if (disconnectedDuration < 2 * 60_000) {
   139→      // 30s - 2 minutes: 30s polling
   140→      pollingInterval = 30_000;
   141→    } else if (disconnectedDuration < 5 * 60_000) {
   142→      // 2-5 minutes: 45s polling
   143→      pollingInterval = 45_000;
   144→    } else {
   145→      // >5 minutes: 60s polling (realtime probably has issues)
   146→      pollingInterval = 60_000;

   155→  onFetchFailure(queryKey: string[], error: Error) {
   156→    const key = JSON.stringify(queryKey);
   157→    const now = Date.now();
   158→    const existing = this.state.fetchFailures.get(key);
   159→
   160→    // Reset count if last failure was too long ago
   161→    const shouldReset = existing && (now - existing.lastFailure) > this.CIRCUIT_BREAKER_RESET_MS;
   162→
   163→    const newCount = shouldReset ? 1 : (existing?.count || 0) + 1;
   164→    this.state.fetchFailures.set(key, { count: newCount, lastFailure: now });
   165→
   166→    const isCircuitBreakerTriggered = newCount >= this.CIRCUIT_BREAKER_THRESHOLD;
   167→
   168→    const errorType = this.classifyError(error);
   169→
   170→    // Notify subscribers so polling intervals can adjust
   171→    if (isCircuitBreakerTriggered) {
   172→      this.notifySubscribers();
   173→
   174→      // Show user-facing error toast (throttled to prevent spam)
   175→      if (now - this.lastErrorToastTime > this.ERROR_TOAST_THROTTLE_MS) {
   176→        this.lastErrorToastTime = now;
   177→
   178→        // Customize message based on error type
   179→        const userMessage = this.getUserFriendlyErrorMessage(errorType, newCount);
   180→        toast.error(userMessage, {

   182→          description: 'Data may be outdated. Will retry automatically.',
   183→          id: 'network-error-toast', // Prevent duplicate toasts
   184→        });
   185→      }
   186→    }
   187→  }
   188→
   189→  /**
   190→   * Get a user-friendly error message based on error type

   192→  private getUserFriendlyErrorMessage(errorType: string, failureCount: number): string {
   193→    switch (errorType) {
   194→      case 'CONNECTION_CLOSED':
   195→      case 'NETWORK_ERROR':
   196→        return 'Connection issue detected';
   197→      case 'TIMEOUT':
   198→        return 'Server is slow to respond';
   199→      case 'RATE_LIMITED':
   200→        return 'Too many requests - slowing down';
   201→      case 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE':
   202→        return 'Service temporarily unavailable';
   203→      case 'AUTH_ERROR':
   204→        return 'Authentication issue - try refreshing';
   205→      default:

   207→    }
   208→  }

   210→  /**
   211→   * Report a successful fetch (resets circuit breaker)

   213→  onFetchSuccess(queryKey: string[]) {

   215→    const existing = this.state.fetchFailures.get(key);
   216→
   217→    if (existing && existing.count > 0) {
   218→      const wasCircuitBreakerActive = existing.count >= this.CIRCUIT_BREAKER_THRESHOLD;
   219→
   220→      // Reset failure count on success
   221→      this.state.fetchFailures.delete(key);
   222→
   223→      // Show recovery toast if circuit breaker was active

   229→      }
   230→    }
   231→  }
   232→
   233→  /**

   235→   */
   236→  private classifyError(error: Error): string {
   237→    const message = error.message?.toLowerCase() || '';
   238→
   239→    if (message.includes('connection_closed') || message.includes('err_connection_closed')) {
   240→      return 'CONNECTION_CLOSED';
   241→    }
   242→    if (message.includes('failed to fetch') || message.includes('network')) {
   243→      return 'NETWORK_ERROR';
   244→    }
   245→    if (message.includes('timeout') || message.includes('timed out')) {

   251→    if (message.includes('401') || message.includes('unauthorized')) {

   253→    }
   254→    if (message.includes('429') || message.includes('rate limit')) {

   256→    }
   257→    if (message.includes('503') || message.includes('service unavailable')) {
   258→      return 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE';
   259→    }
   260→    return 'UNKNOWN';
   261→  }

   263→  /**

   270→    if (!lastEvent) {

   273→

1→/**
     2→ * RealtimeConnection - Manages Supabase WebSocket connection lifecycle
     3→ *
     4→ * Single responsibility: Connect, reconnect, and emit connection status changes.
     5→ * Does NOT filter events or make business decisions about what to invalidate.
     6→ *
     7→ * State machine: disconnected → connecting → connected ↔ reconnecting → failed
     8→ */
     9→
    10→import { supabase } from '@/integrations/supabase/client';
    11→import { RealtimeChannel } from '@supabase/supabase-js';
    12→import { dataFreshnessManager } from './DataFreshnessManager';
    13→import { handleError } from '@/shared/lib/errorHandler';

    15→  ConnectionState,
    16→  ConnectionStatusCallback,
    17→  RawDatabaseEvent,

    22→  INITIAL_CONNECTION_STATE
    23→} from './types';
    24→
    25→type RawEventCallback = (event: RawDatabaseEvent) => void;
    26→
    27→export class RealtimeConnection {
    28→  private channel: RealtimeChannel | null = null;
    29→  private state: ConnectionState = { ...INITIAL_CONNECTION_STATE };

    31→

    51→  /**
    52→   * Connect to a project's realtime channel.
    53→   * If already connected to a different project, disconnects first.
    54→   */
    55→  async connect(projectId: string): Promise<boolean> {
    56→    // If connecting to same project and already connected, no-op
    57→    if (this.state.projectId === projectId && this.state.status === 'connected') {
    58→      return true;
    59→    }
    60→
    61→    // If connecting to different project, disconnect first
    62→    if (this.state.projectId && this.state.projectId !== projectId) {

    66→    return this.doConnect(projectId);

    72→  async disconnect(): Promise<void> {
    73→
    74→    this.clearTimeouts();
    75→
    76→    if (this.channel) {
    77→      try {
    78→        await this.channel.unsubscribe();
    79→      } catch (e) {

   145→  private async doConnect(projectId: string): Promise<boolean> {

   184→    // Create and subscribe to channel
   185→    const topic = `task-updates:${projectId}`;

   238→      .on('postgres_changes',

   240→        (payload) => this.emitEvent('generations', 'INSERT', payload.new, null)
   241→      )
   242→      .on('postgres_changes',
   243→        { event: 'UPDATE', schema: 'public', table: 'generations', filter: `project_id=eq.${projectId}` },
   244→        (payload) => this.emitEvent('generations', 'UPDATE', payload.new, payload.old)
   245→      )
   246→      .on('postgres_changes',

   250→
   251→    // Shot generations: INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE (no project filter - cross-project table)
   252→    this.channel
   253→      .on('postgres_changes',

   260→      )
   261→      .on('postgres_changes',
   262→        { event: 'DELETE', schema: 'public', table: 'shot_generations' },
   263→        (payload) => this.emitEvent('shot_generations', 'DELETE', payload.old, null)
   264→      );
   265→
   266→    // Variants: INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE (no project filter - cross-project table)
   267→    this.channel
   268→      .on('postgres_changes',
   269→        { event: 'INSERT', schema: 'public', table: 'generation_variants' },
   270→        (payload) => this.emitEvent('generation_variants', 'INSERT', payload.new, null)
   271→      )
   272→      .on('postgres_changes',
   273→        { event: 'UPDATE', schema: 'public', table: 'generation_variants' },
   274→        (payload) => this.emitEvent('generation_variants', 'UPDATE', payload.new, payload.old)
   275→      )
   276→      .on('postgres_changes',
   277→        { event: 'DELETE', schema: 'public', table: 'generation_variants' },
   278→        (payload) => this.emitEvent('generation_variants', 'DELETE', payload.old, null)
   279→      );
   280→  }
   281→
   282→  private emitEvent(
   283→    table: DatabaseTable,
   284→    eventType: DatabaseEventType,
   285→    newRecord: unknown,
   286→    oldRecord: unknown
   287→  ): void {
   288→    const event: RawDatabaseEvent = {
   289→      table,
   290→      eventType,
   291→      new: newRecord as Record<string, unknown>,
   292→      old: oldRecord as Partial<Record<string, unknown>> | null,
   293→      receivedAt: Date.now(),
   294→    };
   295→
   296→    this.eventCallbacks.forEach((callback) => {
   297→      try {
   298→        callback(event);
   299→      } catch (error) {
   300→        handleError(error, { context: 'RealtimeConnection.eventCallback', showToast: false });
   301→      }
   302→    });
   303→  }
   304→
   305→  // ===========================================================================
   306→  // Private: Reconnection Logic
   307→  // ===========================================================================
   308→
   309→  private handleSubscribeFailure(reason: string, projectId: string): void {
   310→    const attempt = this.state.reconnectAttempt + 1;
   311→    const isExhausted = attempt > this.config.maxReconnectAttempts;
   312→
   313→    if (isExhausted) {
   314→      console.error('[RealtimeConnection] Max reconnect attempts reached');
   315→      this.setState({
   316→        status: 'failed',
   317→        error: `Connection failed after ${this.config.maxReconnectAttempts} attempts: ${reason}`,
   318→        reconnectAttempt: attempt,
   319→        nextRetryAt: null,
   320→      });
   321→      dataFreshnessManager.onRealtimeStatusChange('error', 'Max reconnect attempts reached');
   322→    } else {
   323→      const delay = Math.min(
   324→        this.config.baseReconnectDelay * Math.pow(2, attempt - 1),
   325→        this.config.maxReconnectDelay
   326→      );
   327→      const nextRetryAt = Date.now() + delay;
   328→
   329→      console.warn(
   330→        `[RealtimeConnection] Subscribe failed: ${reason}. ` +
   331→        `Retrying in ${delay}ms (attempt ${attempt}/${this.config.maxReconnectAttempts})`
   332→      );
   333→
   334→      this.setState({
   335→        status: 'reconnecting',
   336→        error: reason,
   337→        reconnectAttempt: attempt,
   338→        nextRetryAt,
   339→      });
   340→      dataFreshnessManager.onRealtimeStatusChange('error', `Reconnecting: ${reason}`);
   341→
   342→      this.scheduleReconnect(projectId, delay);
   343→    }
   344→  }
   345→
   346→  private scheduleReconnect(projectId: string, delay: number): void {
   347→    this.clearTimeouts();
   348→
   349→    this.reconnectTimeout = setTimeout(async () => {
   350→      this.reconnectTimeout = null;
   351→
   352→      // Clean up old channel before reconnecting
   353→      if (this.channel) {
   354→        try {
   355→          await this.channel.unsubscribe();
   356→        } catch (e) {
   357→          // Ignore
   358→        }
   359→        this.channel = null;
   360→      }
   361→
   362→      await this.doConnect(projectId);
   363→      // If failed, doConnect will call handleSubscribeFailure which schedules next retry
   364→    }, delay);
   365→  }
   366→
   367→  private handleAuthHeal = (): void => {
   368→
   369→    // Only attempt reconnect if we're in a recoverable state
   370→    if (
   371→      this.state.projectId &&
   372→      (this.state.status === 'reconnecting' || this.state.status === 'failed')
   373→    ) {
   374→      // Reset attempt count on auth heal (fresh start)
   375→      this.setState({ reconnectAttempt: 0 });
   376→      this.doConnect(this.state.projectId);
   377→    }
   378→  };
   379→
   380→  // ===========================================================================
   381→  // Private: State Management
   382→  // ===========================================================================
   383→
   384→  private setState(updates: Partial<ConnectionState>): void {
   385→    const prevStatus = this.state.status;
   386→
   387→    this.state = {
   388→      ...this.state,
   389→      ...updates,
   390→      statusChangedAt: updates.status && updates.status !== prevStatus
   391→        ? Date.now()
   392→        : this.state.statusChangedAt,
   393→    };
   394→
   395→    // Notify callbacks
   396→    const snapshot = this.getState();
   397→    this.statusCallbacks.forEach((callback) => {
   398→      try {
   399→        callback(snapshot);
   400→      } catch (error) {
   401→        handleError(error, { context: 'RealtimeConnection.statusCallback', showToast: false });
   402→      }
   403→    });
   404→  }
   405→
   406→  private clearTimeouts(): void {
   407→    if (this.reconnectTimeout) {
   408→      clearTimeout(this.reconnectTimeout);
   409→      this.reconnectTimeout = null;
   410→    }
   411→    if (this.subscribeTimeout) {
   412→      clearTimeout(this.subscribeTimeout);
   413→      this.subscribeTimeout = null;
   414→    }
   415→  }
   416→}
   417→
   418→// Singleton instance
   419→export const realtimeConnection = new RealtimeConnection();
   420→

   266→  private processGenerationUpdates(

     2→ * Global Settings Write Queue
     3→ *
     4→ * Prevents network exhaustion by serializing and coalescing settings writes.
     5→ *
     6→ * Features:
