    21→  patch: Record<string, unknown>;
    22→}
    23→
    24→interface PendingWrite {
    25→  write: QueuedWrite;
    26→  resolvers: Array<{ resolve: (value: unknown) => void; reject: (error: unknown) => void }>;
    27→  timerId: NodeJS.Timeout | null;
    28→  enqueuedAt: number;
    29→}
    30→
    31→// Configuration
    32→const DEBOUNCE_MS = 300;
    33→const MAX_CONCURRENT = 1;
    34→
    35→// State
    36→const pendingByTarget = new Map<string, PendingWrite>();
    37→let inFlightCount = 0;
    38→const flushQueue: Array<{ targetKey: string; pending: PendingWrite }> = [];
    39→
    40→// The actual write function - injected to avoid circular imports
    41→let writeFunction: ((write: QueuedWrite) => Promise<unknown>) | null = null;
    42→
    43→/**
    44→ * Set the write function that performs the actual DB update.
    45→ * Must be called once at app init (in useToolSettings.ts).
    46→ */
    47→export function setSettingsWriteFunction(fn: (write: QueuedWrite) => Promise<unknown>) {
    48→  writeFunction = fn;
    49→}
    50→
    51→/**
    52→ * Create a unique key for deduplication
    53→ */
    54→function targetKey(write: QueuedWrite): string {
    55→  return `${write.scope}:${write.entityId}:${write.toolId}`;
    56→}
    57→
    58→/**
    59→ * Deep merge two objects (shallow merge of nested objects)
    60→ */
    61→function mergePatch(existing: Record<string, unknown>, incoming: Record<string, unknown>): Record<string, unknown> {
    62→  return { ...existing, ...incoming };
    63→}
    64→
    65→/**
    66→ * Process the next item in the flush queue
    67→ */
    68→async function processQueue() {
    69→  if (inFlightCount >= MAX_CONCURRENT || flushQueue.length === 0) {
    70→    return;
    71→  }
    72→
    73→  const next = flushQueue.shift();
    74→  if (!next) return;
    75→
    76→  const { targetKey: key, pending } = next;
    77→  
    78→  // Remove from pending map (we're about to process it)
    79→  pendingByTarget.delete(key);
    80→  
    81→  inFlightCount++;
    82→  
    83→  try {
    84→    if (!writeFunction) {
    85→      throw new Error('[SettingsWriteQueue] Write function not initialized');
    86→    }
    87→    
    88→    const result = await writeFunction(pending.write);
    89→    
    90→    // Resolve all waiters
    91→    for (const { resolve } of pending.resolvers) {
    92→      resolve(result);
    93→    }
    94→  } catch (error) {
    95→    handleError(error, { context: 'SettingsWriteQueue', showToast: false });
    96→
    97→    // Reject all waiters
    98→    for (const { reject } of pending.resolvers) {
    99→      reject(error);
   100→    }
   101→  } finally {
   102→    inFlightCount--;
   103→    
   104→    // Process next item
   105→    processQueue();
   106→  }
   107→}
   108→
   109→/**
   110→ * Schedule a pending write for flush
   111→ */
   112→function scheduleFlush(key: string, pending: PendingWrite) {
   113→  // Clear existing timer
   114→  if (pending.timerId) {
   115→    clearTimeout(pending.timerId);
   116→    pending.timerId = null;
   117→  }
   118→  
   119→  // Add to flush queue and process
   120→  flushQueue.push({ targetKey: key, pending });
   121→  processQueue();
   122→}
   123→
   124→/**
   125→ * Enqueue a settings write.
   126→ * 
   127→ * Returns a promise that resolves when the write completes.
   128→ * Multiple writes to the same target within the debounce window are merged.
   129→ * 
   130→ * @param write - The write to enqueue
   131→ * @param mode - 'debounced' (default) waits for debounce window; 'immediate' flushes now
   132→ */
   133→export function enqueueSettingsWrite(
   134→  write: QueuedWrite,
   135→  mode: 'debounced' | 'immediate' = 'debounced'
   136→): Promise<unknown> {
   137→  const key = targetKey(write);
   138→  
   139→  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
   140→    const existing = pendingByTarget.get(key);
   141→    
   142→    if (existing) {
   143→      // Merge with existing pending write
   144→      existing.write.patch = mergePatch(existing.write.patch, write.patch);
   145→      existing.resolvers.push({ resolve, reject });
   146→
   147→      if (mode === 'immediate') {
   148→        // Cancel debounce timer and flush now
   149→        scheduleFlush(key, existing);
   150→      }
   151→      // else: existing timer will handle it
   152→      
   153→    } else {
   154→      // Create new pending write
   155→      const pending: PendingWrite = {
   156→        write: { ...write, patch: { ...write.patch } },
   157→        resolvers: [{ resolve, reject }],
   158→        timerId: null,
   159→        enqueuedAt: Date.now(),
   160→      };
   161→
   162→      pendingByTarget.set(key, pending);
   163→
   164→      if (mode === 'immediate') {
   165→        scheduleFlush(key, pending);
   166→      } else {
   167→        // Set debounce timer
   168→        pending.timerId = setTimeout(() => {
   169→          scheduleFlush(key, pending);
   170→        }, DEBOUNCE_MS);
   171→      }
   172→    }
   173→  });
   174→}
   175→
   176→
   177→/**
   178→ * Flush all pending writes immediately.
   179→ * Best-effort: returns without waiting.
   180→ */
   181→function flushAll(): void {
   182→  for (const [key, pending] of pendingByTarget.entries()) {
   183→    if (pending.timerId) {
   184→      clearTimeout(pending.timerId);
   185→      pending.timerId = null;
   186→    }
   187→    flushQueue.push({ targetKey: key, pending });
   188→  }
   189→  pendingByTarget.clear();
   190→  processQueue();
   191→}
   192→
   193→// Best-effort flush on page unload and tab hide
   194→// Mobile browsers don't reliably fire beforeunload (e.g., tab switching on iOS Safari),
   195→// so we also flush on visibilitychange to prevent losing pending writes.
   196→if (typeof window !== 'undefined') {
   197→  window.addEventListener('beforeunload', () => {
   198→    flushAll();
   199→  });
   200→
   201→  document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', () => {
   202→    if (document.visibilityState === 'hidden') {
   203→      flushAll();
   204→    }
   205→  });
   206→}
   207→

1→/**
     2→ * Processes a style reference image to match project aspect ratio.
     3→ * Always crops the image to fit the target aspect ratio (center-cropping).
     4→ * Images are scaled to 1.5x the project resolution for higher quality style reference.
     5→ */
     6→
     7→import { parseRatio, ASPECT_RATIO_TO_RESOLUTION } from './aspectRatios';
     8→
     9→/**
    10→ * Gets the scaled dimensions (1.5x) for a given aspect ratio string
    11→ * @param aspectRatioString The aspect ratio string (e.g., "16:9", "1:1")
    12→ * @returns Object with scaled width and height, or null if invalid
    13→ */
    14→const getScaledDimensions = (aspectRatioString: string): { width: number; height: number } | null => {
    15→  
    16→  // Direct lookup first (handles exact matches like "1:1", "16:9", etc.)
    17→  if (ASPECT_RATIO_TO_RESOLUTION[aspectRatioString]) {
    18→    const resolution = ASPECT_RATIO_TO_RESOLUTION[aspectRatioString];
    19→    const [width, height] = resolution.split('x').map(Number);
    20→    const scaled = { width: Math.round(width * 1.5), height: Math.round(height * 1.5) };
    21→    return scaled;
    22→  }
    23→  
    24→  // Find the aspect ratio key that matches our target ratio numerically
    25→  const targetRatio = parseRatio(aspectRatioString);
    26→  
    27→  if (isNaN(targetRatio)) {
    28→    const resolution = ASPECT_RATIO_TO_RESOLUTION['1:1'] || '670x670';
    29→    const [width, height] = resolution.split('x').map(Number);
    30→    const scaled = { width: Math.round(width * 1.5), height: Math.round(height * 1.5) };
    31→    return scaled;
    32→  }
    33→
    34→  const aspectRatioKey = Object.keys(ASPECT_RATIO_TO_RESOLUTION).find(key => {
    35→    const keyRatio = parseRatio(key);
    36→    const matches = !isNaN(keyRatio) && Math.abs(keyRatio - targetRatio) < 0.001;
    37→    return matches;
    38→  });
    39→
    40→  if (!aspectRatioKey) {
    41→    // Fallback to 1:1 if we can't find a match
    42→    const resolution = ASPECT_RATIO_TO_RESOLUTION['1:1'] || '670x670';
    43→    const [width, height] = resolution.split('x').map(Number);
    44→    const scaled = { width: Math.round(width * 1.5), height: Math.round(height * 1.5) };
    45→    return scaled;
    46→  }
    47→
    48→  const resolution = ASPECT_RATIO_TO_RESOLUTION[aspectRatioKey];
    49→  const [width, height] = resolution.split('x').map(Number);
    50→  const scaled = { width: Math.round(width * 1.5), height: Math.round(height * 1.5) };
    51→  return scaled;
    52→};
    53→
    54→/**
    55→ * Processes a style reference image to match project aspect ratio at 1.5x scale.
    56→ * Always crops the image to fit (center-cropping) - no padding/dead space added.
    57→ * This function works with data URLs for processing - the result should be uploaded to storage.
    58→ * 
    59→ * @param dataURL The base64 data URL of the image
    60→ * @param targetAspectRatio The target aspect ratio as a number (width / height)
    61→ * @param aspectRatioString Optional aspect ratio string for dimension lookup (e.g., "16:9")
    62→ * @returns Promise with the processed image as a data URL (ready for upload)
    63→ */
    64→const processStyleReferenceForAspectRatio = async (
    65→  dataURL: string,
    66→  targetAspectRatio: number,
    67→  aspectRatioString?: string
    68→): Promise<string | null> => {
    69→  if (isNaN(targetAspectRatio) || targetAspectRatio <= 0) {
    70→    console.error("Invalid target aspect ratio.");
    71→    return null;
    72→  }
    73→
    74→  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    75→    const img = new Image();
    76→    img.onload = () => {
    77→      const originalWidth = img.width;
    78→      const originalHeight = img.height;
    79→      const originalAspectRatio = originalWidth / originalHeight;
    80→
    81→      // Get target dimensions (1.5x project resolution) if aspect ratio string is provided
    82→      let targetDimensions: { width: number; height: number } | null = null;
    83→      if (aspectRatioString) {
    84→        targetDimensions = getScaledDimensions(aspectRatioString);
    85→      }
    86→
    87→      // Calculate dimensions for the target aspect ratio
    88→      let canvasWidth: number;
    89→      let canvasHeight: number;
    90→      let drawX = 0;
    91→      let drawY = 0;
    92→      let drawWidth = originalWidth;
    93→      let drawHeight = originalHeight;
    94→
    95→      if (Math.abs(originalAspectRatio - targetAspectRatio) < 0.001) {
    96→        // Aspect ratios are essentially the same, but still scale to target dimensions if available
    97→        if (targetDimensions) {
    98→          canvasWidth = targetDimensions.width;
    99→          canvasHeight = targetDimensions.height;
   100→          // Scale the original image to fit the target dimensions
   101→          const scaleX = canvasWidth / originalWidth;
   102→          const scaleY = canvasHeight / originalHeight;
   103→          const scale = Math.min(scaleX, scaleY);
   104→          
   105→          drawWidth = originalWidth * scale;
   106→          drawHeight = originalHeight * scale;
   107→          drawX = (canvasWidth - drawWidth) / 2;
   108→          drawY = (canvasHeight - drawHeight) / 2;
   109→        } else {
   110→          resolve(dataURL);
   111→          return;
   112→        }
   113→      }
   114→
   115→      else if (originalAspectRatio > targetAspectRatio) {
   116→        // Original image is wider than target - crop the width
   117→        if (targetDimensions) {
   118→          canvasWidth = targetDimensions.width;
   119→          canvasHeight = targetDimensions.height;
   120→          // Scale to fill height, crop width (center horizontally)
   121→          const scale = canvasHeight / originalHeight;
   122→          drawWidth = originalWidth * scale;
   123→          drawHeight = canvasHeight;
   124→          drawX = (canvasWidth - drawWidth) / 2;
   125→          drawY = 0;
   126→        } else {
   127→          canvasHeight = originalHeight;
   128→          canvasWidth = originalHeight * targetAspectRatio;
   129→          drawX = 0;
   130→          drawY = 0;
   131→          drawWidth = canvasWidth;
   132→          drawHeight = originalHeight;
   133→        }
   134→      } else {
   135→        // Original image is taller than target - crop the height
   136→        if (targetDimensions) {
   137→          canvasWidth = targetDimensions.width;
   138→          canvasHeight = targetDimensions.height;
   139→          // Scale to fill width, crop height (center vertically)
   140→          const scale = canvasWidth / originalWidth;
   141→          drawWidth = canvasWidth;
   142→          drawHeight = originalHeight * scale;
   143→          drawX = 0;
   144→          drawY = (canvasHeight - drawHeight) / 2;
   145→        } else {
   146→          canvasWidth = originalWidth;
   147→          canvasHeight = originalWidth / targetAspectRatio;
   148→          drawX = 0;
   149→          drawY = 0;
   150→          drawWidth = originalWidth;
   151→          drawHeight = canvasHeight;
   152→        }
   153→      }
   154→
   155→      const canvas = document.createElement("canvas");
   156→      canvas.width = Math.round(canvasWidth);
   157→      canvas.height = Math.round(canvasHeight);
   158→      
   159→      const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
   160→      
   161→      // Verify the context was created successfully
   162→
   163→      if (!ctx) {
   164→        reject(new Error("Failed to get canvas context"));
   165→        return;
   166→      }
   167→
   168→      // Clear canvas before drawing
   169→      ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
   170→      
   171→      // Draw the image with calculated dimensions and positioning (center-cropped to fill canvas)
   172→      ctx.drawImage(
   173→        img,
   174→        0, 0, originalWidth, originalHeight, // source: full original image
   175→        drawX, drawY, drawWidth, drawHeight // destination: scaled and positioned to fill canvas
   176→      );
   177→
   178→      // Convert to data URL
   179→      const processedDataURL = canvas.toDataURL('image/png'); // Use PNG to preserve transparency
   180→      
   181→      // Debug: Check the dataURL dimensions by creating a test image
   182→      const testImg = new Image();
   183→      testImg.onload = () => {
   184→      };
   185→      testImg.src = processedDataURL;
   186→      
   187→      resolve(processedDataURL);
   188→    };
   189→
   190→    img.onerror = () => {
   191→      reject(new Error("Failed to load image from data URL"));
   192→    };
   193→
   194→    img.src = dataURL;
   195→  });
   196→};
   197→
   198→/**
   199→ * Processes a style reference image from aspect ratio string (e.g., "16:9") at 1.5x scale
   200→ * 
   201→ * @param dataURL The base64 data URL of the image
   202→ * @param aspectRatioString The aspect ratio string (e.g., "16:9", "1:1")
   203→ * @returns Promise with the processed image as a data URL
   204→ */
   205→export const processStyleReferenceForAspectRatioString = async (
   206→  dataURL: string,
   207→  aspectRatioString: string
   208→): Promise<string | null> => {
   209→  const targetAspectRatio = parseRatio(aspectRatioString);
   210→  if (isNaN(targetAspectRatio)) {
   211→    console.error("Invalid aspect ratio string:", aspectRatioString);
   212→    return null;
   213→  }
   214→  
   215→  return processStyleReferenceForAspectRatio(dataURL, targetAspectRatio, aspectRatioString);

1→/**
     2→ * Centralized error handling utility
     3→ *
     4→ * Provides consistent error handling across the app:
     5→ * - Categorizes errors by type
     6→ * - Logs with structured context
     7→ * - Shows appropriate user feedback via toast
     8→ * - Respects error type-specific behavior (silent errors, auth redirects, etc.)
     9→ */
    10→
    11→import { toast } from '@/shared/hooks/use-toast';
    12→import {
    13→  AppError,
    14→  categorizeError,
    15→  isNetworkError,
    16→  SilentError
    17→} from './errors';
    18→
    19→interface HandleErrorOptions {
    20→  /** Context string for logging (e.g., "ImageUpload", "TaskCreation") */
    21→  context: string;
    22→  /** Additional data to include in logs */
    23→  logData?: Record<string, unknown>;
    24→  /** Custom toast title (defaults based on error type) */
    25→  toastTitle?: string;
    26→  /** Override whether to show toast (null = use error's default) */
    27→  showToast?: boolean;
    28→  /** Callback after error is handled */
    29→  onError?: (error: AppError) => void;
    30→}
    31→
    32→/**
    33→ * Toast titles by error type
    34→ */
    35→const DEFAULT_TITLES: Record<string, string> = {
    36→  NetworkError: 'Connection Error',
    37→  AuthError: 'Authentication Required',
    38→  ValidationError: 'Invalid Input',
    39→  ServerError: 'Server Error',
    40→  AppError: 'Error',
    41→};
    42→
    43→/**
    44→ * Handle an error with consistent logging and user feedback
    45→ *
    46→ * @example
    47→ * ```typescript
    48→ * try {
    49→ *   await uploadImage(file);
    50→ * } catch (error) {
    51→ *   handleError(error, { context: 'ImageUpload', logData: { fileName: file.name } });
    52→ * }
    53→ * ```
    54→ */
    55→export function handleError(error: unknown, options: HandleErrorOptions): AppError {
    56→  const { context, logData, toastTitle, showToast, onError } = options;
    57→
    58→  // Categorize the error
    59→  const appError = categorizeError(error, { context, ...logData });
    60→
    61→  // Build log tag
    62→  const tag = `[${context}]`;
    63→
    64→  // Log the error with context
    65→  if (appError instanceof SilentError) {
    66→  } else {
    67→    // Regular errors get error-level logging
    68→    console.error(`${tag} ${appError.name}:`, appError.message, {
    69→      errorType: appError.name,
    70→      cause: appError.cause?.message,
    71→      ...appError.context,
    72→    });
    73→  }
    74→
    75→  // Determine if we should show a toast
    76→  const shouldShowToast = showToast ?? appError.showToast;
    77→
    78→  if (shouldShowToast) {
    79→    const title = toastTitle ?? DEFAULT_TITLES[appError.name] ?? DEFAULT_TITLES.AppError;
    80→
    81→    // Use the error's message or fall back to a generic message
    82→    let description = appError.message;
    83→
    84→    // For network errors, provide more helpful messages
    85→    if (isNetworkError(appError)) {
    86→      if (appError.isOffline) {
    87→        description = 'You appear to be offline. Please check your connection.';
    88→      } else if (appError.isTimeout) {
    89→        description = 'Request timed out. Please try again.';
    90→      }
    91→    }
    92→
    93→    toast({
    94→      title,
    95→      description,
    96→      variant: 'destructive',
    97→    });
    98→  }
    99→
   100→  // Call optional callback
   101→  onError?.(appError);
   102→
   103→  return appError;
   104→}
   105→
   106→
   107→// Re-export error types for convenience
   108→export {
   109→  AppError,
   110→  NetworkError,
   111→  AuthError,
   112→  SilentError,
   113→  isAppError,
   114→  isAuthError,
   115→  isNetworkError,
   116→} from './errors';
   117→

1→/**
     2→ * RealtimeProvider - Manages realtime connection and provides status to the app
     3→ *
     4→ * This provider:
     5→ * 1. Connects to the realtime service when a project is selected
     6→ * 2. Wires raw events from connection → processor → invalidation
     7→ * 3. Exposes connection status to the component tree
     8→ *
     9→ */
    10→
    11→import React, { createContext, useContext, useEffect, useState, useCallback } from 'react';
    12→import { useProject } from '@/shared/contexts/ProjectContext';
    13→import { realtimeConnection } from '@/shared/realtime/RealtimeConnection';
    14→import { realtimeEventProcessor } from '@/shared/realtime/RealtimeEventProcessor';
    15→import { dataFreshnessManager } from '@/shared/realtime/DataFreshnessManager';
    16→import { useRealtimeInvalidation } from '@/shared/hooks/useRealtimeInvalidation';
    17→import type { ConnectionState, ConnectionStatus } from '@/shared/realtime/types';
    18→
    19→// =============================================================================
    20→// Context
    21→// =============================================================================
    22→
    23→interface RealtimeContextValue {
    24→  /** Current connection status */
    25→  status: ConnectionStatus;
    26→  /** Whether currently connected */
    27→  isConnected: boolean;
    28→  /** Whether connection is in progress */
    29→  isConnecting: boolean;
    30→  /** Whether in a failed state (exhausted retries) */
    31→  isFailed: boolean;
    32→  /** Error message if any */
    33→  error: string | null;
    34→  /** Current reconnect attempt (0 if not reconnecting) */
    35→  reconnectAttempt: number;
    36→  /** Manually trigger reconnection */
    37→  reconnect: () => void;
    38→}
    39→
    40→const RealtimeContext = createContext<RealtimeContextValue>({
    41→  status: 'disconnected',
    42→  isConnected: false,
    43→  isConnecting: false,
    44→  isFailed: false,
    45→  error: null,
    46→  reconnectAttempt: 0,
    47→  reconnect: () => {},
    48→});
    49→
    50→export const useRealtime = () => useContext(RealtimeContext);
    51→
    52→// =============================================================================
    53→// Provider
    54→// =============================================================================
    55→
    56→interface RealtimeProviderProps {
    57→  children: React.ReactNode;
    58→}
    59→
    60→export function RealtimeProvider({ children }: RealtimeProviderProps) {
    61→  const { selectedProjectId } = useProject();
    62→  const [connectionState, setConnectionState] = useState<ConnectionState>(
    63→    realtimeConnection.getState()
    64→  );
    65→
    66→  // Set up the invalidation hook (subscribes to processed events)
    67→  useRealtimeInvalidation();
    68→
    69→  // Wire connection events → processor
    70→  useEffect(() => {
    71→    const unsubscribe = realtimeConnection.onEvent((event) => {
    72→      realtimeEventProcessor.process(event);
    73→    });
    74→    return unsubscribe;
    75→  }, []);
    76→
    77→  // Subscribe to connection status changes
    78→  useEffect(() => {
    79→    const unsubscribe = realtimeConnection.onStatusChange((state) => {
    80→      setConnectionState(state);
    81→    });
    82→    return unsubscribe;
    83→  }, []);
    84→
    85→  // Connect/disconnect when project changes
    86→  useEffect(() => {
    87→    if (!selectedProjectId) {
    88→      realtimeConnection.disconnect();
    89→      dataFreshnessManager.reset();
    90→      return;
    91→    }
    92→
    93→    realtimeConnection.connect(selectedProjectId);
    94→
    95→    return () => {
    96→      // Don't disconnect on cleanup - let the next effect handle it
    97→      // This prevents disconnect/reconnect when the component re-renders
    98→    };
    99→  }, [selectedProjectId]);
   100→
   101→  // Clean up on unmount
   102→  useEffect(() => {
   103→    return () => {
   104→      realtimeEventProcessor.clear();
   105→    };
   106→  }, []);
   107→
   108→  // Manual reconnect function
   109→  const reconnect = useCallback(() => {
   110→    if (selectedProjectId) {
   111→      realtimeConnection.reset();
   112→      realtimeConnection.connect(selectedProjectId);
   113→    }
   114→  }, [selectedProjectId]);
   115→
   116→  // Derive context value from connection state
   117→  const contextValue: RealtimeContextValue = {
   118→    status: connectionState.status,
   119→    isConnected: connectionState.status === 'connected',
   120→    isConnecting: connectionState.status === 'connecting',
   121→    isFailed: connectionState.status === 'failed',
   122→    error: connectionState.error,
   123→    reconnectAttempt: connectionState.reconnectAttempt,
   124→    reconnect,
   125→  };
   126→
   127→  return (
   128→    <RealtimeContext.Provider value={contextValue}>
   129→      {children}
   130→    </RealtimeContext.Provider>
   131→  );
   132→}
   133→
   134→

1→/**
     2→ * Tool Settings Service
     3→ *
     4→ * Pure async functions for fetching tool settings from Supabase.
     5→ * Extracted from useToolSettings.ts to reduce hook file complexity.
     6→ *
     7→ * Contains:
     8→ * - Auth timeout/caching logic (getUserWithTimeout)
     9→ * - Settings fetch with single-flight deduplication (fetchToolSettingsSupabase)
    10→ * - Module-level state for caching and deduplication
    11→ */
    12→
    13→import { supabase } from '@/integrations/supabase/client';
    14→import { toolsManifest } from '@/tools';
    15→import { deepMerge } from '@/shared/lib/deepEqual';
    16→import { isCancellationError, isAbortError, getErrorMessage } from '@/shared/lib/errorUtils';
    17→import { handleError } from '@/shared/lib/errorHandler';
    18→
    19→// ============================================================================
    20→// Module-level state
    21→// ============================================================================
    22→
    23→// Single-flight dedupe for settings fetches across components
    24→const inflightSettingsFetches = new Map<string, Promise<unknown>>();
    25→
    26→// Single-flight dedupe for getSession calls (it's slow - 600ms to 16s!)
    27→let inflightGetSession: Promise<{ data: { session: { user: { id: string } } | null } }> | null = null;
    28→
    29→// Lightweight user cache to avoid repeated auth calls within a short window
    30→let cachedUser: { id: string } | null = null;
    31→let cachedUserAt: number = 0;
    32→const USER_CACHE_MS = 10_000; // 10 seconds
    33→
    34→// Tool defaults registry - client-side version matching server
    35→const toolDefaults: Record<string, unknown> = Object.fromEntries(
    36→  toolsManifest.map(toolSettings => [toolSettings.id, toolSettings.defaults])
    37→);
    38→
    39→// ============================================================================
    40→// Types
    41→// ============================================================================
    42→
    43→interface ToolSettingsContext {
    44→  projectId?: string;
    45→  shotId?: string;
    46→}
    47→
    48→/** The wrapper format returned by fetchToolSettingsSupabase */
    49→export interface SettingsFetchResult<T = unknown> {
    50→  settings: T;
    51→  hasShotSettings: boolean;
    52→}
    53→
    54→// ============================================================================
    55→// Auth helpers
    56→// ============================================================================
    57→
    58→/**
    59→ * Get authenticated user with timeout protection.
    60→ *
    61→ * Uses a local cache + single-flight deduplication to avoid repeated
    62→ * slow getSession() calls (600ms-16s on mobile networks).
    63→ *
    64→ * @param timeoutMs - Timeout in ms (default 15000, generous for mobile)
    65→ */
    66→export async function getUserWithTimeout(timeoutMs = 15000) {
    67→  const controller = new AbortController();
    68→
    69→  const timeoutId = setTimeout(() => {
    70→    controller.abort();
    71→  }, timeoutMs);
    72→
    73→  try {
    74→    // FIRST: Check cached user to avoid slow getSession calls
    75→    // This is critical because getSession() can take 600ms-16s!
    76→    if (cachedUser && (Date.now() - cachedUserAt) < USER_CACHE_MS) {
    77→      clearTimeout(timeoutId);
    78→      return { data: { user: { id: cachedUser.id } }, error: null };
    79→    }
    80→
    81→    // Fast path: use local session (no network) to avoid auth network call in background
    82→    // Single-flight the getSession call - it's slow and multiple components call it simultaneously
    83→    if (!inflightGetSession) {
    84→      inflightGetSession = supabase.auth.getSession().finally(() => {
    85→        inflightGetSession = null;
    86→      });
    87→    }
    88→
    89→    const { data: sessionData } = await inflightGetSession;
    90→
    91→    const sessionUser = sessionData?.session?.user || null;
    92→    if (sessionUser) {
    93→      cachedUser = { id: sessionUser.id };
    94→      cachedUserAt = Date.now();
    95→      clearTimeout(timeoutId);
    96→      return { data: { user: sessionUser }, error: null };
    97→    }
    98→
    99→    const result = await Promise.race([
   100→      supabase.auth.getUser(),
   101→      new Promise<{ data: { user: null }, error: Error }>((_, reject) =>
   102→        setTimeout(() => reject(new Error('Auth timeout - please check your connection')), timeoutMs)
   103→      )
   104→    ]);
   105→
   106→    clearTimeout(timeoutId);
   107→    const fetchedUserId = result?.data?.user?.id;
   108→    if (fetchedUserId) {
   109→      cachedUser = { id: fetchedUserId };
   110→      cachedUserAt = Date.now();
   111→    }
   112→    return result;
   113→  } catch (error: unknown) {
   114→    clearTimeout(timeoutId);
   115→    if (isAbortError(error)) {
   116→      throw new Error('Auth request was cancelled - please try again');
   117→    }
   118→    throw error;
   119→  }
   120→}
   121→
   122→// ============================================================================
   123→// Settings fetch
   124→// ============================================================================
   125→
   126→/**
   127→ * Fetch and merge tool settings from all scopes using direct Supabase calls.
   128→ *
   129→ * Merges in priority order: defaults -> user -> project -> shot.
   130→ * Uses single-flight deduplication for concurrent identical requests.
   131→ *
   132→ * @returns `{ settings, hasShotSettings }` wrapper
   133→ */
   134→export async function fetchToolSettingsSupabase(
   135→  toolId: string,
   136→  ctx: ToolSettingsContext,
   137→  signal?: AbortSignal
   138→): Promise<SettingsFetchResult> {
   139→  try {
   140→    // Check if request was cancelled before starting - throw to signal cancellation
   141→    if (signal?.aborted) {
   142→      throw new DOMException('Request was cancelled', 'AbortError');
   143→    }
   144→
   145→    // Single-flight dedupe key for concurrent identical requests
   146→    const singleFlightKey = JSON.stringify({ toolId, projectId: ctx.projectId ?? null, shotId: ctx.shotId ?? null });
   147→    const existingPromise = inflightSettingsFetches.get(singleFlightKey);
   148→    if (existingPromise) {
   149→      return existingPromise as Promise<SettingsFetchResult>;
   150→    }
   151→
   152→    const promise = (async (): Promise<SettingsFetchResult> => {
   153→      // Mobile optimization: Cache user info to avoid repeated auth calls
   154→      // Add timeout to prevent hanging on mobile connections (aligned with Supabase global timeout)
   155→      // Use generous timeout for mobile networks
   156→      const { data: { user }, error: authError } = await getUserWithTimeout();
   157→
   158→      if (authError || !user) {
   159→        throw new Error('Authentication required');
   160→      }
   161→
   162→      // Check again after auth call - throw to signal cancellation
   163→      // React Query's retry logic won't retry cancelled requests
   164→      if (signal?.aborted) {
   165→        throw new DOMException('Request was cancelled', 'AbortError');
   166→      }
   167→
   168→      // Mobile optimization: Use more efficient queries with targeted JSON extraction
   169→      // NOTE: We fetch the entire settings JSON to avoid SQL path issues with tool IDs containing hyphens.
   170→      const [userResult, projectResult, shotResult] = await Promise.all([
   171→        supabase
   172→          .from('users')
   173→          .select('settings')
   174→          .eq('id', user.id)
   175→          .maybeSingle(),
   176→
   177→        ctx.projectId
   178→          ? supabase
   179→              .from('projects')
   180→              .select('settings')
   181→              .eq('id', ctx.projectId)
   182→              .maybeSingle()
   183→          : Promise.resolve({ data: null, error: null }),
   184→
   185→        ctx.shotId
   186→          ? supabase
   187→              .from('shots')
   188→              .select('settings')
   189→              .eq('id', ctx.shotId)
   190→              .maybeSingle()
   191→          : Promise.resolve({ data: null, error: null }),
   192→      ]);
   193→
   194→      // Handle errors more gracefully for mobile
   195→
   196→      // Extract tool-specific settings from the full settings JSON
   197→      const userSettingsData = userResult.data?.settings as Record<string, unknown> | null;
   198→      const projectSettingsData = projectResult.data?.settings as Record<string, unknown> | null;
   199→      const shotSettingsData = shotResult.data?.settings as Record<string, unknown> | null;
   200→      const userSettings = (userSettingsData?.[toolId] as Record<string, unknown>) ?? {};
   201→      const projectSettings = (projectSettingsData?.[toolId] as Record<string, unknown>) ?? {};
   202→      const shotSettings = (shotSettingsData?.[toolId] as Record<string, unknown>) ?? {};
   203→
   204→      // Check if shot actually had settings stored (not just empty object)
   205→      const hasShotSettings = shotSettings && Object.keys(shotSettings).length > 0;
   206→
   207→      // Merge in priority order: defaults -> user -> project -> shot
   208→      const merged = deepMerge(
   209→        {},
   210→        toolDefaults[toolId] ?? {},
   211→        userSettings,
   212→        projectSettings,
   213→        shotSettings
   214→      );
   215→
   216→      return { settings: merged, hasShotSettings };
   217→    })();
   218→
   219→    inflightSettingsFetches.set(singleFlightKey, promise);
   220→    promise.finally(() => {
   221→      inflightSettingsFetches.delete(singleFlightKey);
   222→    });
   223→    return promise;
   224→
   225→  } catch (error: unknown) {
   226→    // Handle abort errors silently to reduce noise during task cancellation
   227→    if (isCancellationError(error)) {
   228→      // Don't log these as errors - they're expected during component unmounting
   229→      throw new DOMException('Request was cancelled', 'AbortError');
   230→    }
   231→    // Enrich logging with environment context
   232→    const errorMsg = getErrorMessage(error);
   233→    try {
   234→      const { data: sess } = await supabase.auth.getSession();
   235→      const contextInfo = {
   236→        visibilityState: typeof document !== 'undefined' ? document.visibilityState : 'unknown',
   237→        hidden: typeof document !== 'undefined' ? document.hidden : false,
   238→        online: typeof navigator !== 'undefined' ? navigator.onLine : true,
   239→        hasSession: !!sess?.session,
   240→      };
   241→
   242→      if (errorMsg.includes('Auth timeout') || errorMsg.includes('Auth request was cancelled')) {
   243→        // Return defaults rather than erroring, so UI remains usable
   244→        return { settings: deepMerge({}, toolDefaults[toolId] ?? {}), hasShotSettings: false };
   245→      }
   246→
   247→      if (errorMsg.includes('Failed to fetch')) {
   248→        handleError(error, { context: 'fetchToolSettingsSupabase.network', showToast: false, logData: contextInfo });
   249→        throw new Error('Network connection issue. Please check your internet connection.');
   250→      }
   251→
   252→      handleError(error, { context: 'fetchToolSettingsSupabase', showToast: false, logData: contextInfo });
   253→    } catch (e) {
   254→      // If context gathering fails, still rethrow the original error
   255→      handleError(error, { context: 'fetchToolSettingsSupabase', showToast: false });
   256→    }
   257→    throw error;
   258→  }
   259→}
   260→

1→import { ReactNode } from 'react';
     2→import {
     3→  AlertDialog,
     4→  AlertDialogContent,
     5→  AlertDialogHeader,
     6→  AlertDialogFooter,
     7→  AlertDialogTitle,
     8→  AlertDialogDescription,
     9→  AlertDialogAction,
    10→  AlertDialogCancel,
    11→} from '@/shared/components/ui/alert-dialog';
    12→import { cn } from '@/shared/lib/utils';
    13→
    14→// ============================================================================
    15→// Types
    16→// ============================================================================
    17→
    18→interface ConfirmOptions {
    19→  /** Dialog title */
    20→  title: string;
    21→  /** Dialog description/message */
    22→  description?: ReactNode;
    23→  /** Confirm button text (default: "Confirm") */
    24→  confirmText?: string;
    25→  /** Cancel button text (default: "Cancel") */
    26→  cancelText?: string;
    27→  /** Whether the action is destructive (styles confirm button red) */
    28→  destructive?: boolean;
    29→}
    30→
    31→// ============================================================================
    32→// Standalone Component (for declarative usage)
    33→// ============================================================================
    34→
    35→interface ConfirmDialogProps extends ConfirmOptions {
    36→  /** Whether the dialog is open */
    37→  open: boolean;
    38→  /** Callback when the open state changes */
    39→  onOpenChange: (open: boolean) => void;
    40→  /** Callback when confirmed */
    41→  onConfirm: () => void;
    42→  /** Callback when cancelled (optional - default just closes) */
    43→  onCancel?: () => void;
    44→  /** Whether the confirm action is loading */
    45→  isLoading?: boolean;
    46→}
    47→
    48→/**
    49→ * Standalone confirmation dialog component for declarative usage.
    50→ *
    51→ * @example
    52→ * ```tsx
    53→ * const [showDelete, setShowDelete] = useState(false);
    54→ *
    55→ * <ConfirmDialog
    56→ *   open={showDelete}
    57→ *   onOpenChange={setShowDelete}
    58→ *   title="Delete Item?"
    59→ *   description="This cannot be undone."
    60→ *   confirmText="Delete"
    61→ *   destructive
    62→ *   onConfirm={handleDelete}
    63→ * />
    64→ * ```
    65→ */
    66→export function ConfirmDialog({
    67→  open,
    68→  onOpenChange,
    69→  title,
    70→  description,
    71→  confirmText = 'Confirm',
    72→  cancelText = 'Cancel',
    73→  destructive = false,
    74→  onConfirm,
    75→  onCancel,
    76→  isLoading = false,
    77→}: ConfirmDialogProps) {
    78→  const handleCancel = () => {
    79→    onCancel?.();
    80→    onOpenChange(false);
    81→  };
    82→
    83→  const handleConfirm = () => {
    84→    onConfirm();
    85→    // Don't close automatically - let the parent handle it after async action completes
    86→    // This allows showing loading state
    87→    if (!isLoading) {
    88→      onOpenChange(false);
    89→    }
    90→  };
    91→
    92→  return (
    93→    <AlertDialog open={open} onOpenChange={onOpenChange}>
    94→      <AlertDialogContent>
    95→        <AlertDialogHeader>
    96→          <AlertDialogTitle>{title}</AlertDialogTitle>
    97→          {description && (
    98→            <AlertDialogDescription>{description}</AlertDialogDescription>
    99→          )}
   100→        </AlertDialogHeader>
   101→        <AlertDialogFooter>
   102→          <AlertDialogCancel onClick={handleCancel} disabled={isLoading}>
   103→            {cancelText}
   104→          </AlertDialogCancel>
   105→          <AlertDialogAction

1→import { handleError } from '@/shared/lib/errorHandler';
     2→
     3→interface ProjectCropResult {
     4→  croppedFile: File;
     5→  croppedImageUrl: string;
     6→}
     7→
     8→// Tolerance for aspect ratio matching - if within this, skip re-encoding
     9→const ASPECT_RATIO_TOLERANCE = 0.01;
    10→
    11→/**
    12→ * Crops an image to a specific aspect ratio (for project dimensions).
    13→ * Preserves quality by:
    14→ * - Skipping re-encoding if aspect ratio already matches
    15→ * - Using maximum quality (1.0) when re-encoding is necessary
    16→ * - Preserving original format (PNG/WebP stay lossless)
    17→ *
    18→ * @param inputFile The image file to crop
    19→ * @param targetAspectRatio The target aspect ratio as a number (width / height)
    20→ * @returns Promise with the cropped file and image URL
    21→ */
    22→export const cropImageToProjectAspectRatio = async (
    23→  inputFile: File,
    24→  targetAspectRatio: number
    25→): Promise<ProjectCropResult | null> => {
    26→
    27→  // Mobile browsers (especially iOS) sometimes provide files with an empty MIME type
    28→  // or HEIC/HEIF types. Treat known image extensions as images even if MIME is missing.
    29→  const hasImageMime = typeof inputFile.type === 'string' && inputFile.type.startsWith('image/');
    30→  const looksLikeImageByName = typeof inputFile.name === 'string' && /\.(heic|heif|jpg|jpeg|png|webp|gif|bmp|tif|tiff)$/i.test(inputFile.name);
    31→
    32→  if (!hasImageMime && !looksLikeImageByName) {
    33→    handleError(new Error(`Invalid file type: ${inputFile?.name} (${inputFile?.type})`), { context: 'imageCropper:invalidFileType', showToast: false });
    34→    return null;
    35→  }
    36→
    37→  if (isNaN(targetAspectRatio) || targetAspectRatio <= 0) {
    38→    handleError(new Error(`Invalid target aspect ratio: ${targetAspectRatio}`), { context: 'imageCropper:invalidAspectRatio', showToast: false });
    39→    return null;
    40→  }
    41→
    42→  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    43→    const reader = new FileReader();
    44→    reader.onload = (event) => {
    45→      const img = new Image();
    46→      img.onload = () => {
    47→        const originalWidth = img.width;
    48→        const originalHeight = img.height;
    49→        const originalAspectRatio = originalWidth / originalHeight;
    50→
    51→        // If aspect ratio already matches within tolerance, skip re-encoding to preserve quality
    52→        const aspectDiff = Math.abs(originalAspectRatio - targetAspectRatio);
    53→        if (aspectDiff < ASPECT_RATIO_TOLERANCE) {
    54→          const croppedImageUrl = URL.createObjectURL(inputFile);
    55→          resolve({
    56→            croppedFile: inputFile,
    57→            croppedImageUrl,
    58→          });
    59→          return;
    60→        }
    61→
    62→        let cropX = 0;
    63→        let cropY = 0;
    64→        let newCanvasWidth = originalWidth;
    65→        let newCanvasHeight = originalHeight;
    66→
    67→        // Calculate new dimensions for cropping, maintaining center
    68→        if (originalAspectRatio > targetAspectRatio) {
    69→          // Original image is wider than target, crop width
    70→          newCanvasWidth = originalHeight * targetAspectRatio;
    71→          newCanvasHeight = originalHeight;
    72→          cropX = (originalWidth - newCanvasWidth) / 2;
    73→        } else if (originalAspectRatio < targetAspectRatio) {
    74→          // Original image is taller than target, crop height
    75→          newCanvasWidth = originalWidth;
    76→          newCanvasHeight = originalWidth / targetAspectRatio;
    77→          cropY = (originalHeight - newCanvasHeight) / 2;
    78→        }
    79→
    80→        const canvas = document.createElement("canvas");
    81→        canvas.width = Math.round(newCanvasWidth);
    82→        canvas.height = Math.round(newCanvasHeight);
    83→        const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
    84→
    85→        if (!ctx) {
    86→          reject(new Error("Failed to get canvas context"));
    87→          return;
    88→        }
    89→
    90→        // Use high-quality image smoothing for any scaling
    91→        ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = true;
    92→        ctx.imageSmoothingQuality = 'high';
    93→
    94→        // Draw the cropped portion of the image onto the canvas
    95→        ctx.drawImage(
    96→          img,
    97→          cropX, // source X
    98→          cropY, // source Y
    99→          newCanvasWidth, // source width
   100→          newCanvasHeight, // source height
   101→          0, // destination X
   102→          0, // destination Y
   103→          canvas.width, // destination width
   104→          canvas.height // destination height
   105→        );
   106→
   107→        // Preserve original format, fallback to JPEG for unsupported types
   108→        const outputMime = /^(image\/(jpeg|png|webp))$/i.test(inputFile.type)
   109→          ? inputFile.type
   110→          : 'image/jpeg';
   111→
   112→        // Use maximum quality (1.0) for JPEG/WebP to minimize quality loss
   113→        const quality = 1.0;
   114→
   115→        canvas.toBlob(
   116→          async (blob) => {
   117→            if (!blob) {
   118→              try {
   119→                const dataUrl = canvas.toDataURL(outputMime, quality);
   120→                blob = await (await fetch(dataUrl)).blob();
   121→              } catch (err) {
   122→                reject(new Error("Failed to create blob from canvas"));
   123→                return;
   124→              }
   125→            }
   126→
   127→            const fileExt = outputMime === 'image/png' ? 'png' : outputMime === 'image/webp' ? 'webp' : 'jpg';
   128→            const safeName = inputFile.name.replace(/\.[^/.]+$/, `.${fileExt}`);
   129→            const croppedFile = new File([blob], safeName, {
   130→              type: outputMime,
   131→              lastModified: Date.now(),
   132→            });
   133→            const croppedImageUrl = URL.createObjectURL(croppedFile);
   134→            resolve({
   135→              croppedFile,
   136→              croppedImageUrl,
   137→            });
   138→          },
   139→          outputMime,
   140→          quality
   141→        );
   142→      };
   143→      img.onerror = (err) => {
   144→        reject(new Error("Failed to load image: " + err));
   145→      };
   146→      if (event.target?.result) {
   147→        img.src = event.target.result as string;
   148→      } else {
   149→        reject(new Error("Failed to read file for cropping."));
   150→      }
   151→    };
   152→    reader.onerror = (err) => {
   153→      reject(new Error("FileReader error: " + err));
   154→    };
   155→    reader.readAsDataURL(inputFile);
   156→  });
   157→};

1→import { supabase } from '@/integrations/supabase/client';
     2→import { isAbortError } from '@/shared/lib/errorUtils';
     3→
     4→type InvokeOptions = {
     5→  body?: unknown;
     6→  headers?: Record<string, string>;
     7→  timeoutMs?: number;
     8→  signal?: AbortSignal;
     9→};
    10→
    11→/**
    12→ * Calls supabase.functions.invoke with a client-side timeout and abort propagation.
    13→ * Ensures long-running invocations do not stall the UI indefinitely.
    14→ */
    15→export async function invokeWithTimeout<T = unknown>(functionName: string, options: InvokeOptions = {}): Promise<T> {
    16→  const { body, headers, timeoutMs = 20000, signal } = options;
    17→
    18→  const controller = new AbortController();
    19→  const signals: AbortSignal[] = [];
    20→  if (signal) signals.push(signal);
    21→  signals.push(controller.signal);
    22→
    23→  // Compose signals: abort if any provided signal aborts
    24→  const composed = new AbortController();
    25→  const onAbort = () => composed.abort();
    26→  signals.forEach(signal => {
    27→    if (signal.aborted) composed.abort();
    28→    else signal.addEventListener('abort', onAbort, { once: true });
    29→  });
    30→
    31→  const tid = setTimeout(() => {
    32→    try { controller.abort(); } catch {}
    33→  }, timeoutMs);
    34→
    35→  try {
    36→    const { data, error } = await supabase.functions.invoke(functionName, {
    37→      body,
    38→      headers,
    39→      signal: composed.signal,
    40→    });
    41→    if (error) {
    42→      throw new Error(error.message || `Function ${functionName} failed`);
    43→    }
    44→    return data as T;
    45→  } catch (err: unknown) {
    46→    if (isAbortError(err)) {
    47→      throw new Error(`Function ${functionName} timed out after ${timeoutMs}ms`);
    48→    }
    49→    throw err;
    50→  } finally {
    51→    clearTimeout(tid);
    52→  }
    53→}
    54→
    55→
    56→

1→/**
     2→ * Utility functions for converting URLs to File objects
     3→ * This allows URL-based image inputs to integrate seamlessly with existing file processing pipelines
     4→ */
     5→
     6→/**
     7→ * Fetches an image from a URL and converts it to a File object
     8→ * @param url The URL of the image to fetch
     9→ * @param filename Optional filename for the created File object
    10→ * @returns Promise<File> The image as a File object
    11→ */
    12→const urlToFile = async (url: string, filename?: string): Promise<File> => {
    13→  // Validate URL format
    14→  if (!isValidImageUrl(url)) {
    15→    throw new Error('Invalid image URL provided');
    16→  }
    17→
    18→  try {
    19→    // Fetch the image
    20→    const response = await fetch(url, {
    21→      mode: 'cors', // Handle CORS for external URLs
    22→      headers: {
    23→        'Accept': 'image/*',
    24→      },
    25→    });
    26→
    27→    if (!response.ok) {
    28→      throw new Error(`Failed to fetch image: ${response.status} ${response.statusText}`);
    29→    }
    30→
    31→    // Get the blob
    32→    const blob = await response.blob();
    33→
    34→    // Validate that we got an image
    35→    if (!blob.type.startsWith('image/')) {
    36→      throw new Error(`URL does not point to an image. Content-Type: ${blob.type}`);
    37→    }
    38→
    39→    // Generate filename if not provided
    40→    const finalFilename = filename || generateFilenameFromUrl(url, blob.type);
    41→
    42→    // Convert blob to File
    43→    const file = new File([blob], finalFilename, {
    44→      type: blob.type,
    45→      lastModified: Date.now(),
    46→    });
    47→
    48→    return file;
    49→  } catch (error) {
    50→    if (error instanceof TypeError) {
    51→      // Network errors, CORS issues, etc.
    52→      throw new Error(`Network error fetching image: ${error.message}`);
    53→    }
    54→    throw error;
    55→  }
    56→};
    57→
    58→/**
    59→ * Validates if a URL looks like it could be an image URL
    60→ * @param url The URL to validate
    61→ * @returns boolean True if the URL appears to be valid for image fetching
    62→ */
    63→const isValidImageUrl = (url: string): boolean => {
    64→  try {
    65→    const urlObj = new URL(url);
    66→    
    67→    // Must be http or https
    68→    if (!['http:', 'https:'].includes(urlObj.protocol)) {
    69→      return false;
    70→    }
    71→
    72→    // Basic URL validation passed
    73→    return true;
    74→  } catch {
    75→    return false;
    76→  }
    77→};
    78→
    79→/**
    80→ * Generates a filename from a URL and MIME type
    81→ * @param url The source URL
    82→ * @param mimeType The MIME type of the image
    83→ * @returns string A suitable filename
    84→ */
    85→const generateFilenameFromUrl = (url: string, mimeType: string): string => {
    86→  try {
    87→    const urlObj = new URL(url);
    88→    const pathname = urlObj.pathname;
    89→    
    90→    // Try to extract filename from URL path
    91→    const segments = pathname.split('/');
    92→    const lastSegment = segments[segments.length - 1];
    93→    
    94→    if (lastSegment && lastSegment.includes('.')) {
    95→      return lastSegment;
    96→    }
    97→    
    98→    // Generate filename based on MIME type
    99→    const extension = getExtensionFromMimeType(mimeType);
   100→    const timestamp = Date.now();
   101→    return `image-from-url-${timestamp}.${extension}`;
   102→  } catch {
   103→    // Fallback filename
   104→    const extension = getExtensionFromMimeType(mimeType);
   105→    const timestamp = Date.now();
   106→    return `image-from-url-${timestamp}.${extension}`;
   107→  }
   108→};
   109→
   110→/**
   111→ * Gets file extension from MIME type
   112→ * @param mimeType The MIME type
   113→ * @returns string The file extension
   114→ */
   115→const getExtensionFromMimeType = (mimeType: string): string => {
   116→  const mimeToExt: Record<string, string> = {
   117→    'image/jpeg': 'jpg',
   118→    'image/jpg': 'jpg',
   119→    'image/png': 'png',
   120→    'image/gif': 'gif',
   121→    'image/webp': 'webp',
   122→    'image/svg+xml': 'svg',
   123→    'image/bmp': 'bmp',
   124→    'image/tiff': 'tiff',
   125→  };
   126→  
   127→  return mimeToExt[mimeType.toLowerCase()] || 'jpg';
   128→};
   129→
   130→/**
   131→ * Validates and converts a URL to a File, with user-friendly error messages
   132→ * @param url The URL to process
   133→ * @param filename Optional filename
   134→ * @returns Promise<File> The converted File object
   135→ */
   136→export const processImageUrl = async (url: string, filename?: string): Promise<File> => {
   137→  const trimmedUrl = url.trim();
   138→  
   139→  if (!trimmedUrl) {
   140→    throw new Error('Please enter a valid image URL');
   141→  }
   142→
   143→  if (!isValidImageUrl(trimmedUrl)) {
   144→    throw new Error('Please enter a valid HTTP or HTTPS image URL');
   145→  }
   146→
   147→  try {
   148→    const file = await urlToFile(trimmedUrl, filename);
   149→    
   150→    // Additional validation: check file size (limit to 10MB for style references)
   151→    const maxSize = 10 * 1024 * 1024; // 10MB
   152→    if (file.size > maxSize) {
   153→      throw new Error('Image is too large. Please use an image smaller than 10MB.');
   154→    }
   155→
   156→    return file;
   157→  } catch (error) {
   158→    if (error instanceof Error) {
   159→      // Re-throw with user-friendly message if it's already user-friendly
   160→      if (error.message.includes('Network error') || 
   161→          error.message.includes('Failed to fetch') ||
   162→          error.message.includes('does not point to an image')) {
   163→        throw new Error(`Unable to load image from URL: ${error.message}`);
   164→      }
   165→      throw error;
   166→    }
   167→    throw new Error('Failed to load image from URL. Please check the URL and try again.');
   168→  }
   169→};
   170→

1→/**
     2→ * Mask generation utilities for image reposition operations.
     3→ * Extracts mask from canvas alpha channel and dilates to eliminate edge artifacts.
     4→ */
     5→
     6→interface MaskGenerationOptions {
     7→  /** Alpha threshold (0-255). Pixels with alpha above this are considered solid. Default: 200 */
     8→  alphaThreshold?: number;
     9→  /** Number of pixels to dilate the mask into the image. Default: 3 */
    10→  dilationPixels?: number;
    11→}
    12→
    13→/**
    14→ * Generates a mask canvas from a transformed image canvas.
    15→ * White areas = regions to inpaint (transparent/edge areas)
    16→ * Black areas = regions to keep (solid image content)
    17→ *
    18→ * The mask is dilated by a few pixels to ensure edge artifacts are included in the inpaint region.
    19→ *
    20→ * @param sourceCanvas - Canvas with transformed image (uses alpha channel for mask detection)
    21→ * @param options - Configuration options for threshold and dilation
    22→ * @returns Canvas containing the generated mask
    23→ */
    24→export function generateMaskFromCanvas(
    25→  sourceCanvas: HTMLCanvasElement,
    26→  options: MaskGenerationOptions = {}
    27→): HTMLCanvasElement {
    28→  const { alphaThreshold = 200, dilationPixels = 3 } = options;
    29→
    30→  const width = sourceCanvas.width;
    31→  const height = sourceCanvas.height;
    32→
    33→  const sourceCtx = sourceCanvas.getContext('2d');
    34→  if (!sourceCtx) {
    35→    throw new Error('Could not get source canvas context');
    36→  }
    37→
    38→  // Create mask canvas
    39→  const maskCanvas = document.createElement('canvas');
    40→  maskCanvas.width = width;
    41→  maskCanvas.height = height;
    42→  const maskCtx = maskCanvas.getContext('2d');
    43→
    44→  if (!maskCtx) {
    45→    throw new Error('Could not create mask canvas context');
    46→  }
    47→
    48→  // Start with white (all areas to be inpainted)
    49→  maskCtx.fillStyle = 'white';
    50→  maskCtx.fillRect(0, 0, width, height);
    51→
    52→  // Get image data from both canvases
    53→  const sourceImageData = sourceCtx.getImageData(0, 0, width, height);
    54→  const maskImageData = maskCtx.getImageData(0, 0, width, height);
    55→
    56→  // First pass: create initial mask based on alpha threshold
    57→  // Pixels with alpha > threshold are considered solid (black in mask = don't inpaint)
    58→  // Semi-transparent edge pixels will be white (inpaint these areas)
    59→  for (let i = 0; i < sourceImageData.data.length; i += 4) {
    60→    const alpha = sourceImageData.data[i + 3];
    61→
    62→    if (alpha > alphaThreshold) {
    63→      // Solid pixel - mark as black in mask (keep original)
    64→      maskImageData.data[i] = 0;     // R
    65→      maskImageData.data[i + 1] = 0; // G
    66→      maskImageData.data[i + 2] = 0; // B
    67→      maskImageData.data[i + 3] = 255; // A
    68→    } else {
    69→      // Transparent/semi-transparent pixel - mark as white in mask (inpaint this area)
    70→      maskImageData.data[i] = 255;     // R
    71→      maskImageData.data[i + 1] = 255; // G
    72→      maskImageData.data[i + 2] = 255; // B
    73→      maskImageData.data[i + 3] = 255; // A
    74→    }
    75→  }
    76→
    77→  // Second pass: dilate the white (inpaint) region
    78→  // This ensures we eat into the image slightly to eliminate any anti-aliased edge artifacts
    79→  if (dilationPixels > 0) {
    80→    const tempMaskData = new Uint8ClampedArray(maskImageData.data);
    81→
    82→    for (let y = 0; y < height; y++) {
    83→      for (let x = 0; x < width; x++) {
    84→        const idx = (y * width + x) * 4;
    85→
    86→        // If this pixel is black (image area), check if any neighbor within dilationPixels is white
    87→        if (tempMaskData[idx] === 0) {
    88→          let shouldDilate = false;
    89→
    90→          // Check neighbors in a square region
    91→          for (let dy = -dilationPixels; dy <= dilationPixels && !shouldDilate; dy++) {
    92→            for (let dx = -dilationPixels; dx <= dilationPixels && !shouldDilate; dx++) {
    93→              const nx = x + dx;
    94→              const ny = y + dy;
    95→
    96→              // Skip out of bounds
    97→              if (nx < 0 || nx >= width || ny < 0 || ny >= height) continue;
    98→
    99→              const neighborIdx = (ny * width + nx) * 4;
   100→              // If neighbor is white (inpaint area), dilate this pixel
   101→              if (tempMaskData[neighborIdx] === 255) {
   102→                shouldDilate = true;
   103→              }
   104→            }
   105→          }
   106→
   107→          if (shouldDilate) {
   108→            // Convert this pixel from black (keep) to white (inpaint)
   109→            maskImageData.data[idx] = 255;     // R
   110→            maskImageData.data[idx + 1] = 255; // G
   111→            maskImageData.data[idx + 2] = 255; // B
   112→            maskImageData.data[idx + 3] = 255; // A
   113→          }
   114→        }
   115→      }
   116→    }
   117→  }
   118→
   119→  maskCtx.putImageData(maskImageData, 0, 0);
   120→
   121→  return maskCanvas;
   122→}
   123→
   124→/**
   125→ * Creates a canvas with a solid background color and the source image drawn on top.
   126→ * This prevents anti-aliased edge pixels from appearing as dark borders by ensuring
   127→ * they blend with the background color.
   128→ *
   129→ * @param sourceCanvas - Canvas with transformed image (may have transparent areas)
   130→ * @param backgroundColor - CSS color for the background (default: '#00FF00' green)
   131→ * @returns Canvas with solid background and image composited on top
   132→ */
   133→export function createCanvasWithBackground(
   134→  sourceCanvas: HTMLCanvasElement,
   135→  backgroundColor: string = '#00FF00'
   136→): HTMLCanvasElement {
   137→  const outputCanvas = document.createElement('canvas');
   138→  outputCanvas.width = sourceCanvas.width;
   139→  outputCanvas.height = sourceCanvas.height;
   140→  const outputCtx = outputCanvas.getContext('2d');
   141→
   142→  if (!outputCtx) {
   143→    throw new Error('Could not create output canvas context');
   144→  }
   145→
   146→  // Fill with background color first
   147→  outputCtx.fillStyle = backgroundColor;
   148→  outputCtx.fillRect(0, 0, outputCanvas.width, outputCanvas.height);
   149→
   150→  // Draw transformed image on top - anti-aliased edges will blend with background
   151→  outputCtx.drawImage(sourceCanvas, 0, 0);
   152→
   153→  return outputCanvas;
   154→}
   155→

1→/**
     2→ * Simple Cache Validator - Console Testing Tool
     3→ *
     4→ * Run this in browser console to test cache cleanup:
     5→ * ```
     6→ * // Test current cache state
     7→ * validateImageCache()
     8→ *
     9→ * // Start real-time monitoring
    10→ * startCacheWatch()
    11→ * ```
    12→ */
    13→
    14→import { handleError } from '@/shared/lib/errorHandler';
    15→
    16→// Make available globally in development
    17→if (typeof window !== 'undefined' && import.meta.env.DEV) {
    18→  (window as any).validateImageCache = () => {
    19→    console.group('🗂️ Image Cache Validation');
    20→    
    21→    try {
    22→      // Simple approach: look at what's actually in the browser
    23→      const generationImages = document.querySelectorAll('img[src*="supabase.co/storage"]');
    24→      const generationVideos = document.querySelectorAll('video[src*="supabase.co/storage"]');
    25→      
    26→      console.log('📊 Current Media State:', {
    27→        visibleImages: generationImages.length,
    28→        visibleVideos: generationVideos.length,
    29→        totalVisibleMedia: generationImages.length + generationVideos.length,
    30→        timestamp: new Date().toISOString()
    31→      });
    32→      
    33→      // Look for pagination indicators
    34→      const paginationText = document.querySelector('[class*="text-sm"][class*="muted-foreground"]')?.textContent;
    35→      const pageMatch = paginationText?.match(/(\d+)-(\d+) of (\d+)/);
    36→      
    37→      if (pageMatch) {
    38→        const [, start, end, total] = pageMatch;
    39→        const currentPage = Math.ceil(parseInt(start) / 25); // Assuming 25 items per page
    40→        console.log('📄 Current Page Info:', {
    41→          currentPage,
    42→          itemRange: `${start}-${end}`,
    43→          totalItems: total,
    44→          estimatedTotalPages: Math.ceil(parseInt(total) / 25)
    45→        });
    46→      } else {
    47→        console.log('📄 Could not detect current page from UI');
    48→      }
    49→      
    50→      // Check for browser cache information
    51→      if ('storage' in navigator && 'estimate' in navigator.storage) {
    52→        navigator.storage.estimate().then(estimate => {
    53→          console.log('💾 Browser Storage Info:', {
    54→            usageInMB: Math.round((estimate.usage || 0) / 1024 / 1024),
    55→            quotaInMB: Math.round((estimate.quota || 0) / 1024 / 1024),
    56→            usagePercent: Math.round(((estimate.usage || 0) / (estimate.quota || 1)) * 100)
    57→          });
    58→        });
    59→      }
    60→      
    61→      console.log('To see detailed cache logs:');
    62→      console.log('   1. Navigate between pages (1 -> 2 -> 5 -> 3)');
    63→      console.log('   2. Watch console for [CacheValidator] messages');
    64→      console.log('   3. Look for "Current cache: pages [X, Y, Z]" logs');
    65→
    66→    } catch (error) {
    67→      handleError(error, { context: 'SimpleCacheValidator', showToast: false });
    68→    }
    69→    
    70→    console.groupEnd();
    71→  };
    72→  
    73→  (window as any).startCacheWatch = () => {
    74→    let lastMediaCount = 0;
    75→    
    76→    const monitor = () => {
    77→      try {
    78→        const images = document.querySelectorAll('img[src*="supabase.co/storage"]');
    79→        const videos = document.querySelectorAll('video[src*="supabase.co/storage"]');
    80→        const currentMediaCount = images.length + videos.length;
    81→        
    82→        if (currentMediaCount !== lastMediaCount) {
    83→          lastMediaCount = currentMediaCount;
    84→        }
    85→      } catch (e) {
    86→        // Silent fail
    87→      }
    88→    };
    89→    
    90→    const intervalId = setInterval(monitor, 1000);
    91→    console.log('🔍 Cache monitoring started (every 1s)');
    92→    console.log('📱 Navigate between pages to see cache behavior');
    93→    console.log('⏹️ Run stopCacheWatch() to stop monitoring');
    94→    
    95→    (window as any).stopCacheWatch = () => {
    96→      clearInterval(intervalId);
    97→      console.log('⏹️ Cache monitoring stopped');
    98→    };
    99→  };
   100→

1→/**
     2→ * Unified Image Loading Priority System
     3→ *
     4→ * Single source of truth for all image loading behavior.
     5→ * Progressive loading is the primary mechanism - individual items no longer have separate delays.
     6→ */
     7→
     8→import type { NavigatorWithDeviceInfo } from '@/types/browser-extensions';
     9→
    10→interface LoadingConfig {
    11→  isMobile: boolean;
    12→  totalImages: number;
    13→  isPreloaded: boolean;
    14→}
    15→
    16→interface ImageLoadingStrategy {
    17→  shouldLoadInInitialBatch: boolean;
    18→  progressiveDelay: number; // Unified delay calculation
    19→  batchGroup: number;
    20→}
    21→
    22→/**
    23→ * Device capability detection for adaptive loading
    24→ */
    25→const getDeviceCapabilities = () => {
    26→  const nav = navigator as NavigatorWithDeviceInfo;
    27→  const isMobile = window.innerWidth <= 768;
    28→  const hasLowMemory = nav.deviceMemory !== undefined && nav.deviceMemory <= 4;
    29→  const hasLowEndCPU = 'hardwareConcurrency' in navigator && navigator.hardwareConcurrency <= 2;
    30→  const hasVeryLowEndCPU = 'hardwareConcurrency' in navigator && navigator.hardwareConcurrency === 1;
    31→  const hasSlowConnection = nav.connection !== undefined &&
    32→    (nav.connection.effectiveType === '2g' ||
    33→     nav.connection.effectiveType === 'slow-2g');
    34→  
    35→  return {
    36→    isMobile,
    37→    hasLowMemory,
    38→    hasLowEndCPU,
    39→    hasVeryLowEndCPU,
    40→    hasSlowConnection,
    41→    isLowEnd: hasSlowConnection || (hasLowMemory && hasLowEndCPU),
    42→    isVeryLowEnd: hasVeryLowEndCPU || (hasSlowConnection && hasLowMemory)
    43→  };
    44→};
    45→
    46→// Performance tracking
    47→interface PerformanceMetrics {
    48→  avgLoadTime: number;
    49→  loadTimes: number[];
    50→  adjustedDelayMultiplier: number;
    51→}
    52→
    53→
    54→/**
    55→ * Adaptive batch configuration based on device capabilities
    56→ */
    57→const getUnifiedBatchConfig = (isMobile: boolean) => {
    58→  const capabilities = getDeviceCapabilities();
    59→  
    60→  // Very low-end mobile: minimal initial batch
    61→  if (capabilities.isVeryLowEnd && isMobile) {
    62→    return {
    63→      initialBatchSize: 2, // Only 2 images immediately
    64→      staggerDelay: 60, // Slower stagger for weak devices
    65→      maxStaggerDelay: 150
    66→    };
    67→  }
    68→  
    69→  // Low-end or mobile: conservative settings
    70→  if (capabilities.isLowEnd || isMobile) {
    71→    return {
    72→      initialBatchSize: 3, // First 3 load immediately
    73→      staggerDelay: capabilities.hasSlowConnection ? 50 : 40, // Adaptive based on connection
    74→      maxStaggerDelay: 120
    75→    };
    76→  }
    77→  
    78→  // Desktop/high-end: aggressive settings
    79→  return {
    80→    initialBatchSize: 4, // First 4 load immediately
    81→    staggerDelay: 25, // Fast delays for good hardware
    82→    maxStaggerDelay: 100
    83→  };
    84→};
    85→
    86→/**
    87→ * Main function: determines loading strategy for an image
    88→ * Simplified to use a single progressive delay calculation
    89→ */
    90→export const getImageLoadingStrategy = (
    91→  index: number, 
    92→  config: LoadingConfig
    93→): ImageLoadingStrategy => {
    94→  const { isMobile, isPreloaded } = config;
    95→  
    96→  const batchConfig = getUnifiedBatchConfig(isMobile);
    97→  const { initialBatchSize, staggerDelay, maxStaggerDelay } = batchConfig;
    98→  
    99→  // Determine which batch this image belongs to
   100→  const batchGroup = Math.floor(index / initialBatchSize);
   101→  
   102→  // Simplified progressive delay calculation
   103→  let progressiveDelay: number;
   104→  const shouldLoadInInitialBatch = index < initialBatchSize;
   105→  
   106→  if (isPreloaded) {
   107→    // Preloaded images always load immediately
   108→    progressiveDelay = 0;
   109→  } else if (index === 0) {
   110→    // First image always loads immediately
   111→    progressiveDelay = 0;
   112→  } else if (shouldLoadInInitialBatch) {
   113→    // Initial batch with minimal delays for smooth appearance
   114→    progressiveDelay = index * 8; // 0ms, 8ms, 16ms, 24ms for first 4
   115→  } else {
   116→    // Progressive stagger for remaining images
   117→    const staggerIndex = index - initialBatchSize;
   118→    progressiveDelay = Math.min(
   119→      staggerDelay * (staggerIndex + 1),
   120→      maxStaggerDelay // Cap maximum delay
   121→    );
   122→  }
   123→  
   124→  return {
   125→    shouldLoadInInitialBatch,
   126→    progressiveDelay,
   127→    batchGroup
   128→  };
   129→};
   130→
   131→
   132→// Legacy functions removed - use getImageLoadingStrategy and getUnifiedBatchConfig instead
   133→

You are writing tests for TASK CREATION files, SHARED UTILS, and TOOL UTILS in a Vite/Vitest project.

## Rules
1. Use explicit vitest imports: `import { describe, it, expect, vi, beforeEach } from 'vitest'`
2. Pattern: `filename.test.ts` in `__tests__/` directories
3. The project uses `@` as alias for `src/`
4. Mock external deps (supabase, etc.) where needed
5. Write each test file using the Write tool
6. Do NOT write tests for files that already have tests — check first by looking for existing test files

## Scope — Three areas:

### Area 1: Task creation files (`src/shared/lib/tasks/`)
Tests go in `src/shared/lib/tasks/__tests__/`

These files build task params for different generation types. The pattern is: they export a function that takes settings/config and returns task params. Mock `createTask` from `@/shared/lib/taskCreation` and verify the params built.

Key files:
1. **individualTravelSegment.ts** (~700 LOC) - Travel segment task creation
2. **imageGeneration.ts** (~492 LOC) - Image generation tasks
3. **joinClips.ts** (~442 LOC) - Join clips tasks

5. **videoEnhance.ts** (~247 LOC) - Video enhance tasks
6. **zImageTurboI2I.ts** (~245 LOC) - Turbo image-to-image

1→/**
     2→ * useSaveFieldAsDefault
     3→ *
     4→ * Shared hook for the "save a single field value as the shot default" pattern.
     5→ * Used by both SegmentSettingsForm and AdvancedSettingsSection to avoid duplicating
     6→ * the save-field-as-default callback and its associated loading state.
     7→ */
     8→
     9→import { useState, useCallback } from 'react';
    10→import type { SegmentSettings } from '../types';
    11→
    12→interface UseSaveFieldAsDefaultProps {
    13→  onSaveFieldAsDefault?: (field: keyof SegmentSettings, value: SegmentSettings[keyof SegmentSettings]) => Promise<boolean>;
    14→  onChange: (updates: Partial<SegmentSettings>) => void;
    15→}
    16→
    17→interface UseSaveFieldAsDefaultReturn {
    18→  savingField: string | null;
    19→  handleSaveFieldAsDefault: (field: keyof SegmentSettings, value: SegmentSettings[keyof SegmentSettings]) => Promise<void>;
    20→}
    21→
    22→export function useSaveFieldAsDefault({
    23→  onSaveFieldAsDefault,
    24→  onChange,
    25→}: UseSaveFieldAsDefaultProps): UseSaveFieldAsDefaultReturn {
    26→  const [savingField, setSavingField] = useState<string | null>(null);
    27→
    28→  const handleSaveFieldAsDefault = useCallback(async (field: keyof SegmentSettings, value: SegmentSettings[keyof SegmentSettings]) => {
    29→    if (!onSaveFieldAsDefault) return;
    30→    setSavingField(field);
    31→    try {
    32→      const success = await onSaveFieldAsDefault(field, value);
    33→      if (success) {
    34→        await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 0));
    35→        onChange({ [field]: undefined } as Partial<SegmentSettings>);
    36→      }
    37→    } finally {
    38→      setSavingField(null);
    39→    }
    40→  }, [onSaveFieldAsDefault, onChange]);
    41→
    42→  return { savingField, handleSaveFieldAsDefault };
    43→}
    44→
