1→import { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
     2→import { toast } from '@/shared/components/ui/sonner';
     3→import { handleError } from '@/shared/lib/errorHandler';
     4→
     5→const MAX_LOCAL_STORAGE_ITEM_LENGTH = 4 * 1024 * 1024; // 4MB
     6→
     7→const PERSISTENT_STATE_EVENT = 'persistentStateChange';
     8→
     9→// Check if localStorage is available (can fail in iOS Safari private mode)
    10→function isLocalStorageAvailable(): boolean {
    11→  try {
    12→    const test = '__localStorage_test__';
    13→    localStorage.setItem(test, test);
    14→    localStorage.removeItem(test);
    15→    return true;
    16→  } catch {
    17→    return false;
    18→  }
    19→}
    20→
    21→function usePersistentState<T>(key: string, defaultValue: T): [T, React.Dispatch<React.SetStateAction<T>>] {
    22→  const [state, setState] = useState<T>(() => {
    23→    // Mobile Safari in private mode can throw on localStorage access
    24→    if (!isLocalStorageAvailable()) {
    25→      return defaultValue;
    26→    }
    27→
    28→    try {
    29→      const storedValue = localStorage.getItem(key);
    30→      if (storedValue) {
    31→        return JSON.parse(storedValue) as T;
    32→      }
    33→    } catch (error) {
    34→      handleError(error, { context: 'usePersistentState', showToast: false });
    35→    }
    36→    return defaultValue;
    37→  });
    38→
    39→  // Listen for updates from other components using the same key
    40→  useEffect(() => {
    41→    function handleExternalUpdate(e: Event) {
    42→      const customEvt = e as CustomEvent<{ key: string; value: unknown }>;
    43→      if (customEvt.detail?.key === key) {
    44→        setState(customEvt.detail.value as T);
    45→      }
    46→    }
    47→
    48→    window.addEventListener(PERSISTENT_STATE_EVENT, handleExternalUpdate);
    49→    return () => window.removeEventListener(PERSISTENT_STATE_EVENT, handleExternalUpdate);
    50→  }, [key]);
    51→
    52→  useEffect(() => {
    53→    // Skip localStorage writes if not available
    54→    if (!isLocalStorageAvailable()) {
    55→      return;
    56→    }
    57→
    58→    try {
    59→      const serializedState = JSON.stringify(state);
    60→      if (serializedState.length > MAX_LOCAL_STORAGE_ITEM_LENGTH) {
    61→        toast.warning("Could not save settings locally.", {
    62→          description: "The data size exceeds the 4MB limit for local storage.",
    63→        });
    64→        return;
    65→      }
    66→      localStorage.setItem(key, serializedState);
    67→
    68→      // Broadcast change to other hook instances in the same tab
    69→      window.dispatchEvent(
    70→        new CustomEvent(PERSISTENT_STATE_EVENT, {
    71→          detail: { key, value: state },
    72→        })
    73→      );
    74→    } catch (error) {
    75→      // Different error message for mobile users
    76→      const isMobile = /iPhone|iPad|iPod|Android/i.test(navigator.userAgent);
    77→      const errorDescription = isMobile
    78→        ? "Local storage may be disabled in private browsing mode. Settings will be lost when the tab is closed."
    79→        : "There was an error writing to your browser's local storage.";
    80→
    81→      handleError(error, {
    82→        context: 'usePersistentState',
    83→        toastTitle: 'Could not save settings locally.',
    84→        toastDescription: errorDescription
    85→      });
    86→    }
    87→  }, [key, state]);
    88→
    89→  return [state, setState];
    90→}
    91→
    92→export default usePersistentState;
    93→

   130→      }
   131→      if (!allProjects && !effectiveProjectId) {
   132→        return { tasks: [], total: 0, hasMore: false, totalPages: 0, distinctTaskTypes: [] };
   133→      }
   134→
   135→      // GALLERY PATTERN: Get count and data separately, efficiently
   136→      // Always get accurate count - the approximation was causing 10x multiplication bug
   137→      const shouldSkipCount = false;
   138→
   139→      // 1. Get total count with lightweight query (skip if fast polling likely)
   140→      // IMPORTANT: Filter to only visible task types at DB level to match what's displayed
   141→      const visibleTaskTypes = getVisibleTaskTypes();
   142→
   143→      let countQuery = supabase
   144→        .from('tasks')
   145→        .select('*', { count: 'exact', head: true })
   146→        .is('params->orchestrator_task_id_ref', null) // Only parent tasks
   147→        .in('task_type', visibleTaskTypes); // Only visible task types
   148→
   149→      // Apply project filter: either single project or multiple projects
   150→      if (allProjects && allProjectIds) {
   151→        countQuery = countQuery.in('project_id', allProjectIds);
   152→      } else {
   153→        countQuery = countQuery.eq('project_id', effectiveProjectId!);
   154→      }
   155→
   156→      if (status && status.length > 0) {
   157→        countQuery = countQuery.in('status', status);
   158→      }
   159→
   160→      // Apply task type filter to count query (server-side filter)
   161→      if (taskType) {
   162→        countQuery = countQuery.eq('task_type', taskType);
   163→      }
   164→
   165→      // 2. Get paginated data with proper database pagination
   166→      // Strategy: Use database pagination for most cases, only fetch extra for Processing status that needs sorting
   167→      const needsCustomSorting = status?.some(s => s === TASK_STATUS.QUEUED || s === TASK_STATUS.IN_PROGRESS);
   168→
   169→      let dataQuery = supabase
   170→        .from('tasks')
   171→        .select('*')
   172→        .is('params->orchestrator_task_id_ref', null) // Only parent tasks
   173→        .in('task_type', visibleTaskTypes); // Only visible task types
   174→
   175→      // Apply project filter: either single project or multiple projects
   176→      if (allProjects && allProjectIds) {
   177→        dataQuery = dataQuery.in('project_id', allProjectIds);
   178→      } else {
   179→        dataQuery = dataQuery.eq('project_id', effectiveProjectId!);
   180→      }
   181→
   182→      // For Succeeded view, order by completion time (most recent first)
   183→      const succeededOnly = status && status.length === 1 && status[0] === TASK_STATUS.COMPLETE;
   184→      if (succeededOnly) {
   185→        dataQuery = dataQuery
   186→          .order('generation_processed_at', { ascending: false, nullsFirst: false })
   187→          .order('created_at', { ascending: false }); // tie-breaker
   188→      } else {
   189→        // Default DB ordering; Processing will use client-side custom sort
   190→        dataQuery = dataQuery.order('created_at', { ascending: false });
   191→      }
   192→
   193→      if (status && status.length > 0) {
   194→        dataQuery = dataQuery.in('status', status);
   195→      }
   196→
   197→      // Apply task type filter to data query (server-side filter)
   198→      if (taskType) {
   199→        dataQuery = dataQuery.eq('task_type', taskType);
   200→      }

   202→      if (needsCustomSorting) {
   203→        // For Processing tasks: Use progressive loading strategy
   204→        // Start with a reasonable chunk size, expand if needed for first page
   205→        const effectiveBaseLimit = Math.max(limit, PAGINATION_CONFIG.DEFAULT_LIMIT);
   206→        let fetchLimit;
   207→
   208→        if (page === 1) {
   209→          // First page: fetch more to get a good sample for sorting, but cap it reasonably
   210→          fetchLimit = Math.min(effectiveBaseLimit * PAGINATION_CONFIG.PROCESSING_FETCH_MULTIPLIER, PAGINATION_CONFIG.PROCESSING_MAX_FETCH);
   211→        } else {
   212→          // Subsequent pages: use standard pagination since first page established sort order
   213→          fetchLimit = effectiveBaseLimit;
   214→        }
   215→
   216→        dataQuery = dataQuery.limit(fetchLimit);
   217→      } else {
   218→        // For Succeeded/Failed: use proper database pagination - no client sorting needed
   219→        dataQuery = dataQuery.range(offset, offset + limit - 1);
   220→      }
   221→
   222→      // Execute queries (skip count for fast polling scenarios)
   223→      const [countResult, { data, error: dataError }] = await Promise.all([
   224→        shouldSkipCount ? Promise.resolve({ count: null, error: null }) : countQuery,
   225→        dataQuery,
   226→      ]);
   227→
   228→      const { count, error: countError } = countResult;
   229→
   230→      if (countError) {
   231→        console.error('[TaskPollingDebug] Count query failed:', countError);
   232→        // Track failure for circuit breaker
   233→        dataFreshnessManager.onFetchFailure(queryKeys.tasks.paginated(effectiveProjectId), countError as Error);
   234→        throw countError;
   235→      }
   236→      if (dataError) {
   237→        console.error('[TaskPollingDebug] Data query failed:', dataError);
   238→        // Track failure for circuit breaker
   239→        dataFreshnessManager.onFetchFailure(queryKeys.tasks.paginated(effectiveProjectId), dataError as Error);
   240→        throw dataError;
   241→      }
   242→
   243→      // Track success for circuit breaker
   244→      dataFreshnessManager.onFetchSuccess(queryKeys.tasks.paginated(effectiveProjectId));
   245→
   246→      // Apply client-side filtering and sorting
   247→      const allTasks = (data || []).map(mapDbTaskToTask);
   248→      const visibleTasks = filterVisibleTasks(allTasks);
   249→
   250→      let paginatedTasks: typeof allTasks;
   251→
   252→      if (needsCustomSorting) {
   253→        // In Progress first, then Queued; within each, oldest to newest by created_at
   254→        const sortedTasks = visibleTasks.sort((a, b) => {
   255→          const getStatusPriority = (status: string) => {
   256→            switch (status) {
   257→              case TASK_STATUS.IN_PROGRESS: return 1;
   258→              case TASK_STATUS.QUEUED: return 2;
   259→              default: return 3;
   260→            }
   261→          };
   262→          const aPriority = getStatusPriority(a.status);
   263→          const bPriority = getStatusPriority(b.status);
   264→          if (aPriority !== bPriority) {
   265→            return aPriority - bPriority; // lower is higher priority
   266→          }
   267→          const aDate = new Date(a.createdAt || 0);
   268→          const bDate = new Date(b.createdAt || 0);
   269→          return aDate.getTime() - bDate.getTime(); // oldest first
   270→        });
   271→        paginatedTasks = sortedTasks.slice(offset, offset + limit);
   272→      } else {
   273→        // For Succeeded/Failed: data is already paginated by database
   274→        paginatedTasks = visibleTasks;
   275→      }
   276→
   277→      // Use approximation when count is skipped during fast polling
   278→      // For Processing tasks, use a more reasonable approximation based on current page
   279→      const total = count !== null ? count : Math.max(paginatedTasks.length, offset + paginatedTasks.length);
   280→      const totalPages = Math.ceil(total / limit);
   281→      const hasMore = count !== null ? offset + limit < total : paginatedTasks.length >= limit;
   282→
   283→      const result: PaginatedTasksResponse = {
   284→        tasks: paginatedTasks,
   285→        total,
   286→        hasMore,
   287→        totalPages,
   288→      };
   289→
   290→      return result;
   291→    },
   292→    enabled: !!effectiveProjectId,
   293→    // Keep previous page's data visible during refetches to avoid UI blanks
   294→    placeholderData: (previousData: PaginatedTasksResponse | undefined) => previousData,
   295→    // Use realtimeBacked preset - tasks updated via realtime + mutations
   296→    ...QUERY_PRESETS.realtimeBacked,
   297→    // SMART POLLING: Intelligent polling based on realtime health
   298→    ...smartPollingConfig,
   299→    refetchIntervalInBackground: true, // Enable background polling

   301→    retry: STANDARD_RETRY,
   302→    retryDelay: STANDARD_RETRY_DELAY,
   303→  });
   304→
   305→  // NUCLEAR OPTION: Force refetch if query has data but no tasks for Processing view
   306→  // SAFETY: Only trigger if data is genuinely stale (older than 30 seconds) to prevent infinite loops
   307→  const isProcessingFilter = status && status.includes('Queued') && status.includes('In Progress');
   308→  const hasStaleEmptyData = query.data && query.data.tasks && query.data.tasks.length === 0 && !query.isFetching;
   309→  const dataAge = query.dataUpdatedAt ? Date.now() - query.dataUpdatedAt : Infinity;
   310→
   311→  // Use React ref to prevent rapid refetches
   312→  const lastRefetchRef = React.useRef<number>(0);
   313→  const timeSinceLastRefetch = Date.now() - lastRefetchRef.current;
   314→
   315→  // When backgrounded, dampen nuclear refetches to avoid thrash under timer clamping
   316→  const isHidden = typeof document !== 'undefined' ? document.hidden : false;
   317→  const minBackoffMs = isHidden ? 60000 : 10000;
   318→  const hiddenStaleThresholdMs = isHidden ? 60000 : 30000;
   319→  const meetsStaleThreshold = dataAge > hiddenStaleThresholdMs;
   320→
   321→  if (isProcessingFilter && hasStaleEmptyData && query.status === 'success' && meetsStaleThreshold && timeSinceLastRefetch > minBackoffMs) {
   322→    lastRefetchRef.current = Date.now();
   323→    // Force immediate refetch
   324→    query.refetch();
   325→  }
   326→
   327→  return query;
   328→};

1→/**
     2→ * useSourceImageChanges Hook
     3→ *
     4→ * Detects when source images for video segments no longer match what was used
     5→ * to create the video. This can happen when:
     6→ * - A different variant is promoted on the source image
     7→ * - The source generation is replaced (reordering, deletion)
     8→ * - The source image slot now has a different generation
     9→ *
    10→ * The warning appears for 5 minutes after a source image changes.
    11→ *
    12→ * Detection approach:
    13→ * 1. Look up what generation is CURRENTLY at each pair_shot_generation_id slot
    14→ * 2. Compare that generation's location with the stored URL from when video was created
    15→ * 3. This detects both variant changes AND slot reordering/replacement
    16→ */
    17→
    18→import { useMemo } from 'react';
    19→import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query';
    20→import { supabase } from '@/integrations/supabase/client';
    21→import { handleError } from '@/shared/lib/errorHandler';
    22→import { extractSegmentImages } from '@/shared/lib/galleryUtils';
    23→
    24→// How long to show the warning after a source change (in milliseconds)
    25→const SOURCE_CHANGE_WARNING_DURATION_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000; // 5 minutes
    26→
    27→interface SourceMismatchInfo {
    28→  segmentId: string;
    29→  hasMismatch: boolean;
    30→  isRecent: boolean;
    31→  startMismatch: boolean;
    32→  endMismatch: boolean;
    33→  changedAt: Date | null;
    34→}
    35→
    36→interface SegmentSourceInfo {
    37→  segmentId: string;
    38→  childOrder: number;
    39→  params: Record<string, unknown>;
    40→  startGenId: string | null;
    41→  endGenId: string | null;
    42→}
    43→
    44→/**
    45→ * Check if video segments' source images have changed
    46→ *
    47→ * @param segments - Array of segment info (id, params, childOrder)
    48→ * @param enabled - Whether to run the query
    49→ * @returns Map of segment ID -> mismatch info
    50→ */
    51→export function useSourceImageChanges(
    52→  segments: SegmentSourceInfo[],
    53→  enabled: boolean = true
    54→) {
    55→  // Extract start generation IDs - videos are attached to the start generation,
    56→  // so we need to find where each start gen is and what's next to it
    57→  const startGenIds = useMemo(() => {
    58→    const genIds = new Set<string>();
    59→
    60→    segments.forEach(seg => {
    61→      // Get the start generation ID (the generation the video is attached to)
    62→      if (seg.startGenId) {
    63→        genIds.add(seg.startGenId);
    64→      }
    65→
    66→    });
    67→
    68→    return Array.from(genIds);
    69→  }, [segments, enabled]);
    70→
    71→  // Query current generations at each slot (shot_generations -> generations)
    72→  const { data: slotData, isLoading } = useQuery({
    73→    queryKey: ['source-slot-generations', ...startGenIds.sort((a, b) => a.localeCompare(b))],
    74→    queryFn: async () => {
    75→      if (startGenIds.length === 0) return {};
    76→
    77→      // Step 1: Find where each start generation is on the timeline
    78→      const { data: startSlots, error: startError } = await supabase
    79→        .from('shot_generations')
    80→        .select('id, shot_id, generation_id, timeline_frame, updated_at')
    81→        .in('generation_id', startGenIds)
    82→        .not('timeline_frame', 'is', null);
    83→
    84→      if (startError) {
    85→        console.error('[SourceChange] ❌ Start slot query error:', startError);
    86→        return {};
    87→      }
    88→
    89→      if (!startSlots || startSlots.length === 0) {
    90→        return {};
    91→      }
    92→
    93→      // Get the shot_id (assuming all segments are from same shot)
    94→      const shotId = startSlots[0].shot_id;
    95→
    96→      // Step 2: Get ALL positioned slots for this shot to find what's next to each start gen
    97→      const { data: allSlots, error: allError } = await supabase
    98→        .from('shot_generations')
    99→        .select('id, generation_id, timeline_frame, updated_at')
   100→        .eq('shot_id', shotId)
   101→        .not('timeline_frame', 'is', null)
   102→        .order('timeline_frame', { ascending: true });
   103→
   104→      if (allError) {
   105→        console.error('[SourceChange] ❌ All slots query error:', allError);
   106→        return {};
   107→      }
   108→
   109→      // Build ordered list for finding "next" generation
   110→      const orderedSlots = allSlots || [];
   111→
   112→      // Build map: startGenId -> { startSlotInfo, nextGenId, nextSlotUpdatedAt }
   113→      const startGenToNext: Record<string, { startSlot: typeof startSlots[number]; nextGenId: string | null; nextSlotUpdatedAt: Date | null }> = {};
   114→      startSlots.forEach(slot => {
   115→        const idx = orderedSlots.findIndex(s => s.generation_id === slot.generation_id);
   116→        const nextSlot = idx >= 0 && idx < orderedSlots.length - 1 ? orderedSlots[idx + 1] : null;
   117→        startGenToNext[slot.generation_id] = {
   118→          startSlot: slot,
   119→          nextGenId: nextSlot?.generation_id || null,
   120→          // Track when the next slot was last updated (for timeline reorder detection)
   121→          nextSlotUpdatedAt: nextSlot?.updated_at ? new Date(nextSlot.updated_at) : null,
   122→        };
   123→      });
   124→
   125→      // Step 3: Get all generation IDs we need (start + next)
   126→      const allGenIds = new Set<string>();
   127→      Object.values(startGenToNext).forEach(({ startSlot, nextGenId }) => {
   128→        allGenIds.add(startSlot.generation_id);
   129→        if (nextGenId) allGenIds.add(nextGenId);
   130→      });
   131→
   132→      // Combine slot data for later processing
   133→      const slotData = orderedSlots;
   134→      const slotError = null;
   135→
   136→      if (slotError) {
   137→        console.error('[SourceChange] ❌ Slot query error:', slotError);
   138→        return {};
   139→      }
   140→
   141→      // Get generation IDs to look up their primary variants
   142→      const genIds = (slotData || []).map(s => s.generation_id).filter(Boolean);
   143→      if (genIds.length === 0) {
   144→        return {};
   145→      }
   146→
   147→      // Query generations with their primary variant location
   148→      const { data: genData, error: genError } = await supabase
   149→        .from('generations')
   150→        .select('id, primary_variant_id, updated_at')
   151→        .in('id', genIds);
   152→
   153→      if (genError) {
   154→        console.error('[SourceChange] ❌ Generation query error:', genError);
   155→        return {};
   156→      }
   157→
   158→      // Get primary variant IDs
   159→      const variantIds = (genData || []).map(g => g.primary_variant_id).filter(Boolean);
   160→
   161→      // Query variants for their locations
   162→      let variantLocations: Record<string, { location: string; created_at: string }> = {};
   163→      if (variantIds.length > 0) {
   164→        const { data: variantData, error: variantError } = await supabase
   165→          .from('generation_variants')
   166→          .select('id, location, created_at')
   167→          .in('id', variantIds);
   168→
   169→        if (variantError) {
   170→          handleError(variantError, { context: 'useSourceImageChanges', showToast: false });
   171→        } else {
   172→          (variantData || []).forEach(v => {
   173→            variantLocations[v.id] = { location: v.location, created_at: v.created_at };
   174→          });
   175→        }
   176→      }
   177→
   178→      // Build gen_id -> variant location map
   179→      const genToVariant: Record<string, { location: string | null; updated_at: Date }> = {};
   180→      (genData || []).forEach(g => {
   181→        const variant = g.primary_variant_id ? variantLocations[g.primary_variant_id] : null;
   182→        genToVariant[g.id] = {
   183→          location: variant?.location || null,
   184→          // Use generation's updated_at since that reflects when primary_variant_id changed
   185→          updated_at: new Date(g.updated_at),
   186→        };
   187→      });
   188→
   189→      // Return everything needed for comparison
   190→      return {
   191→        genToVariant, // genId -> { location, updated_at }
   192→        startGenToNext, // startGenId -> { startSlot, nextGenId }
   193→      };
   194→    },
   195→    enabled: enabled && startGenIds.length > 0,
   196→    staleTime: 0, // Always refetch on invalidation for immediate warning updates
   197→    refetchInterval: 60000, // Refetch every minute to update "recent" status
   198→  });
   199→
   200→  // Compare stored URLs with current locations
   201→  const mismatchMap = useMemo(() => {
   202→    const map = new Map<string, SourceMismatchInfo>();
   203→    if (!slotData) return map;
   204→
   205→    const { genToVariant, startGenToNext } = slotData;
   206→    if (!genToVariant || !startGenToNext) return map;
   207→
   208→    const now = Date.now();
   209→
   210→    // Helper to normalize URLs for comparison
   211→    const normalizeUrl = (url: string | null | undefined): string => {
   212→      if (!url) return '';
   213→      try {
   214→        const parsed = new URL(url);
   215→        return parsed.pathname;
   216→      } catch {
   217→        return url;
   218→      }
   219→    };
   220→
   221→    segments.forEach(seg => {
   222→      // Extract stored URLs from segment params
   223→      const { startUrl, endUrl } = extractSegmentImages(seg.params, seg.childOrder);
   224→
   225→      // Get current state by looking up where start gen is and what's next to it
   226→      const startGenInfo = seg.startGenId ? startGenToNext[seg.startGenId] : null;
   227→      const nextGenId = startGenInfo?.nextGenId;
   228→
   229→      // Get current URLs for start gen and the generation that's now next to it
   230→      const currentStartInfo = seg.startGenId ? genToVariant[seg.startGenId] : null;
   231→      const currentEndInfo = nextGenId ? genToVariant[nextGenId] : null;
   232→
   233→      const currentStartUrl = currentStartInfo?.location || null;
   234→      const currentEndUrl = currentEndInfo?.location || null;
   235→
   236→      // Compare stored URLs with current URLs
   237→      const startMismatch = startUrl && currentStartUrl
   238→        ? normalizeUrl(startUrl) !== normalizeUrl(currentStartUrl)
   239→        : false;
   240→
   241→      const endMismatch = endUrl && currentEndUrl
   242→        ? normalizeUrl(endUrl) !== normalizeUrl(currentEndUrl)
   243→        : (endUrl && !currentEndUrl); // Also mismatch if there's no next image anymore
   244→
   245→      const hasMismatch = startMismatch || endMismatch;
   246→
   247→
   248→      if (hasMismatch) {
   249→        // Find the most recent change
   250→        // For start image: use generation's updated_at (reflects variant changes)
   251→        const startChangedAt = startMismatch && currentStartInfo?.updated_at
   252→          ? currentStartInfo.updated_at
   253→          : null;
   254→
   255→        // For end image: check if it's a timeline reorder (different gen) or variant change (same gen)
   256→        let endChangedAt: Date | null = null;
   257→        if (endMismatch) {
   258→          const isReorderMismatch = nextGenId !== seg.endGenId;
   259→          if (isReorderMismatch && startGenInfo?.nextSlotUpdatedAt) {
   260→            // Timeline was reordered - use the slot's updated_at
   261→            endChangedAt = startGenInfo.nextSlotUpdatedAt;
   262→          } else if (currentEndInfo?.updated_at) {
   263→            // Same generation but different variant - use generation's updated_at
   264→            endChangedAt = currentEndInfo.updated_at;
   265→          }
   266→        }
   267→
   268→        let changedAt: Date | null = null;
   269→        if (startChangedAt && endChangedAt) {
   270→          changedAt = startChangedAt > endChangedAt ? startChangedAt : endChangedAt;
   271→        } else {
   272→          changedAt = startChangedAt || endChangedAt;
   273→        }
   274→
   275→        const isRecent = changedAt
   276→          ? (now - changedAt.getTime()) < SOURCE_CHANGE_WARNING_DURATION_MS
   277→          : false;
   278→
   279→        map.set(seg.segmentId, {
   280→          segmentId: seg.segmentId,
   281→          hasMismatch,
   282→          isRecent,
   283→          startMismatch,
   284→          endMismatch,
   285→          changedAt,
   286→        });
   287→      }
   288→    });
   289→
   290→    return map;
   291→  }, [segments, slotData]);
   292→
   293→  // Helper to check if a specific segment has a recent mismatch
   294→  const hasRecentMismatch = useMemo(() => {
   295→    return (segmentId: string): boolean => {
   296→      const info = mismatchMap.get(segmentId);
   297→      const result = info?.isRecent ?? false;
   298→      return result;
   299→    };
   300→  }, [mismatchMap]);
   301→
   302→  return {
   303→    mismatchMap,
   304→    hasRecentMismatch,
   305→    isLoading,
   306→    hasAnyMismatches: mismatchMap.size > 0,
   307→  };
   308→}
   309→

     5→const MAX_LOCAL_STORAGE_ITEM_LENGTH = 4 * 1024 * 1024; // 4MB

     7→const PERSISTENT_STATE_EVENT = 'persistentStateChange';
     8→
     9→// Check if localStorage is available (can fail in iOS Safari private mode)
    10→function isLocalStorageAvailable(): boolean {
    11→  try {
    12→    const test = '__localStorage_test__';
    13→    localStorage.setItem(test, test);
    14→    localStorage.removeItem(test);
    15→    return true;
    16→  } catch {
    17→    return false;
    18→  }
    19→}
    20→
    21→function usePersistentState<T>(key: string, defaultValue: T): [T, React.Dispatch<React.SetStateAction<T>>] {
    22→  const [state, setState] = useState<T>(() => {
    23→    // Mobile Safari in private mode can throw on localStorage access
    24→    if (!isLocalStorageAvailable()) {
    25→      return defaultValue;
    26→    }
    27→
    28→    try {
    29→      const storedValue = localStorage.getItem(key);
    30→      if (storedValue) {
    31→        return JSON.parse(storedValue) as T;
    32→      }
    33→    } catch (error) {
    34→      handleError(error, { context: 'usePersistentState', showToast: false });
    35→    }
    36→    return defaultValue;
    37→  });
    38→
    39→  // Listen for updates from other components using the same key
    40→  useEffect(() => {
    41→    function handleExternalUpdate(e: Event) {
    42→      const customEvt = e as CustomEvent<{ key: string; value: unknown }>;
    43→      if (customEvt.detail?.key === key) {
    44→        setState(customEvt.detail.value as T);
    45→      }
    46→    }
    47→
    48→    window.addEventListener(PERSISTENT_STATE_EVENT, handleExternalUpdate);
    49→    return () => window.removeEventListener(PERSISTENT_STATE_EVENT, handleExternalUpdate);
    50→  }, [key]);
    51→
    52→  useEffect(() => {
    53→    // Skip localStorage writes if not available
    54→    if (!isLocalStorageAvailable()) {
    55→      return;
    56→    }
    57→
    58→    try {
    59→      const serializedState = JSON.stringify(state);
    60→      if (serializedState.length > MAX_LOCAL_STORAGE_ITEM_LENGTH) {
    61→        toast.warning("Could not save settings locally.", {
    62→          description: "The data size exceeds the 4MB limit for local storage.",
    63→        });
    64→        return;
    65→      }
    66→      localStorage.setItem(key, serializedState);
    67→
    68→      // Broadcast change to other hook instances in the same tab
    69→      window.dispatchEvent(
    70→        new CustomEvent(PERSISTENT_STATE_EVENT, {
    71→          detail: { key, value: state },
    72→        })
    73→      );
    74→    } catch (error) {
    75→      // Different error message for mobile users
    76→      const isMobile = /iPhone|iPad|iPod|Android/i.test(navigator.userAgent);
    77→      const errorDescription = isMobile
    78→        ? "Local storage may be disabled in private browsing mode. Settings will be lost when the tab is closed."
    79→        : "There was an error writing to your browser's local storage.";
    80→
    81→      handleError(error, {
    82→        context: 'usePersistentState',
    83→        toastTitle: 'Could not save settings locally.',
    84→        toastDescription: errorDescription
    85→      });
    86→    }
    87→  }, [key, state]);
    88→
    89→  return [state, setState];
    90→}
    91→
    92→export default usePersistentState;
    93→

   213→/**
   214→ * Utility function to expand single-element arrays to match a target count
   215→ * This is commonly needed for steerable motion tasks where user provides
   216→ * one value that should be applied to all segments.
   217→ * 
   218→ * @param arr - Array to potentially expand
   219→ * @param targetCount - Target count for the array
   220→ * @returns Expanded array or original array if no expansion needed
   221→ */
   222→export function expandArrayToCount<T>(arr: T[] | undefined, targetCount: number): T[] {
   223→  if (!arr || arr.length === 0) {
   224→    return [];
   225→  }
   226→
   227→  if (arr.length === 1 && targetCount > 1) {
   228→    return Array(targetCount).fill(arr[0]);
   229→  }
   230→
   231→  // Truncate arrays that are longer than the target count
   232→  // This handles the case where images were deleted and arrays are stale
   233→  if (arr.length > targetCount) {
   234→    return arr.slice(0, targetCount);
   235→  }
   236→
   237→  return arr;
   238→}

   247→export function validateRequiredFields(params: Record<string, unknown>, requiredFields: string[]): void {

   250→    
   251→    if (value === undefined || value === null) {

   315→  if (hiresFix.hires_steps !== undefined) params.hires_steps = hiresFix.hires_steps;

   318→  if (hiresFix.lightning_lora_strength_phase_2 !== undefined) params.lightning_lora_strength_phase_2 = hiresFix.lightning_lora_strength_phase_2;

   326→ *
   327→ * - Throws if every task failed (surfaces the first error).
   328→ * - Logs individual failures when some succeed.
   329→ * - Returns the fulfilled TaskCreationResult values.
   330→ *
   331→ * @param results - The settled promise array from Promise.allSettled
   332→ * @param context - Label used in error/log messages (e.g. "BatchImageGeneration")
   333→ */
   334→export function processBatchResults(
   335→  results: PromiseSettledResult<TaskCreationResult>[],
   336→  context: string,
   337→): TaskCreationResult[] {
   338→  const successful = results.filter(r => r.status === 'fulfilled').length;
   339→  const failed = results.filter(r => r.status === 'rejected').length;
   340→
   341→  if (successful === 0) {
   342→    const firstError = results.find(r => r.status === 'rejected') as PromiseRejectedResult;
   343→    throw new Error(`All batch tasks failed: ${firstError.reason}`);
   344→  }
   345→
   346→  if (failed > 0) {
   347→    results.forEach((result, index) => {
   348→      if (result.status === 'rejected') {
   349→        handleError(result.reason, { context: `${context}:task${index + 1}`, showToast: false });
   350→      }
   351→    });
   352→  }
   353→
   354→  return results
   355→    .filter((r): r is PromiseFulfilledResult<TaskCreationResult> => r.status === 'fulfilled')
   356→    .map(r => r.value);
   357→}

    38→   * If false, the hook will skip fetching/saving settings and immediately report ready=true.
    39→   * Useful when the relevant entity (e.g. project) has not been selected yet.
    40→   */
    41→  enabled?: boolean;
    42→  /**
    43→   * Explicit defaults for fields that aren't in the tools manifest.
    44→   * Use this for non-tool callers (e.g. PromptEditorModal) to avoid
    45→   * the "no default value" warning and ensure correct reset behavior.
    46→   */
    47→  defaults?: Record<string, unknown>;
    48→}
    49→
    50→interface UsePersistentToolStateResult {
    51→  ready: boolean;
    52→  isSaving: boolean;
    53→  saveError?: Error;
    54→  hasUserInteracted: boolean;
    55→  markAsInteracted: () => void;
    56→}
    57→
    58→/**
    59→ * Hook that synchronizes existing `useState` variables with persistent tool settings.
    60→ *
    61→ * Unlike `useAutoSaveSettings` which owns its own state, this hook binds to
    62→ * pre-existing `[value, setter]` pairs -- useful when the form already manages
    63→ * its own `useState` and you want to add persistence without restructuring.
    64→ *
    65→ * Key difference from `useAutoSaveSettings`: the `markAsInteracted()` guard.
    66→ * Settings are only saved after the user explicitly interacts, preventing
    67→ * auto-initialization effects from being persisted as user choices.
    68→ *
    69→ * For new features, prefer `useAutoSaveSettings` unless you specifically need
    70→ * the bind-to-existing-useState pattern or the interaction guard.
    71→ *
    72→ * @param toolId - The tool identifier (e.g., 'image-generation', 'video-travel')
    73→ * @param context - Context for settings resolution (projectId, shotId, etc.)
    74→ * @param stateMapping - Object mapping setting keys to [value, setter] tuples
    75→ * @param options - Additional options for behavior customization
    76→ * @returns Object with ready state, saving state, and interaction tracking
    77→ *
    78→ * @see docs/structure_detail/settings_system.md for the full settings hook decision tree
    79→ *
    80→ * @example
    81→ * const { ready, isSaving, markAsInteracted } = usePersistentToolState(
    82→ *   'image-generation',
    83→ *   { projectId },
    84→ *   {
    85→ *     generationMode: [generationMode, setGenerationMode],
    86→ *     imagesPerPrompt: [imagesPerPrompt, setImagesPerPrompt],
    87→ *   }
    88→ * );
    89→ * // Call markAsInteracted() in onChange handlers to enable persistence
    90→ */
    91→export function usePersistentToolState<T extends Record<string, unknown>>(
    92→  toolId: string,
    93→  context: { projectId?: string; shotId?: string },
    94→  stateMapping: StateMapping<T>,
    95→  options: UsePersistentToolStateOptions = {}
    96→): UsePersistentToolStateResult {
    97→  const { debounceMs = 500, scope = 'project', enabled = true, defaults: explicitDefaults } = options;
    98→  
    99→  // Fast-path: if persistence is disabled, provide a noop implementation so the UI can render immediately.
   100→  if (!enabled) {
   101→    const noop = () => {};
   102→    return {
   103→      ready: true,
   104→      isSaving: false,
   105→      saveError: undefined,
   106→      hasUserInteracted: false,
   107→      markAsInteracted: noop,
   108→    } as UsePersistentToolStateResult;
   109→  }
   110→
   111→  // Obtain current settings and mutation helpers
   112→  const {
   113→    settings,
   114→    isLoading: isLoadingSettings,
   115→    update: updateSettings,
   116→    isUpdating,
   117→  } = useToolSettings<T>(toolId, { ...context, enabled });
   118→
   119→  // Track hydration and interaction state
   120→  const hasHydratedRef = useRef(false);
   121→  const saveTimeoutRef = useRef<NodeJS.Timeout | null>(null);
   122→  const userHasInteractedRef = useRef(false);
   123→  const lastSavedSettingsRef = useRef<T | null>(null);
   124→  const hydratedForEntityRef = useRef<string | null>(null);
   125→
   126→  // Public state for consumers
   127→  const [ready, setReady] = useState(false);
   128→  const [saveError, setSaveError] = useState<Error | undefined>();
   129→  const [hasUserInteracted, setHasUserInteracted] = useState(false);
   130→
   131→  // Get a unique key for the current entity (project/shot)
   132→  const entityKey = scope === 'shot' ? context.shotId : context.projectId;
   133→
   134→  // Reset hydration when entity changes
   135→  useEffect(() => {
   136→    if (entityKey !== hydratedForEntityRef.current) {
   137→      hasHydratedRef.current = false;
   138→      userHasInteractedRef.current = false;
   139→      lastSavedSettingsRef.current = null;
   140→      hydratedForEntityRef.current = entityKey || null;
   141→      setReady(false);
   142→      setHasUserInteracted(false);
   143→    }
   144→  }, [entityKey, toolId]);
   145→
   146→  // Hydrate local state from persisted settings
   147→  useEffect(() => {
   148→    if (!isLoadingSettings && !hasHydratedRef.current && entityKey) {
   149→      // Use an empty object if settings could not be fetched (e.g. first time or API failure)
   150→      const effectiveSettings: Partial<T> = (settings as Partial<T>) || {};
   151→      
   152→      // Get defaults for this tool to reset undefined values
   153→      const toolDefaults = explicitDefaults || toolsManifest.find(t => t.id === toolId)?.defaults || {};
   154→      
   155→      hasHydratedRef.current = true;
   156→      userHasInteractedRef.current = false;
   157→      
   158→      // Apply each setting to its corresponding setter
   159→      // CRITICAL FIX: Always reset values when switching projects to prevent stale state
   160→      Object.entries(stateMapping).forEach(([key, [currentValue, setter]]) => {
   161→        if (effectiveSettings[key as keyof T] !== undefined) {
   162→          // Value exists in DB - use it
   163→          setter(effectiveSettings[key as keyof T] as T[keyof T]);
   164→        } else if (toolDefaults[key as keyof typeof toolDefaults] !== undefined) {
   165→          // Value missing in DB but has a default - reset to default
   166→          setter(toolDefaults[key as keyof typeof toolDefaults] as T[keyof T]);
   167→        } else {
   168→          // SAFETY NET: No value in DB and no default - infer empty value from current type
   169→          // This prevents stale state but ideally all fields should have explicit defaults
   170→          const emptyValue = inferEmptyValue(currentValue);
   171→          
   172→          // Warn in development if we're using inference (indicates missing default)
   173→          if (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development') {
   174→            console.warn(
   175→              `[usePersistentToolState] Field "${key}" in tool "${toolId}" has no default value. ` +
   176→              `Inferring empty value (${JSON.stringify(emptyValue)}). ` +
   177→              `Consider adding explicit default in settings.ts`
   178→            );
   179→          }
   180→          
   181→          setter(emptyValue as T[keyof T]);
   182→        }
   183→      });
   184→
   185→      // Mark as ready after hydration
   186→      setReady(true);
   187→    }
   188→  }, [settings, isLoadingSettings, stateMapping, entityKey, toolId]);
   189→
   190→  // Collect current state values from the mapping
   191→  const getCurrentState = useCallback((): T => {
   192→    const currentState: Record<string, unknown> = {};
   193→    Object.entries(stateMapping).forEach(([key, [value]]) => {
   194→      currentState[key] = value;
   195→    });
   196→    return currentState as T;
   197→  }, [stateMapping]);
   198→
   199→  // Function to mark that user has interacted
   200→  const markAsInteracted = useCallback(() => {
   201→    userHasInteractedRef.current = true;
   202→    setHasUserInteracted(true);
   203→  }, []);
   204→
   205→  // Save settings with debouncing and deep comparison
   206→  useEffect(() => {
   207→    if (!entityKey || !settings || !hasHydratedRef.current || !userHasInteractedRef.current) {
   208→      return;
   209→    }
   210→
   211→    // Clear any pending save
   212→    if (saveTimeoutRef.current) {
   213→      clearTimeout(saveTimeoutRef.current);
   214→    }
   215→
   216→    // Debounce the save
   217→    saveTimeoutRef.current = setTimeout(async () => {
   218→      const currentState = getCurrentState();
   219→      
   220→      // Check if we just saved these exact settings
   221→      if (lastSavedSettingsRef.current && 
   222→          deepEqual(sanitizeSettings(currentState), sanitizeSettings(lastSavedSettingsRef.current))) {
   223→        return;
   224→      }
   225→
   226→      // Check if settings actually changed from what's in the database
   227→      if (!isUpdating && !deepEqual(sanitizeSettings(currentState), sanitizeSettings(settings))) {
   228→        try {
   229→          lastSavedSettingsRef.current = currentState;
   230→          await updateSettings(scope, currentState);
   231→          setSaveError(undefined);
   232→        } catch (error) {
   233→          handleError(error, { context: 'usePersistentToolState', showToast: false });
   234→          setSaveError(error as Error);
   235→        }
   236→      }
   237→    }, Math.min(debounceMs, 100)); // Cap debounce at 100ms for performance
   238→
   239→    // Cleanup timeout on unmount or dependencies change
   240→    return () => {
   241→      if (saveTimeoutRef.current) {
   242→        clearTimeout(saveTimeoutRef.current);
   243→      }
   244→    };
   245→  }, [
   246→    entityKey,
   247→    settings,
   248→    getCurrentState,
   249→    updateSettings,
   250→    isUpdating,
   251→    scope,
   252→    debounceMs,
   253→    toolId,
   254→    // Include all state values to trigger saves on change
   255→    ...Object.entries(stateMapping).map(([_, [value]]) => value)
   256→  ]);
   257→
   258→  return {
   259→    ready,
   260→    isSaving: isUpdating,
   261→    saveError,
   262→    hasUserInteracted,
   263→    markAsInteracted
   264→  };
   265→}

1→import { useMemo } from 'react';
     2→import { isValid } from 'date-fns';
     3→import { useTimestampUpdater } from './useTimestampUpdater';
     4→
     5→/**
     6→ * Hook for formatting "In Progress" task timestamps based on generation_started_at
     7→ * Shows "Processing: <1 min" for <1 min, "Processing: For X mins/hrs" for longer durations
     8→ */
     9→
    10→interface UseProcessingTimestampOptions {
    11→  /** Date when generation started */
    12→  generationStartedAt?: string | Date | null;
    13→  /** Disable automatic updates */
    14→  disabled?: boolean;
    15→}
    16→
    17→interface UseCompletedTimestampOptions {
    18→  /** Date when generation was processed/completed */
    19→  generationProcessedAt?: string | Date | null;
    20→  /** Disable automatic updates */
    21→  disabled?: boolean;
    22→}
    23→
    24→/**
    25→ * Custom formatting for processing duration
    26→ */
    27→const formatProcessingDuration = (startDate: Date): string => {
    28→  const now = Date.now();
    29→  const startTime = startDate.getTime();
    30→  const diffMs = now - startTime;
    31→  const diffMinutes = Math.floor(diffMs / (1000 * 60));
    32→  
    33→  // Less than 1 minute
    34→  if (diffMinutes < 1) {
    35→    return 'Processing for <1 min';
    36→  }
    37→  
    38→  // 1-59 minutes
    39→  if (diffMinutes < 60) {
    40→    return `Processing for ${diffMinutes} min${diffMinutes === 1 ? '' : 's'}`;
    41→  }
    42→  
    43→  // Hours and minutes
    44→  const hours = Math.floor(diffMinutes / 60);
    45→  const remainingMinutes = diffMinutes % 60;
    46→  
    47→  if (remainingMinutes === 0) {
    48→    return `Processing for ${hours} hr${hours === 1 ? '' : 's'}`;
    49→  } else {
    50→    return `Processing for ${hours} hr${hours === 1 ? '' : 's'}, ${remainingMinutes} min${remainingMinutes === 1 ? '' : 's'}`;
    51→  }
    52→};
    53→
    54→/**
    55→ * Custom formatting for completed task - shows how long ago it was completed
    56→ */
    57→const formatCompletedTime = (completedDate: Date): string => {
    58→  const now = Date.now();
    59→  const completedTime = completedDate.getTime();
    60→  const diffMs = now - completedTime;
    61→  const diffMinutes = Math.floor(diffMs / (1000 * 60));
    62→  
    63→  // Less than 1 minute
    64→  if (diffMinutes < 1) {
    65→    return 'Completed <1 min ago';
    66→  }
    67→  
    68→  // 1-59 minutes
    69→  if (diffMinutes < 60) {
    70→    return `Completed ${diffMinutes} min${diffMinutes === 1 ? '' : 's'} ago`;
    71→  }
    72→  
    73→  // Less than 24 hours - show hours and minutes
    74→  if (diffMinutes < 24 * 60) {
    75→    const hours = Math.floor(diffMinutes / 60);
    76→    const remainingMinutes = diffMinutes % 60;
    77→    
    78→    if (remainingMinutes === 0) {
    79→      return `Completed ${hours} hr${hours === 1 ? '' : 's'} ago`;
    80→    } else {
    81→      return `Completed ${hours} hr${hours === 1 ? '' : 's'}, ${remainingMinutes} min${remainingMinutes === 1 ? '' : 's'} ago`;
    82→    }
    83→  }
    84→  
    85→  // Days and hours
    86→  const days = Math.floor(diffMinutes / (24 * 60));
    87→  const remainingHours = Math.floor((diffMinutes % (24 * 60)) / 60);
    88→  
    89→  if (remainingHours === 0) {
    90→    return `Completed ${days} day${days === 1 ? '' : 's'} ago`;
    91→  } else {
    92→    return `Completed ${days} day${days === 1 ? '' : 's'}, ${remainingHours} hr${remainingHours === 1 ? '' : 's'} ago`;
    93→  }
    94→};
    95→
    96→/**
    97→ * Shared hook for live-updating timestamp formatting.
    98→ * Parses a date, sets up live update triggers, and formats using the provided formatter.
    99→ */
   100→function useLiveTimestamp(
   101→  dateInput: string | Date | null | undefined,
   102→  disabled: boolean,
   103→  formatter: (date: Date) => string,
   104→): string | null {
   105→  const parsedDate = useMemo(() => {
   106→    if (!dateInput) return null;
   107→    const parsed = typeof dateInput === 'string' ? new Date(dateInput) : dateInput;
   108→    return isValid(parsed) ? parsed : null;
   109→  }, [dateInput]);
   110→
   111→  const { updateTrigger } = useTimestampUpdater({
   112→    date: parsedDate,
   113→    disabled,
   114→    isVisible: true,
   115→  });
   116→
   117→  const formattedTime = useMemo(() => {
   118→    if (!parsedDate) return null;
   119→    return formatter(parsedDate);
   120→  }, [parsedDate?.getTime(), updateTrigger]);
   121→
   122→  return formattedTime;
   123→}
   124→
   125→/**
   126→ * Hook that returns a formatted, live-updating processing timestamp string
   127→ *
   128→ * @example
   129→ * const processingTime = useProcessingTimestamp({ generationStartedAt: task.generationStartedAt });
   130→ * return <span>{processingTime}</span>;
   131→ */
   132→export function useProcessingTimestamp({
   133→  generationStartedAt,
   134→  disabled = false
   135→}: UseProcessingTimestampOptions = {}) {
   136→  return useLiveTimestamp(generationStartedAt, disabled, formatProcessingDuration);

   138→
   139→/**

   145→ * });

   148→export function useCompletedTimestamp({
   149→  generationProcessedAt,
   150→  disabled = false
   151→}: UseCompletedTimestampOptions = {}) {

   153→}

1→import { useQuery, useMutation, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';
     2→import { useRef, useEffect, useCallback } from 'react';
     3→import { useProject } from '@/shared/contexts/ProjectContext';
     4→import { handleError } from '@/shared/lib/errorHandler';
     5→import { queryKeys } from '@/shared/lib/queryKeys';
     6→import { supabase } from '@/integrations/supabase/client';
     7→import { QUERY_PRESETS, STANDARD_RETRY_DELAY } from '@/shared/lib/queryDefaults';
     8→import {
     9→  enqueueSettingsWrite,
    10→  setSettingsWriteFunction,
    11→  type QueuedWrite
    12→} from '@/shared/lib/settingsWriteQueue';
    13→import { deepMerge } from '@/shared/lib/deepEqual';
    14→import { isCancellationError } from '@/shared/lib/errorUtils';
    15→import {
    16→  fetchToolSettingsSupabase,
    17→  getUserWithTimeout,
    18→  type SettingsFetchResult,
    19→} from '@/shared/lib/toolSettingsService';
    20→
    21→export type SettingsScope = 'user' | 'project' | 'shot';
    22→
    23→interface UpdateToolSettingsParams {
    24→  scope: SettingsScope;
    25→  id: string;
    26→  toolId: string;
    27→  patch: unknown;
    28→}
    29→
    30→/**
    31→ * Raw write function - performs the actual DB update.
    32→ * Used internally by the settings write queue.
    33→ *
    34→ * @internal Use updateToolSettingsSupabase (queued) for normal usage
    35→ */
    36→async function rawUpdateToolSettings(write: QueuedWrite): Promise<Record<string, unknown>> {
    37→  const { scope, entityId: id, toolId, patch } = write;
    38→
    39→  try {
    40→    let tableName: string;
    41→    switch (scope) {
    42→      case 'user':
    43→        tableName = 'users';
    44→        break;
    45→      case 'project':
    46→        tableName = 'projects';
    47→        break;
    48→      case 'shot':
    49→        tableName = 'shots';
    50→        break;
    51→      default:
    52→        throw new Error(`Invalid scope: ${scope}`);
    53→    }
    54→
    55→    // For patch updates, we need to fetch current settings to merge
    56→    // This is necessary because the caller provides a partial update
    57→    // TODO: In the future, consider passing full settings to eliminate this fetch
    58→    const { data: currentEntity, error: fetchError } = await supabase
    59→      .from(tableName)
    60→      .select('settings')
    61→      .eq('id', id)
    62→      .single();
    63→
    64→    if (fetchError) {
    65→      // Check for network exhaustion - include the error type in the message for downstream handling
    66→      const errorMessage = fetchError.message || '';
    67→      if (errorMessage.includes('ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES') ||
    68→          errorMessage.includes('Failed to fetch') ||
    69→          fetchError.code === 'ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES') {
    70→        throw new Error(`Network exhaustion: ${errorMessage}`);
    71→      }
    72→      throw new Error(`Failed to fetch current ${scope} settings: ${errorMessage}`);
    73→    }
    74→
    75→    // Merge patch with current tool settings
    76→    const currentSettings = (currentEntity?.settings as Record<string, unknown>) ?? {};
    77→    const currentToolSettings = (currentSettings[toolId] as Record<string, unknown>) ?? {};
    78→    const updatedToolSettings = deepMerge({}, currentToolSettings, patch);
    79→
    80→    // Use atomic PostgreSQL function to update settings
    81→    // This is much faster than update() because it happens in a single DB operation
    82→    const { error: rpcError } = await supabase.rpc('update_tool_settings_atomic', {
    83→      p_table_name: tableName,
    84→      p_id: id,
    85→      p_tool_id: toolId,
    86→      p_settings: updatedToolSettings
    87→    });
    88→
    89→    if (rpcError) {
    90→      throw new Error(`Failed to update ${scope} settings: ${rpcError.message}`);
    91→    }
    92→
    93→    // CRITICAL: Return the full merged settings, not just the patch
    94→    // This ensures the cache gets the exact same data that was saved to the DB
    95→    // Prevents data loss when cache is stale (e.g., multiple tabs, concurrent edits)
    96→    return updatedToolSettings;
    97→
    98→  } catch (error: unknown) {
    99→    // Handle abort errors silently to reduce noise during task cancellation
   100→    if (isCancellationError(error)) {

   102→      throw new Error('Request was cancelled');

   113→/**
   114→ * Update tool settings using the global write queue.

   116→ * This is the main entry point for settings updates. It:
   117→ * - Debounces rapid updates (300ms window)
   118→ * - Coalesces multiple writes to the same target

   123→ * @returns The full merged settings after update

   125→export function updateToolSettingsSupabase(
   126→  params: UpdateToolSettingsParams,
   127→  _signal?: AbortSignal,
   128→  mode: 'debounced' | 'immediate' = 'debounced'

   130→  const { scope, id, toolId, patch } = params;
   131→

   133→    scope,
   134→    entityId: id,
   135→    toolId,
   136→    patch: patch as Record<string, unknown>,

   178→    settings: { ...prevSettings, ...updates } as T,
   179→    hasShotSettings: wrapper ? ((prev as SettingsFetchResult).hasShotSettings ?? false) : false

   183→// Type overloads
   184→export function useToolSettings<T>(toolId: string, context?: { projectId?: string; shotId?: string; enabled?: boolean }): {

   243→      try {
   244→        const result = await fetchToolSettingsSupabase(toolId, { projectId, shotId }, signal);

   256→    // Use static preset - tool settings rarely change, mutation invalidates on save
   257→    ...QUERY_PRESETS.static,
   258→    staleTime: 10 * 60 * 1000, // Override: 10 minutes (longer than static default)
   259→    // Mobile-specific optimizations
   260→    retry: (failureCount, error) => {
   261→      // Don't retry auth errors, cancelled requests, or abort errors
   262→      if (error?.message?.includes('Authentication required') ||
   263→          error?.message?.includes('Request was cancelled') ||

   312→          idForScope = projectId;
   313→        } else if (scope === 'shot') {
   314→          idForScope = shotId;

   324→      const fullMergedSettings = await updateToolSettingsSupabase({

   341→      // CRITICAL: The cache stores { settings: T, hasShotSettings: boolean } shape
   342→      queryClient.setQueryData(

   344→        (oldData: unknown) => {

   367→      if (error?.name === 'AbortError' ||

   375→      const isNetworkExhaustion = error?.message?.includes('ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES') ||

    21→export function useProjectSelection({

    32→  const [selectedProjectId, setSelectedProjectIdState] = useState<string | null>(() => {
    33→    try {

    45→    return null;
    46→  });

    60→

    63→  const applyCrossDeviceSync = useCallback((projects: Project[]) => {

    93→export function useVideoScrubbing(
    94→  options: UseVideoScrubbingOptions = {}
    95→): UseVideoScrubbingReturn {
    96→  const {
    97→    enabled = true,
    98→    playOnStopScrubbing = true,
    99→    playDelay = 400,
   100→    resetOnLeave = true,
   101→    onProgressChange,
   102→    onHoverStart,

   123→  const [isPlaying, setIsPlaying] = useState(false);
   124→  // Track when video element changes to re-run effects

   127→  // Get the active video element (external or internal ref)

   134→    externalVideoRef.current = video;
   135→    // Increment version to trigger re-run of event listener effects
   136→    setVideoElementVersion(v => v + 1);
   137→    if (video && video.duration && Number.isFinite(video.duration)) {
   138→      setDurationState(video.duration);
   139→    }
   140→  }, []);
   141→
   142→  // Set duration manually
   143→  const setDuration = useCallback((dur: number) => {
   144→    if (Number.isFinite(dur) && dur > 0) {
   145→      setDurationState(dur);
   146→    }
   147→  }, []);
   148→
   149→  // Reset state
   150→  const reset = useCallback(() => {
   151→    setProgress(0);
   152→    setCurrentTime(0);
   153→    setScrubberPosition(null);
   154→    setScrubberVisible(true);
   155→    setIsPlaying(false);
   156→    lastMouseXRef.current = null;
   157→
   158→    if (mouseMoveTimeoutRef.current) {

   161→    }
   162→  }, []);
   163→
   164→  // Seek to progress
   165→  const seekToProgress = useCallback((prog: number) => {
   166→    const video = getVideo();
   167→    const dur = duration || (video?.duration ?? 0);
   168→
   169→    if (!Number.isFinite(dur) || dur <= 0) return;
   170→
   171→    const clampedProgress = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, prog));
   172→    const targetTime = clampedProgress * dur;
   173→
   174→    if (Number.isFinite(targetTime)) {
   175→      if (video) {
   176→        video.currentTime = targetTime;
   177→      }
   178→      setProgress(clampedProgress);
   179→      setCurrentTime(targetTime);
   180→      onProgressChange?.(clampedProgress, targetTime);
   181→    }
   182→  }, [duration, getVideo, onProgressChange]);
   183→
   184→  // Play
   185→  const play = useCallback(() => {
   186→    const video = getVideo();
   187→    if (video) {
   188→      video.play().catch(() => {
   189→        // Ignore autoplay errors
   190→      });
   191→    }
   192→  }, [getVideo]);
   193→
   194→  // Pause
   195→  const pause = useCallback(() => {
   196→    const video = getVideo();
   197→    if (video) {
   198→      video.pause();
   199→    }
   200→  }, [getVideo]);

   202→  // Handle mouse move (scrubbing)

   204→    if (!enabled) return;
   205→
   206→    const container = containerRef.current;
   207→    if (!container) return;
   208→
   209→    const rect = container.getBoundingClientRect();
   210→    const mouseX = e.clientX - rect.left;
   211→    lastMouseXRef.current = mouseX;
   212→
   213→    const prog = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, mouseX / rect.width));
   214→
   215→    // Always show scrubber position (percentage-based) even if duration isn't ready
   216→    setScrubberPosition(prog * 100);
   217→    setScrubberVisible(true);

   220→    const video = getVideo();

   268→  // Handle mouse enter

   271→
   272→    isHoveringRef.current = true;
   273→    setIsHovering(true);
   274→    onHoverStart?.();
   275→
   276→    const video = getVideo();
   277→    if (video) {
   278→      // Prime video loading if needed
   279→      if (video.readyState === 0) {
   280→        video.load();
   281→      }
   282→      video.pause();
   283→      setIsPlaying(false);
   284→    }
   285→  }, [enabled, getVideo, onHoverStart]);
   286→
   287→  // Handle mouse leave
   288→  const handleMouseLeave = useCallback(() => {
   289→    if (!enabled) return;
   290→
   291→    isHoveringRef.current = false;
   292→    setIsHovering(false);
   293→    lastMouseXRef.current = null;
   294→    setScrubberPosition(null);
   295→    setScrubberVisible(true);
   296→
   297→    if (mouseMoveTimeoutRef.current) {
   298→      clearTimeout(mouseMoveTimeoutRef.current);
   299→      mouseMoveTimeoutRef.current = null;
   300→    }
   301→
   302→    const video = getVideo();
   303→    if (video) {
   304→      video.pause();
   305→      if (resetOnLeave) {
   306→        video.currentTime = 0;
   307→        setProgress(0);
   308→        setCurrentTime(0);
   309→      }
   310→      setIsPlaying(false);
   311→    }
   312→
   313→    onHoverEnd?.();
   314→    onPlayPause?.();
   315→  }, [enabled, resetOnLeave, getVideo, onHoverEnd, onPlayPause]);
   316→
   317→  // Handle video metadata loaded
   318→  const handleLoadedMetadata = useCallback(() => {
   319→    const video = getVideo();

   325→    setDurationState(newDuration);

   327→    // Recalculate scrubber if user was hovering while metadata loaded
   328→    if (isHoveringRef.current && lastMouseXRef.current !== null && containerRef.current) {
   329→      const rect = containerRef.current.getBoundingClientRect();
   330→      const prog = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, lastMouseXRef.current / rect.width));
   331→      const targetTime = prog * newDuration;

   333→      if (Number.isFinite(targetTime)) {
   334→        setScrubberPosition(prog * 100);
   335→        setScrubberVisible(true);
   336→        setProgress(prog);
   337→        setCurrentTime(targetTime);

   339→        video.pause();
   340→        video.currentTime = targetTime;

   353→      onPlayStart?.();
   354→    };
   355→
   356→    const handlePause = () => {
   357→      setIsPlaying(false);
   358→      onPlayPause?.();
   359→    };
   360→
   361→    const handleDurationChange = () => {
   362→      if (video.duration && Number.isFinite(video.duration)) {

   364→      }
   365→    };
   366→
   367→    // Update progress/currentTime during playback
   368→    const handleTimeUpdate = () => {
   369→      const dur = video.duration;
   370→      if (!Number.isFinite(dur) || dur <= 0) return;

   372→      const time = video.currentTime;
   373→      const prog = time / dur;
   374→

   376→      setProgress(prog);

1→import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
     2→import { usePrefetchToolSettings } from '@/shared/hooks/usePrefetchToolSettings';
     3→import { useMobileTimeoutFallback } from '@/shared/hooks/useMobileTimeoutFallback';
     4→import { Project } from '@/types/project';
     5→
     6→interface UseProjectDefaultsOptions {
     7→  userId: string | null;
     8→  selectedProjectId: string | null;
     9→  isLoadingProjects: boolean;
    10→  isLoadingPreferences: boolean;
    11→  projects: Project[];
    12→  fetchProjects: () => Promise<void>;
    13→  applyCrossDeviceSync: (projects: Project[]) => void;
    14→}
    15→
    16→/**
    17→ * Orchestrates project-related side effects:
    18→ * - Triggers fetchProjects when userId is available
    19→ * - Cross-device sync when preferences + projects are both loaded
    20→ * - Prefetches tool settings for the selected project
    21→ * - Mobile timeout fallback for stalled fetches
    22→ */
    23→export function useProjectDefaults({
    24→  userId,
    25→  selectedProjectId,
    26→  isLoadingProjects,
    27→  isLoadingPreferences,
    28→  projects,
    29→  fetchProjects,
    30→  applyCrossDeviceSync,
    31→}: UseProjectDefaultsOptions) {
    32→  // [PROFILING] Track fetch invocations to detect triple-fetch issue
    33→  const fetchInvocationCountRef = useRef(0);
    34→  const lastFetchReasonRef = useRef<string>('');
    35→
    36→  // Prefetch all tool settings for the currently selected project
    37→  usePrefetchToolSettings(selectedProjectId);
    38→
    39→  // Trigger initial project fetch when userId becomes available
    40→  useEffect(() => {
    41→    if (userId) {
    42→      fetchInvocationCountRef.current += 1;
    43→      const reason = `userId=${!!userId}, isLoadingPreferences=${isLoadingPreferences}`;
    44→      lastFetchReasonRef.current = reason;
    45→
    46→      fetchProjects();
    47→    }
    48→  }, [userId, isLoadingPreferences, fetchProjects]);
    49→
    50→  // Cross-device sync: apply server preferences once projects + prefs are loaded
    51→  useEffect(() => {
    52→    if (projects.length > 0) {
    53→      applyCrossDeviceSync(projects);
    54→    }
    55→  }, [projects, applyCrossDeviceSync]);
    56→
    57→  // [MobileStallFix] Fallback recovery: retry fetch if projects loading stalls
    58→  useMobileTimeoutFallback({
    59→    isLoading: isLoadingProjects,
    60→    onTimeout: fetchProjects,
    61→    mobileTimeoutMs: 15000,
    62→    desktopTimeoutMs: 10000,
    63→    enabled: !!userId,
    64→  });
    65→}
    66→

   105→      return false;
   106→    }
   107→
   108→    try {
   109→      // Set canvas size to match video
   110→      if (canvas.width !== video.videoWidth || canvas.height !== video.videoHeight) {
   111→        canvas.width = video.videoWidth;
   112→        canvas.height = video.videoHeight;
   113→      }
   114→
   115→      ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
   116→      ctx.drawImage(video, 0, 0);
   117→
   118→      // Check if draw succeeded
   119→      if (isCanvasBlank(canvas)) {
   120→        seekingRef.current = false;
   121→        return false;
   122→      }
   123→
   124→      lastDrawnFrameRef.current = frame;
   125→      return true;
   126→    } catch (e) {
   127→      seekingRef.current = false;
   128→      return false;
   129→    }
   130→  }, [isCanvasBlank]);
   131→
   132→  // Ensure video is ready for seeking
   133→  const ensureVideoReady = useCallback(async (video: HTMLVideoElement): Promise<boolean> => {
   134→    if (video.readyState >= 2) {
   135→      return true;
   136→    }
   137→
   138→    return new Promise<boolean>((resolve) => {
   139→      const handleReady = () => {
   140→        video.removeEventListener('canplay', handleReady);
   141→        video.removeEventListener('loadeddata', handleReady);
   142→        resolve(true);
   143→      };
   144→
   145→      video.addEventListener('canplay', handleReady);
   146→      video.addEventListener('loadeddata', handleReady);
   147→
   148→      setTimeout(() => {
   149→        video.removeEventListener('canplay', handleReady);
   150→        video.removeEventListener('loadeddata', handleReady);
   151→        resolve(video.readyState >= 1);
   152→      }, 1000);
   153→
   154→      if (video.readyState < 2) video.load();
   155→    });
   156→  }, []);
   157→
   158→  // Seek to frame and draw
   159→  const seekToFrameCountRef = useRef(0);
   160→  const seekToFrame = useCallback(async (frame: number) => {
   161→    const video = videoRef.current;
   162→
   163→    const now = Date.now();
   164→    const timeSinceLastSeek = now - lastSeekTimeRef.current;
   165→
   166→    // Throttle seeks
   167→    if (seekingRef.current || timeSinceLastSeek < seekThrottleMs) {
   168→      pendingSeekRef.current = frame;
   169→
   170→      if (!seekingRef.current) {
   171→        setTimeout(() => {
   172→          const pending = pendingSeekRef.current;
   173→          if (pending !== null) {
   174→            pendingSeekRef.current = null;
   175→            seekToFrame(pending);
   176→          }
   177→        }, seekThrottleMs - timeSinceLastSeek);
   178→      }
   179→      return;
   180→    }
   181→
   182→    seekingRef.current = true;
   183→    lastSeekTimeRef.current = now;
   184→
   185→    try {
   186→      const ready = await ensureVideoReady(video);
   187→      if (!ready) {
   188→        return;
   189→      }
   190→
   191→      const timeInSeconds = frame / frameRate;
   192→
   193→      seekToFrameCountRef.current++;
   194→
   195→      // Skip seek if already at this frame
   196→      if (Math.abs(video.currentTime - timeInSeconds) < 0.05) {
   197→        drawVideoFrame(video, frame);
   198→        return;
   199→      }
   200→
   201→      video.currentTime = timeInSeconds;
   202→
   203→      await new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
   204→        const handleSeeked = () => {
   205→          video.removeEventListener('seeked', handleSeeked);
   206→          drawVideoFrame(video, frame);
   207→          resolve();
   208→        };
   209→
   210→        video.addEventListener('seeked', handleSeeked, { once: true });
   211→
   212→        setTimeout(() => {
   213→          video.removeEventListener('seeked', handleSeeked);
   214→          drawVideoFrame(video, frame);
   215→          resolve();
   216→        }, 500);
   217→      });
   218→    } finally {
   219→      seekingRef.current = false;
   220→
   221→      // Process pending seek
   222→      const pendingFrame = pendingSeekRef.current;
   223→      if (pendingFrame !== null && pendingFrame !== frame) {
   224→        pendingSeekRef.current = null;
   225→        seekToFrame(pendingFrame);
   226→      }
   227→    }
   228→  }, [enabled, frameRate, seekThrottleMs, ensureVideoReady, drawVideoFrame]);
   229→
   230→  const handleMouseEnter = useCallback(() => {
   231→    setIsHovering(true);
   232→  }, []);
   233→
   234→  const handleMouseLeave = useCallback(() => {
   235→    setIsHovering(false);
   236→  }, []);
   237→
   238→  const updateHoverPosition = useCallback((x: number, y: number, frame?: number) => {
   239→    setHoverPosition({ x, y });
   240→    if (frame !== undefined && frame !== currentFrame) {
   241→      setCurrentFrame(frame);
   242→      seekToFrame(frame);
   243→    }
   244→  }, [currentFrame, seekToFrame]);
   245→
   246→  const reset = useCallback(() => {
   247→    seekingRef.current = false;
   248→    pendingSeekRef.current = null;
   249→    lastSeekTimeRef.current = 0;
   250→    setIsHovering(false);
   251→    setCurrentFrame(-1);
   252→  }, []);
   253→
   254→  // Track video ready state
   255→  useEffect(() => {
   256→    const video = videoRef.current;
   257→    if (!video) {
   258→      return;
   259→    }
   260→
   261→    const checkReady = () => {
   262→      const ready = video.readyState >= 2;
   263→      setIsVideoReady(ready);
   264→    };
   265→
   266→    video.addEventListener('canplay', checkReady);
   267→    video.addEventListener('loadeddata', checkReady);
   268→    checkReady();
   269→
   270→    return () => {
   271→      video.removeEventListener('canplay', checkReady);
   272→      video.removeEventListener('loadeddata', checkReady);
   273→    };
   274→  }, [videoUrl]);
   275→
   276→  return {
   277→    canvasRef,
   278→    videoRef,
   279→    currentFrame,
   280→    isVideoReady,
   281→    isHovering,
   282→    hoverPosition,
   283→    seekToFrame,
   284→    handleMouseEnter,
   285→    handleMouseLeave,
   286→    updateHoverPosition,
   287→    reset,
   288→  };
   289→}

1→import { useState, useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
     2→
     3→interface UseScrollFadeOptions {
     4→  /** Whether the modal is open (to trigger re-checks) */
     5→  isOpen?: boolean;
     6→  /** Threshold in pixels from bottom to consider "scrolled to bottom" */
     7→  bottomThreshold?: number;
     8→  /** Whether to enable debug logging */
     9→  debug?: boolean;
    10→  /** Show fade immediately when opened, then adjust based on content */
    11→  preloadFade?: boolean;
    12→}
    13→
    14→interface UseScrollFadeReturn {
    15→  /** Whether to show the fade overlay */
    16→  showFade: boolean;
    17→  /** Ref to attach to the scrollable container */
    18→  scrollRef: React.RefObject<HTMLDivElement>;
    19→}
    20→
    21→/**
    22→ * Hook for smart scroll-aware fade effect that appears above footer borders
    23→ * Only shows when content is scrollable and user hasn't reached the bottom
    24→ */
    25→export const useScrollFade = ({
    26→  isOpen = true,
    27→  bottomThreshold = 5,
    28→  debug = false,
    29→  preloadFade = false
    30→}: UseScrollFadeOptions = {}): UseScrollFadeReturn => {
    31→  const [showFade, setShowFade] = useState(preloadFade && isOpen);
    32→  const scrollRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
    33→
    34→  useEffect(() => {
    35→    // If preloadFade is enabled, show fade immediately when opening
    36→    if (preloadFade && isOpen) {
    37→      setShowFade(true);
    38→    }
    39→
    40→    // Reduced delay for faster response, but still ensure DOM is ready
    41→    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
    42→      const container = scrollRef.current;
    43→      if (!container) {
    44→        return;
    45→      }
    46→
    47→    const checkScroll = () => {
    48→      const { scrollTop, scrollHeight, clientHeight } = container;
    49→      const isScrolledToBottom = scrollTop + clientHeight >= scrollHeight - bottomThreshold;
    50→      const hasScrollableContent = scrollHeight > clientHeight;
    51→      
    52→      // Only show fade when:
    53→      // 1. Content is scrollable (overflows container)
    54→      // 2. User hasn't reached the bottom
    55→      const shouldShowFade = hasScrollableContent && !isScrolledToBottom;
    56→      
    57→      setShowFade(shouldShowFade);
    58→    };
    59→
    60→    // Initial check
    61→    checkScroll();
    62→
    63→    // Check on scroll
    64→    container.addEventListener('scroll', checkScroll, { passive: true });
    65→    
    66→    // Check when container size changes
    67→    const resizeObserver = new ResizeObserver(() => {
    68→      // Use setTimeout to ensure layout is complete
    69→      setTimeout(checkScroll, 0);
    70→    });
    71→    resizeObserver.observe(container);
    72→    
    73→    // Check when content changes (dynamic loading, etc.)
    74→    const mutationObserver = new MutationObserver(() => {
    75→      setTimeout(checkScroll, 0);
    76→    });
    77→    mutationObserver.observe(container, {
    78→      childList: true,
    79→      subtree: true,
    80→      characterData: true,
    81→      attributes: false
    82→    });
    83→
    84→      return () => {
    85→        container.removeEventListener('scroll', checkScroll);
    86→        resizeObserver.disconnect();
    87→        mutationObserver.disconnect();
    88→      };
    89→    }, 50); // Reduced delay from 100ms to 50ms for faster response
    90→
    91→    return () => {
    92→      clearTimeout(timer);
    93→    };
    94→  }, [isOpen, bottomThreshold, debug, preloadFade]);
    95→
    96→
    97→  return {
    98→    showFade,
    99→    scrollRef
   100→  };
   101→};
   102→

   144→function useDeleteFromTable(table: 'generations' | 'generation_variants', entityLabel: string) {
   145→  return useMutation({
