     6→
     7→interface ShotNavigationOptions {
     8→  /** Whether to scroll to top after navigation */
     9→  scrollToTop?: boolean;
    10→  /** Whether to close mobile panes after navigation */
    11→  closeMobilePanes?: boolean;
    12→  /** Whether to replace the current history entry instead of pushing */
    13→  replace?: boolean;
    14→  /** Custom scroll behavior */
    15→  scrollBehavior?: 'auto' | 'smooth';
    16→  /** Delay before scrolling (useful for waiting for navigation to complete) */
    17→  scrollDelay?: number;
    18→  /** Whether this shot was just created (show loading instead of "not found" while cache syncs) */
    19→  isNewlyCreated?: boolean;
    20→}
    21→
    22→interface ShotNavigationResult {
    23→  /** Navigate to a specific shot */
    24→  navigateToShot: (shot: Shot, options?: ShotNavigationOptions) => void;
    25→  /** Navigate to the shot editor without a specific shot (shows shot list) */
    26→  navigateToShotEditor: (options?: ShotNavigationOptions) => void;
    27→  /** Navigate to the next shot in a list */
    28→  navigateToNextShot: (shots: Shot[], currentShot: Shot, options?: ShotNavigationOptions) => boolean;
    29→  /** Navigate to the previous shot in a list */
    30→  navigateToPreviousShot: (shots: Shot[], currentShot: Shot, options?: ShotNavigationOptions) => boolean;
    31→}
    32→
    33→export const useShotNavigation = (): ShotNavigationResult => {
    34→  const navigate = useNavigate();
    35→  const { setCurrentShotId } = useCurrentShot();
    36→  const isMobile = useIsMobile();
    37→
    38→  const defaultOptions: Required<ShotNavigationOptions> = {
    39→    scrollToTop: true,
    40→    closeMobilePanes: true,
    41→    replace: false,
    42→    scrollBehavior: 'smooth',
    43→    scrollDelay: 200, // Increased to 200ms to ensure DOM has updated
    44→    isNewlyCreated: false,
    45→  };
    46→
    47→  // If we want an "already at top" feel, scroll BEFORE navigation.
    48→  // Only do this for non-animated (auto) scrolling to avoid a weird double-animation.
    49→  const preScrollToTopIfNeeded = (options: Required<ShotNavigationOptions>) => {
    50→    if (!options.scrollToTop) return;
    51→    if (options.scrollBehavior !== 'auto') return;
    52→    // Avoid delaying the "start at top" behavior.
    53→    if (options.scrollDelay !== 0) return;
    54→    window.scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: 'auto' });
    55→    // Also dispatch event for custom scroll containers (e.g. mobile split view)
    56→    window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('app:scrollToTop', { detail: { behavior: 'auto' } }));
    57→  };
    58→
    59→  const performScroll = (options: Required<ShotNavigationOptions>) => {
    60→    if (options.scrollToTop) {
    61→      const scrollFn = () => {
    62→        // Use requestAnimationFrame to ensure DOM has painted
    63→        requestAnimationFrame(() => {
    64→          // Always scroll the window - containerRef is just a wrapper div, not a scroll container
    65→          window.scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: options.scrollBehavior });
    66→          // Also dispatch event for custom scroll containers (e.g. mobile split view)
    67→          window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('app:scrollToTop', { detail: { behavior: options.scrollBehavior } }));
    68→        });
    69→      };
    70→      
    71→      if (options.scrollDelay > 0) {
    72→        setTimeout(scrollFn, options.scrollDelay);
    73→      } else {
    74→        scrollFn();
    75→      }
    76→    }
    77→  };
    78→
    79→  const closePanes = (options: Required<ShotNavigationOptions>) => {
    80→    if (options.closeMobilePanes && isMobile) {
    81→      window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('mobilePaneOpen', { detail: { side: null } }));
    82→    }
    83→  };
    84→
    85→  const navigateToShot = (shot: Shot, options: ShotNavigationOptions = {}) => {
    86→    const opts = { ...defaultOptions, ...options };
    87→
    88→    preScrollToTopIfNeeded(opts);
    89→
    90→    // Update the current shot context
    91→    setCurrentShotId(shot.id);
    92→
    93→    // Navigate to the shot with hash
    94→    const targetUrl = travelShotUrl(shot.id);
    95→    navigate(targetUrl, {
    96→      state: {
    97→        fromShotClick: true,
    98→        shotData: shot,
    99→        isNewlyCreated: opts.isNewlyCreated
   100→      },
   101→      replace: opts.replace,
   102→    });
   103→
   104→    // Handle side effects
   105→    performScroll(opts);
   106→    closePanes(opts);
   107→
   108→  };
   109→
   110→  const navigateToShotEditor = (options: ShotNavigationOptions = {}) => {
   111→    const opts = { ...defaultOptions, ...options };
   112→    
   113→    // Clear current shot selection
   114→    setCurrentShotId(null);
   115→    
   116→    // Navigate to the shot editor without a specific shot
   117→    navigate(TOOL_ROUTES.TRAVEL_BETWEEN_IMAGES, {
   118→      state: { fromShotClick: false },
   119→      replace: opts.replace,
   120→    });
   121→    
   122→    // Handle side effects
   123→    performScroll(opts);
   124→    closePanes(opts);
   125→  };
   126→
   127→  const navigateToNextShot = (shots: Shot[], currentShot: Shot, options: ShotNavigationOptions = {}): boolean => {
   128→    const currentIndex = shots.findIndex(shot => shot.id === currentShot.id);
   129→    if (currentIndex >= 0 && currentIndex < shots.length - 1) {
   130→      const nextShot = shots[currentIndex + 1];
   131→      navigateToShot(nextShot, { ...options, replace: true });
   132→      return true;
   133→    }
   134→    return false;
   135→  };
   136→
   137→  const navigateToPreviousShot = (shots: Shot[], currentShot: Shot, options: ShotNavigationOptions = {}): boolean => {
   138→    const currentIndex = shots.findIndex(shot => shot.id === currentShot.id);
   139→    if (currentIndex > 0) {
   140→      const previousShot = shots[currentIndex - 1];
   141→      navigateToShot(previousShot, { ...options, replace: true });
   142→      return true;
   143→    }
   144→    return false;
   145→  };
   146→
   147→  return {
   148→    navigateToShot,
   149→    navigateToShotEditor,
   150→    navigateToNextShot,
   151→    navigateToPreviousShot,
   152→  };
   153→};

1→/**
     2→ * Shared download logic for ImageLightbox and VideoLightbox
     3→ *
     4→ * Resolves the correct URL (from intended variant or effective URL),
     5→ * extracts prompt for filename, and delegates to downloadMedia.
     6→ */
     7→
     8→import type { GenerationRow, GenerationVariant } from '@/shared/hooks/useVariants';
     9→import { readSegmentOverrides } from '@/shared/utils/settingsMigration';
    10→import { downloadMedia } from './download';
    11→
    12→interface LightboxDownloadOptions {
    13→  /** Ref to the variant the user intends to download (synchronous, avoids race condition) */
    14→  intendedVariantId: string | null;
    15→  /** All loaded variants */
    16→  variants: GenerationVariant[];
    17→  /** Fallback URL when no variant matches */
    18→  fallbackUrl: string;
    19→  /** The media object for id, metadata, params, contentType */
    20→  media: GenerationRow;
    21→  /** Whether this is a video download */
    22→  isVideo: boolean;
    23→  /** Called with true/false to manage download loading state */
    24→  setIsDownloading: (v: boolean) => void;
    25→}
    26→
    27→/**
    28→ * Execute a lightbox download with variant resolution and prompt-based filename.
    29→ */
    30→export async function handleLightboxDownload({
    31→  intendedVariantId,
    32→  variants,
    33→  fallbackUrl,
    34→  media,
    35→  isVideo,
    36→  setIsDownloading,
    37→}: LightboxDownloadOptions): Promise<void> {
    38→  let urlToDownload: string | undefined;
    39→
    40→  if (intendedVariantId && variants.length > 0) {
    41→    const intendedVariant = variants.find((v) => v.id === intendedVariantId);
    42→    if (intendedVariant?.location) {
    43→      urlToDownload = intendedVariant.location;
    44→    }
    45→  }
    46→
    47→  if (!urlToDownload) {
    48→    urlToDownload = fallbackUrl;
    49→  }
    50→
    51→  if (!urlToDownload) return;
    52→
    53→  setIsDownloading(true);
    54→  try {
    55→    const segmentOverrides = readSegmentOverrides(media.metadata as Record<string, unknown> | null);
    56→    const prompt = media.params?.prompt ||
    57→                   (media.metadata as Record<string, unknown> | undefined)?.enhanced_prompt as string | undefined ||
    58→                   segmentOverrides.prompt ||
    59→                   (media.metadata as Record<string, unknown> | undefined)?.prompt as string | undefined;
    60→    await downloadMedia(urlToDownload, media.id, isVideo, media.contentType, prompt);
    61→  } finally {
    62→    setIsDownloading(false);
    63→  }
    64→}
    65→

1→import { useState, useEffect, useRef, useCallback } from 'react';
     2→import { GenerationRow } from '@/types/shots';
     3→import { supabase } from '@/integrations/supabase/client';
     4→import { useToolSettings, type SettingsScope } from '@/shared/hooks/useToolSettings';
     5→
     6→/**
     7→ * Shared hook for edit tool media persistence.
     8→ * Handles loading last-edited media from project settings on mount,
     9→ * preloading the media URL, and saving selection changes back to settings.
    10→ *
    11→ * Used by EditImagesPage and EditVideoPage.
    12→ */
    13→
    14→interface UseEditToolMediaPersistenceParams {
    15→  /** The tool settings key, e.g. 'edit-images-ui' */
    16→  settingsToolId: string;
    17→  /** Current project ID */
    18→  projectId: string | undefined;
    19→  /** Called after a generation is fetched from DB, before setting it as selected.
    20→   *  Use this to preload images/posters. */
    21→  preloadMedia?: (generation: GenerationRow) => void;
    22→  /** Called after successfully loading persisted generation from DB.
    23→   *  Use this to restore extra state like video segments.
    24→   *  Receives the full settings object. */
    25→  onSettingsLoaded?: (settings: Record<string, unknown>) => void;
    26→  /** Extra data to merge when clearing settings on editor close.
    27→   *  e.g. { lastEditedMediaSegments: undefined } for video */
    28→  extraClearData?: Record<string, unknown>;
    29→}
    30→
    31→interface UseEditToolMediaPersistenceReturn {
    32→  /** The selected media from persisted settings, or null */
    33→  selectedMedia: GenerationRow | null;
    34→  /** Set the selected media (also persists to settings) */
    35→  setSelectedMedia: (media: GenerationRow | null) => void;
    36→  /** Call this when user explicitly closes the editor */
    37→  handleEditorClose: () => void;
    38→  /** Whether settings are loading or persisted media is being fetched */
    39→  isLoading: boolean;
    40→  /** Whether we have a stored ID that hasn't resolved yet (for skeleton display) */
    41→  showSkeleton: boolean;
    42→  /** The raw UI settings object */
    43→  uiSettings: Record<string, unknown> | undefined;
    44→  /** The update function from useToolSettings */
    45→  updateUISettings: (scope: SettingsScope, settings: Record<string, unknown>) => Promise<void>;
    46→  /** Whether the underlying tool settings are loading */
    47→  isUISettingsLoading: boolean;
    48→  /** Ref tracking whether user explicitly closed the editor */
    49→  userClosedEditor: React.MutableRefObject<boolean>;
    50→}
    51→
    52→export function useEditToolMediaPersistence({
    53→  settingsToolId,
    54→  projectId,
    55→  preloadMedia,
    56→  onSettingsLoaded,
    57→  extraClearData,
    58→}: UseEditToolMediaPersistenceParams): UseEditToolMediaPersistenceReturn {
    59→  const [selectedMedia, setSelectedMediaState] = useState<GenerationRow | null>(null);
    60→  const [isLoadingPersistedMedia, setIsLoadingPersistedMedia] = useState(false);
    61→
    62→  // Track if we've already loaded from settings to prevent re-loading
    63→  const hasLoadedFromSettings = useRef(false);
    64→  // Track if user has explicitly closed the editor (vs initial mount state)
    65→  const userClosedEditor = useRef(false);
    66→
    67→  // Project-level UI settings for persisting last edited media
    68→  const {
    69→    settings: uiSettings,
    70→    update: updateUISettings,
    71→    isLoading: isUISettingsLoading,
    72→  } = useToolSettings<Record<string, unknown>>(settingsToolId, {
    73→    projectId,
    74→    enabled: !!projectId,
    75→  });
    76→
    77→  // Load last edited media from database settings on mount
    78→  useEffect(() => {
    79→    if (!projectId || isUISettingsLoading || hasLoadedFromSettings.current) return;
    80→
    81→    const storedId = uiSettings?.lastEditedMediaId as string | undefined;
    82→    hasLoadedFromSettings.current = true; // Mark as attempted even if no stored ID
    83→
    84→    if (storedId && !selectedMedia) {
    85→      setIsLoadingPersistedMedia(true);
    86→      supabase
    87→        .from('generations')
    88→        .select('*')
    89→        .eq('id', storedId)
    90→        .single()
    91→        .then(({ data, error }) => {
    92→          if (data && !error) {
    93→            const gen = data as GenerationRow;
    94→            preloadMedia?.(gen);
    95→            setSelectedMediaState(gen);
    96→            // Let caller restore extra state from settings
    97→            if (onSettingsLoaded && uiSettings) {
    98→              onSettingsLoaded(uiSettings);
    99→            }
   100→          } else {
   101→            // Clear invalid stored ID
   102→            updateUISettings('project', {
   103→              lastEditedMediaId: undefined,
   104→              ...extraClearData,
   105→            });
   106→          }
   107→          setIsLoadingPersistedMedia(false);
   108→        });
   109→    }
   110→  }, [projectId, uiSettings?.lastEditedMediaId, isUISettingsLoading, selectedMedia, updateUISettings, preloadMedia, onSettingsLoaded, uiSettings, extraClearData]);
   111→
   112→  // Persist selected media ID to database settings (or clear it when media is removed)
   113→  useEffect(() => {
   114→    if (!projectId || isUISettingsLoading || !hasLoadedFromSettings.current) return;
   115→
   116→    if (selectedMedia && selectedMedia.id !== (uiSettings?.lastEditedMediaId as string | undefined)) {
   117→      updateUISettings('project', { lastEditedMediaId: selectedMedia.id });
   118→      userClosedEditor.current = false; // Reset close flag when new media selected
   119→    } else if (!selectedMedia && uiSettings?.lastEditedMediaId && userClosedEditor.current) {
   120→      // Only clear when user explicitly closed the editor, not on initial mount
   121→      updateUISettings('project', {
   122→        lastEditedMediaId: undefined,
   123→        ...extraClearData,
   124→      });
   125→    }
   126→  }, [selectedMedia?.id, projectId, isUISettingsLoading, uiSettings?.lastEditedMediaId, updateUISettings, extraClearData]);
   127→
   128→  // Wrapper to set media from outside (e.g. gallery selection, upload result)
   129→  const setSelectedMedia = useCallback((media: GenerationRow | null) => {
   130→    setSelectedMediaState(media);
   131→  }, []);
   132→
   133→  // Call when user explicitly closes the editor
   134→  const handleEditorClose = useCallback(() => {
   135→    userClosedEditor.current = true;
   136→    setSelectedMediaState(null);
   137→  }, []);
   138→
   139→  const showSkeleton = isUISettingsLoading || isLoadingPersistedMedia ||
   140→    (!!uiSettings?.lastEditedMediaId && !selectedMedia && !userClosedEditor.current);
   141→
   142→  return {
   143→    selectedMedia,
   144→    setSelectedMedia,
   145→    handleEditorClose,
   146→    isLoading: isUISettingsLoading || isLoadingPersistedMedia,
   147→    showSkeleton,
   148→    uiSettings,
   149→    updateUISettings,
   150→    isUISettingsLoading,
   151→    userClosedEditor,
   152→  };
   153→}
   154→

     9→/** Raw generation data from Supabase */

    23→ * Build shot associations array from shot_generations relation
    24→ */

    26→  return shotGenerations.map((sg) => ({
    27→    shot_id: sg.shot_id,
    28→    timeline_frame: sg.timeline_frame,

    30→  }));
    31→};
    32→
    33→/**
    34→ * Transform database generation data to GenerationRow format
    35→ */
    36→export const transformExternalGeneration = (
    37→  data: RawGenerationData,
    38→  shotGenerations: ShotGenerationJoinRow[]
    39→): GenerationRow => {
    40→  const allAssociations = buildShotAssociations(shotGenerations);
    41→
    42→  const transformedData = {

    45→    shotImageEntryId: data.id,

    48→    location: data.location,
    49→    type: data.type,
    50→    createdAt: data.created_at,
    51→    timeline_frame: shotGenerations.length > 0 ? shotGenerations[0].timeline_frame : undefined,
    52→    metadata: (typeof data.params === 'object' && data.params !== null && !Array.isArray(data.params))
    53→      ? data.params as Record<string, unknown>
    54→      : {},
    55→    starred: data.starred ?? false,
    56→    params: data.params || {},
    57→    based_on: data.based_on,
    58→    all_shot_associations: allAssociations,
    59→    ...(shotGenerations.length > 0 ? {
    60→      shot_id: shotGenerations[0].shot_id,
    61→      position: shotGenerations[0].timeline_frame,
    62→    } : {})
    63→  } as GenerationRow;
    64→
    65→  return transformedData;

1→import { GenerationRow } from '@/types/shots';
     2→import { 
     3→  calculateFrameForIndex, 
     4→  extractExistingFrames 
     5→} from '@/shared/utils/timelinePositionCalculator';
     6→
     7→/**
     8→ * Calculate frame position for inserting at a given index
     9→ * The frame position should be the midpoint between surrounding images,
    10→ * with collision detection to ensure uniqueness.
    11→ * 
    12→ * NOTE: This calculates timeline_frame (the frame number for video export),
    13→ * NOT the grid index position. The grid index comes from BatchDropZone.
    14→ * 
    15→ * IMPORTANT: currentImages are GenerationRow objects where:
    16→ * - .id = shot_generations.id (unique per shot entry)
    17→ * - .generation_id = generations.id (the actual generation)
    18→ * - .timeline_frame = frame number for video positioning
    19→ */
    20→export const getFramePositionForIndex = (
    21→  index: number,
    22→  currentImages: GenerationRow[],
    23→  batchVideoFrames: number
    24→): number | undefined => {
    25→  // Extract existing frames from current images (filters out videos and null frames)
    26→  const existingFrames = extractExistingFrames(currentImages);
    27→  
    28→  // Use unified calculator with collision detection
    29→  return calculateFrameForIndex(index, existingFrames, batchVideoFrames);
    30→};
    31→
    32→/**
    33→ * Get range of image IDs between two indices (inclusive)
    34→ */
    35→export const getImageRange = (
    36→  startIndex: number,
    37→  endIndex: number,
    38→  currentImages: GenerationRow[]
    39→): string[] => {
    40→  const minIndex = Math.min(startIndex, endIndex);
    41→  const maxIndex = Math.max(startIndex, endIndex);
    42→  const rangeIds: string[] = [];
    43→  
    44→  for (let i = minIndex; i <= maxIndex; i++) {
    45→    if (currentImages[i]) {
    46→      // img.id is shot_generations.id - unique per entry
    47→      rangeIds.push(currentImages[i].id);
    48→    }
    49→  }
    50→  
    51→  return rangeIds;
    52→};
    53→
    54→/**
    55→ * Calculate aspect ratio style for images
    56→ */
    57→export const getAspectRatioStyle = (projectAspectRatio?: string) => {
    58→  if (projectAspectRatio) {
    59→    const [w, h] = projectAspectRatio.split(':').map(Number);
    60→    if (!isNaN(w) && !isNaN(h)) {
    61→      const aspectRatio = w / h;
    62→      return { aspectRatio: `${aspectRatio}` };
    63→    }
    64→  }
    65→  
    66→  // Default to square aspect ratio
    67→  return { aspectRatio: '1' };
    68→};

1→import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query';
     2→import { supabase } from '@/integrations/supabase/client';
     3→import { getVisibleTaskTypes } from '@/shared/lib/taskConfig';
     4→import { useSmartPollingConfig } from '@/shared/hooks/useSmartPolling';
     5→import { QUERY_PRESETS, STANDARD_RETRY, STANDARD_RETRY_DELAY } from '@/shared/lib/queryDefaults';
     6→import { queryKeys } from '@/shared/lib/queryKeys';
     7→import { dataFreshnessManager } from '@/shared/realtime/DataFreshnessManager';
     8→import { handleError } from '@/shared/lib/errorHandler';
     9→
    10→// Hook to get status counts for indicators
    11→export const useTaskStatusCounts = (projectId: string | null) => {
    12→  // SMART POLLING: Use DataFreshnessManager for intelligent polling decisions
    13→  const smartPollingConfig = useSmartPollingConfig(projectId ? queryKeys.tasks.statusCounts(projectId) : ['task-status-counts', null]);
    14→
    15→  return useQuery({
    16→    queryKey: projectId ? queryKeys.tasks.statusCounts(projectId) : ['task-status-counts', null],
    17→    queryFn: async () => {
    18→      // [TasksPaneCountMismatch] Note on counting rules for correlation with list visibility
    19→
    20→      if (!projectId) {
    21→        return { processing: 0, recentSuccesses: 0, recentFailures: 0 };
    22→      }
    23→
    24→      // Match TasksPane list semantics: only count visible task types (and parent tasks)
    25→      const visibleTaskTypes = getVisibleTaskTypes();
    26→
    27→      // Get 1 hour ago timestamp
    28→      const oneHourAgo = new Date(Date.now() - 60 * 60 * 1000).toISOString();
    29→
    30→      // Execute all queries in parallel with error resilience
    31→      const [processingResult, successResult, failureResult] = await Promise.allSettled([
    32→        // Query for processing tasks (any time)
    33→        supabase
    34→          .from('tasks')
    35→          .select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true })
    36→          .eq('project_id', projectId)
    37→          .in('status', ['Queued', 'In Progress'])
    38→          .is('params->orchestrator_task_id_ref', null) // Only parent tasks; include orchestrators
    39→          .in('task_type', visibleTaskTypes), // Only visible task types
    40→
    41→        // Query for recent successes (last hour)
    42→        supabase
    43→          .from('tasks')
    44→          .select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true })
    45→          .eq('project_id', projectId)
    46→          .eq('status', 'Complete')
    47→          // `updated_at` is often null/unreliable in this schema; `generation_processed_at` is the real completion timestamp.
    48→          .gte('generation_processed_at', oneHourAgo)
    49→          .is('params->orchestrator_task_id_ref', null) // Only parent tasks
    50→          .in('task_type', visibleTaskTypes), // Only visible task types
    51→
    52→        // Query for recent failures (last hour)
    53→        // NOTE: Use `updated_at` for failures since `generation_processed_at` is only set on success
    54→        // NOTE: Only count 'Failed', not 'Cancelled' - cancelled tasks are user-initiated and not errors
    55→        supabase
    56→          .from('tasks')
    57→          .select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true })
    58→          .eq('project_id', projectId)
    59→          .eq('status', 'Failed')
    60→          .gte('updated_at', oneHourAgo)
    61→          .is('params->orchestrator_task_id_ref', null) // Only parent tasks
    62→          .in('task_type', visibleTaskTypes) // Only visible task types
    63→      ]);
    64→
    65→      // Handle processing count result
    66→      let processingCount = 0;
    67→      if (processingResult.status === 'fulfilled') {
    68→        const { count, error } = processingResult.value;
    69→        if (error) {
    70→          handleError(error, { context: 'useTaskStatusCounts.processing', showToast: false, logData: { projectId } });
    71→        } else {
    72→          processingCount = count || 0;
    73→        }
    74→      } else {
    75→        handleError(processingResult.reason instanceof Error ? processingResult.reason : new Error(String(processingResult.reason)), { context: 'useTaskStatusCounts.processing', showToast: false, logData: { projectId } });
    76→      }
    77→
    78→      // Handle success count result
    79→      let successCount = 0;
    80→      if (successResult.status === 'fulfilled') {
    81→        const { count, error } = successResult.value;
    82→        if (error) {
    83→          handleError(error, { context: 'useTaskStatusCounts.success', showToast: false, logData: { projectId } });
    84→        } else {
    85→          successCount = count || 0;
    86→        }
    87→      } else {
    88→        handleError(successResult.reason instanceof Error ? successResult.reason : new Error(String(successResult.reason)), { context: 'useTaskStatusCounts.success', showToast: false, logData: { projectId } });
    89→      }
    90→
    91→      // Handle failure count result
    92→      let failureCount = 0;
    93→      if (failureResult.status === 'fulfilled') {
    94→        const { count, error } = failureResult.value;
    95→        if (error) {
    96→          handleError(error, { context: 'useTaskStatusCounts.failure', showToast: false, logData: { projectId } });
    97→        } else {
    98→          failureCount = count || 0;
    99→        }
   100→      } else {

   125→        dataFreshnessManager.onFetchFailure(queryKeys.tasks.statusCounts(projectId), errorReason as Error);
   126→      } else {

   128→      }
   129→
   130→      return result;
   131→    },

     3→// Map a specific lora_type to its broad filter category
     4→export function getFilterCategory(loraType: string | undefined): ModelFilterCategory {
     5→  if (!loraType) return 'all';
     6→  const lower = loraType.toLowerCase();
     7→  if (lower.includes('qwen')) return 'qwen';
     8→  if (lower.includes('wan')) return 'wan';

    13→export function getDefaultSubFilter(loraType: string | undefined): string {
    14→  if (!loraType) return 'all';
    15→  const normalized = loraType.trim();
    16→  // If the passed lora_type matches a sub-filter option, default to it.
    17→  const qwenOptions = getSubFilterOptions('qwen').map(opt => opt.value);
    18→  const wanOptions = getSubFilterOptions('wan').map(opt => opt.value);

1→export function validateHuggingFaceUrl(url: string): { isValid: boolean; message: string } {
     2→  if (!url) return { isValid: false, message: 'URL is required' };
     3→
     4→  if (url.startsWith('blob:')) {
     5→    return {
     6→      isValid: false,
     7→      message: 'This is a blob URL (a temporary browser link). Use the direct /resolve/ download URL from HuggingFace instead.'
     8→    };
     9→  }
    10→
    11→  // HuggingFace /blob/ URLs are view pages, not direct downloads — need /resolve/
    12→  if (url.includes('huggingface.co') && url.includes('/blob/')) {
    13→    return {
    14→      isValid: false,
    15→      message: 'This is a HuggingFace page link. Replace /blob/ with /resolve/ in the URL to get the direct download link.'
    16→    };
    17→  }
    18→
    19→  // Check if it's a /resolve/ URL
    20→  if (!url.includes('/resolve/')) {
    21→    return {
    22→      isValid: false,
    23→      message: 'Must be a /resolve/ URL for direct download'
    24→    };
    25→  }
    26→
    27→  // Check if it's a HuggingFace URL
    28→  if (!url.includes('huggingface.co')) {
    29→    return {
    30→      isValid: false,
    31→      message: 'Must be a HuggingFace URL'
    32→    };
    33→  }
    34→
    35→  return { isValid: true, message: '' };
    36→}
    37→
    38→function extractFilenameFromUrl(url: string): string {
    39→  try {
    40→    // Extract filename from /resolve/ URL
    41→    const urlParts = url.split('/');
    42→    const filename = urlParts[urlParts.length - 1];
    43→    return filename || '';
    44→  } catch {
    45→    return '';
    46→  }
    47→}
    48→
    49→export function generateUniqueFilename(
    50→  name: string,
    51→  baseModel: string,
    52→  huggingfaceUrl: string = '',
    53→  existingFilenames: string[] = []
    54→): string {
    55→  // First try to get filename from HuggingFace URL
    56→  let filename = extractFilenameFromUrl(huggingfaceUrl);
    57→
    58→  // If filename is generic, too short, or missing, make it specific
    59→  const genericNames = ['model.safetensors', 'lora.safetensors', 'pytorch_lora_weights.safetensors'];
    60→  const isGeneric = genericNames.includes(filename.toLowerCase()) || filename.length < 8;
    61→
    62→  if (!filename || isGeneric) {
    63→    const cleanName = name.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]/g, '_');
    64→    const cleanBaseModel = baseModel.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]/g, '_');
    65→    const extension = filename.includes('.') ? filename.split('.').pop() : 'safetensors';
    66→    filename = `${cleanName}_${cleanBaseModel}.${extension}`;
    67→  }
    68→
    69→  // Ensure filename is unique by adding suffix if needed
    70→  let uniqueFilename = filename;
    71→  let counter = 1;
    72→  while (existingFilenames.includes(uniqueFilename)) {
    73→    const baseName = filename.substring(0, filename.lastIndexOf('.'));
    74→    const extension = filename.substring(filename.lastIndexOf('.'));
    75→    uniqueFilename = `${baseName}_${counter}${extension}`;
    76→    counter++;
    77→  }
    78→
    79→  return uniqueFilename;
    80→}
    81→

1→import { GenerationRow } from '@/types/shots';
     2→
     3→/**
     4→ * Calculate new order for multi-drag operation
     5→ */
     6→export const calculateMultiDragOrder = (
     7→  currentImages: GenerationRow[],
     8→  selectedIds: string[],
     9→  activeIndex: number,
    10→  overIndex: number,
    11→  _activeId: string,
    12→  overId: string
    13→): GenerationRow[] => {
    14→  // img.id is shot_generations.id - unique per entry
    15→  const selectedItems = currentImages.filter((img) => selectedIds.includes(img.id));
    16→  const remainingItems = currentImages.filter((img) => !selectedIds.includes(img.id));
    17→
    18→  // If dropping onto a selected item, we need to determine the correct insertion point
    19→  let targetIndex: number;
    20→  let newItems: GenerationRow[];
    21→  
    22→  if (selectedIds.includes(overId)) {
    23→    // Dropping onto a selected item - use the position relative to non-selected items
    24→    const selectedItemIndices = selectedItems.map(item => 
    25→      currentImages.findIndex(img => img.id === item.id)
    26→    ).sort((a, b) => a - b);
    27→    
    28→    const overIndexInSelected = selectedItemIndices.indexOf(overIndex);
    29→    
    30→    if (overIndexInSelected === 0) {
    31→      // Dropping on first selected item - insert at beginning of group
    32→      targetIndex = selectedItemIndices[0];
    33→    } else {
    34→      // Dropping on other selected item - insert after the previous non-selected item
    35→      const prevSelectedIndex = selectedItemIndices[overIndexInSelected - 1];
    36→      const itemsBetween = currentImages.slice(prevSelectedIndex + 1, overIndex);
    37→      const nonSelectedBetween = itemsBetween.filter(item => !selectedIds.includes(item.id));
    38→      targetIndex = prevSelectedIndex + nonSelectedBetween.length + 1;
    39→    }
    40→    
    41→    const overInRemainingIndex = remainingItems.findIndex((_, idx) => {
    42→      const remainingItemIndex = currentImages.findIndex(img => 
    43→        img.id === remainingItems[idx].id
    44→      );
    45→      return remainingItemIndex >= targetIndex;
    46→    });
    47→    
    48→    if (overInRemainingIndex === -1) {
    49→      // Insert at end
    50→      newItems = [...remainingItems, ...selectedItems];
    51→    } else {
    52→      newItems = [
    53→        ...remainingItems.slice(0, overInRemainingIndex),
    54→        ...selectedItems,
    55→        ...remainingItems.slice(overInRemainingIndex),
    56→      ];
    57→    }
    58→  } else {
    59→    // Dropping onto a non-selected item - use original logic
    60→    const overInRemainingIndex = remainingItems.findIndex((img) => img.id === overId);
    61→
    62→    if (activeIndex > overIndex) {
    63→      // Dragging up
    64→      newItems = [
    65→        ...remainingItems.slice(0, overInRemainingIndex),
    66→        ...selectedItems,
    67→        ...remainingItems.slice(overInRemainingIndex),
    68→      ];
    69→    } else {
    70→      // Dragging down
    71→      newItems = [
    72→        ...remainingItems.slice(0, overInRemainingIndex + 1),
    73→        ...selectedItems,
    74→        ...remainingItems.slice(overInRemainingIndex + 1),
    75→      ];
    76→    }
    77→  }
    78→
    79→  return newItems;
    80→};
    81→

1→/**
     2→ * Media dimension extraction utilities
     3→ *
     4→ * Shared by ImageLightbox and VideoLightbox to compute image dimensions
     5→ * from generation params/metadata (resolution, aspect ratio).
     6→ */
     7→
     8→import { ASPECT_RATIO_TO_RESOLUTION, findClosestAspectRatio, parseRatio } from '@/shared/lib/aspectRatios';
     9→import type { GenerationParams } from '@/types/shots';
    10→
    11→/**
    12→ * Parse a "WxH" resolution string into { width, height }.
    13→ */
    14→export function resolutionToDimensions(resolution: string): { width: number; height: number } | null {
    15→  if (!resolution || typeof resolution !== 'string' || !resolution.includes('x')) return null;
    16→  const [w, h] = resolution.split('x').map(Number);
    17→  if (!isNaN(w) && !isNaN(h) && w > 0 && h > 0) {
    18→    return { width: w, height: h };
    19→  }
    20→  return null;
    21→}
    22→
    23→/**
    24→ * Convert an aspect ratio string (e.g. "16:9") to pixel dimensions
    25→ * by finding the closest known resolution mapping.
    26→ */
    27→export function aspectRatioToDimensions(aspectRatio: string): { width: number; height: number } | null {
    28→  if (!aspectRatio) return null;
    29→  const directResolution = ASPECT_RATIO_TO_RESOLUTION[aspectRatio];
    30→  if (directResolution) return resolutionToDimensions(directResolution);
    31→  const ratio = parseRatio(aspectRatio);
    32→  if (!isNaN(ratio)) {
    33→    const closestAspectRatio = findClosestAspectRatio(ratio);
    34→    const closestResolution = ASPECT_RATIO_TO_RESOLUTION[closestAspectRatio];
    35→    if (closestResolution) return resolutionToDimensions(closestResolution);
    36→  }
    37→  return null;
    38→}
    39→
    40→interface MediaLike {
    41→  params?: GenerationParams | Record<string, unknown>;
    42→  metadata?: Record<string, unknown>;
    43→}
    44→
    45→/**
    46→ * Extract dimensions from a media object by checking, in priority order:
    47→ *   1. metadata.width/height
    48→ *   2. Various resolution fields (params, metadata, orchestrator_details)
    49→ *   3. Various aspect_ratio fields
    50→ *
    51→ * @param media - The media object with params/metadata
    52→ * @param extended - When true, checks extended resolution/aspect-ratio sources
    53→ *                   (orchestrator_details, custom_aspect_ratio). ImageLightbox uses
    54→ *                   extended=true, VideoLightbox uses extended=false.
    55→ */
    56→export function extractDimensionsFromMedia(
    57→  media: MediaLike | null | undefined,
    58→  extended = false,
    59→): { width: number; height: number } | null {
    60→  if (!media) return null;
    61→
    62→  const params = media.params as GenerationParams | undefined;
    63→  const metadata = media.metadata as Record<string, unknown> | undefined;
    64→
    65→  // Check metadata for width/height (these may exist as extended metadata fields)
    66→  if (metadata?.width && metadata?.height && typeof metadata.width === 'number' && typeof metadata.height === 'number') {
    67→    return { width: metadata.width, height: metadata.height };
    68→  }
    69→
    70→  // Build resolution sources - extended adds orchestrator_details and more param paths
    71→  const resolutionSources: unknown[] = [
    72→    params?.resolution,
    73→    (params as Record<string, unknown>)?.originalParams,
    74→    metadata?.resolution,
    75→  ];
    76→
    77→  if (extended) {
    78→    resolutionSources.push(
    79→      (params as Record<string, unknown>)?.orchestrator_details,
    80→      (metadata?.originalParams as Record<string, unknown> | undefined)?.resolution,
    81→      ((metadata?.originalParams as Record<string, unknown> | undefined)?.orchestrator_details as Record<string, unknown> | undefined)?.resolution,
    82→    );
    83→  }
    84→
    85→  for (const res of resolutionSources) {
    86→    if (typeof res === 'string') {
    87→      const dims = resolutionToDimensions(res);
    88→      if (dims) return dims;
    89→    }
    90→  }
    91→
    92→  // Build aspect ratio sources
    93→  const aspectRatioSources: unknown[] = [
    94→    params?.aspect_ratio,
    95→    metadata?.aspect_ratio,
    96→  ];
    97→
    98→  if (extended) {
    99→    aspectRatioSources.push(
   100→      (params as Record<string, unknown>)?.custom_aspect_ratio,
   101→      (params as Record<string, unknown>)?.originalParams,
   102→      (params as Record<string, unknown>)?.orchestrator_details,
   103→      (metadata?.originalParams as Record<string, unknown> | undefined)?.aspect_ratio,
   104→      ((metadata?.originalParams as Record<string, unknown> | undefined)?.orchestrator_details as Record<string, unknown> | undefined)?.aspect_ratio,
   105→    );
   106→  }
   107→
   108→  for (const ar of aspectRatioSources) {
   109→    if (ar && typeof ar === 'string') {
   110→      const dims = aspectRatioToDimensions(ar);
   111→      if (dims) return dims;
   112→    }
   113→  }
   114→
   115→  return null;
   116→}
   117→

   104→export const extractTaskParentGenerationId = (params: Record<string, unknown>): string | undefined => {
   105→  const p = params as DeepJsonParams;
   106→  return (
   107→    (p?.parent_generation_id as string) ||
   108→    ((p?.orchestrator_details as DeepJsonParams)?.parent_generation_id as string) ||
   109→    ((p?.full_orchestrator_payload as DeepJsonParams)?.parent_generation_id as string) ||
   110→    undefined
   111→  );
   112→};
   113→
   114→/**
   115→ * Extract pair_shot_generation_id from task params for segment videos.
   116→ * This identifies which timeline pair the segment belongs to.
   117→ */
   118→export const extractPairShotGenerationId = (task: Task): string | null => {
   119→  const params = task.params as DeepJsonParams;
   120→
   121→  const orchDetails = params?.orchestrator_details as DeepJsonParams | undefined;
   122→  const pairIds = orchDetails?.pair_shot_generation_ids as string[] | undefined;
   123→  const segmentIndex = (params?.segment_index as number) ?? 0;
   124→
   125→  return (
   126→    (params?.pair_shot_generation_id as string) ||
   127→    ((params?.individual_segment_params as DeepJsonParams)?.pair_shot_generation_id as string) ||
   128→    (pairIds?.[segmentIndex]) ||
   129→    null
   130→  );
   131→};
   132→
   133→/**
   134→ * Check if a task is a segment video (individual_travel_segment)
   135→ * These should open in shot context for proper timeline integration.
   136→ */
   137→export const isSegmentVideoTask = (task: Task): boolean => {
   138→  return task.taskType === 'individual_travel_segment';
   139→};
   140→
   141→/**
   142→ * Check if a segment is still connected to its shot's timeline.
   143→ * Returns true if the pair_shot_generation_id exists in shot_generations
   144→ * for the given shot and is positioned on the timeline.
   145→ */
   146→export const checkSegmentConnection = async (
   147→  pairShotGenerationId: string | null,
   148→  shotId: string
   149→): Promise<boolean> => {
   150→  if (!pairShotGenerationId) return false;
   151→
   152→  const { data } = await supabase
   153→    .from('shot_generations')
   154→    .select('id, shot_id, timeline_frame')
   155→    .eq('id', pairShotGenerationId)
   156→    .maybeSingle();
   157→
   158→  // Check if it exists, belongs to the right shot, and is on timeline
   159→  return !!data && data.shot_id === shotId && (data.timeline_frame ?? -1) >= 0;
   160→};
   161→
   162→
   163→
   164→

    72→

    74→  // This enables cross-project inheritance for the first shot in a new project
    75→  const isNewProject = !shots || shots.length === 0;

   137→  }

   139→  return {
   140→    mainSettings,
   141→    uiSettings,
   142→    joinSegmentsSettings
   143→  };
   144→}
   145→
   146→/**

   173→  }

   179→      // Clear prompt for new shots (shot-specific, shouldn't inherit)

   187→  
   188→  // NOTE: LoRAs no longer need separate DB save - they're part of mainSettings
   189→  // and will be saved by useShotSettings when it picks up from sessionStorage
   190→}
   191→
   192→/**

   196→export async function inheritSettingsForNewShot(

1→import { toast } from '@/shared/components/ui/sonner';
     2→import { handleError } from '@/shared/lib/errorHandler';
     3→import { isAbortError } from '@/shared/lib/errorUtils';
     4→import type { NavigatorWithDeviceInfo } from '@/types/browser-extensions';
     5→
     6→/**
     7→ * Detect if running as iOS/iPadOS PWA (standalone mode)
     8→ */
     9→const isIOSPwa = (): boolean => {
    10→  // Check if running in standalone mode (PWA)
    11→  const nav = window.navigator as NavigatorWithDeviceInfo;
    12→  const isStandalone = nav.standalone === true ||
    13→    window.matchMedia('(display-mode: standalone)').matches;
    14→  
    15→  // Check if iOS/iPadOS
    16→  const isIOS = /iPad|iPhone|iPod/.test(navigator.userAgent) ||
    17→    (navigator.platform === 'MacIntel' && navigator.maxTouchPoints > 1);
    18→  
    19→  return isStandalone && isIOS;
    20→};
    21→
    22→/**
    23→ * Get file extension from content type or URL
    24→ */
    25→const getFileExtension = (url: string, isVideo: boolean, contentType?: string): string => {
    26→  // Priority 1: Use stored content type if available
    27→  if (contentType) {
    28→    const ext = contentType.split('/')[1]?.split(';')[0]?.trim();
    29→    if (ext && ext !== 'octet-stream') {
    30→      return ext;
    31→    }
    32→  }
    33→  
    34→  // Priority 2: Extract from URL (strip query params first)
    35→  const urlWithoutParams = url.split('?')[0];
    36→  const urlParts = urlWithoutParams.split('.');
    37→  if (urlParts.length > 1) {
    38→    const ext = urlParts.pop()!;
    39→    if (ext && ext.length <= 5) { // Reasonable extension length
    40→      return ext;
    41→    }
    42→  }
    43→  
    44→  // Priority 3: Default based on media type
    45→  return isVideo ? 'mp4' : 'png';
    46→};
    47→
    48→/**
    49→ * Sanitize a string for use as a filename
    50→ * Removes/replaces characters that are invalid in most filesystems
    51→ */
    52→const sanitizeFilename = (str: string, maxLength: number = 50): string => {
    53→  // Remove or replace invalid filename characters
    54→  let sanitized = str
    55→    .replace(/[<>:"/\\|?*]/g, '') // Remove invalid chars
    56→    .replace(/\s+/g, '_') // Replace spaces with underscores
    57→    .replace(/_+/g, '_') // Collapse multiple underscores
    58→    .replace(/^_|_$/g, '') // Trim leading/trailing underscores
    59→    .trim();
    60→
    61→  // Truncate to maxLength
    62→  if (sanitized.length > maxLength) {
    63→    sanitized = sanitized.substring(0, maxLength).replace(/_$/, '');
    64→  }
    65→
    66→  return sanitized || 'media';
    67→};
    68→
    69→/**
    70→ * Download media (image or video) from a URL
    71→ * Handles timeouts, fallbacks, and error cases
    72→ * Special handling for iOS PWA where download attribute doesn't work
    73→ *
    74→ * @param url - The URL to download from
    75→ * @param mediaId - Media ID for filename (UUID)
    76→ * @param isVideo - Whether the media is a video
    77→ * @param contentType - Optional MIME type for proper file extension (e.g., 'video/mp4')
    78→ * @param prompt - Optional prompt text to use in filename for better readability
    79→ */
    80→export const downloadMedia = async (url: string, mediaId: string, isVideo: boolean, contentType?: string, prompt?: string): Promise<void> => {
    81→  const fileExt = getFileExtension(url, isVideo, contentType);
    82→
    83→  // Generate a user-friendly filename:
    84→  // - If prompt is available: use sanitized prompt + short ID suffix for uniqueness
    85→  // - Otherwise: use media_<short_id> format
    86→  const shortId = typeof mediaId === 'string' && mediaId.length > 8 ? mediaId.substring(0, 8) : mediaId;
    87→  let filename: string;
    88→  if (prompt && typeof prompt === 'string' && prompt.trim()) {
    89→    const sanitizedPrompt = sanitizeFilename(prompt, 40);
    90→    filename = `${sanitizedPrompt}_${shortId}.${fileExt}`;
    91→  } else {
    92→    filename = `media_${shortId}.${fileExt}`;
    93→  }
    94→
    95→  // For iOS PWA, use Web Share API or open in new tab
    96→  // The download attribute doesn't work in standalone mode
    97→  if (isIOSPwa()) {
    98→    
    99→    try {
   100→      // Try Web Share API first (allows saving to Photos or Files)
   101→      if (navigator.share && navigator.canShare) {
   102→        // Fetch the file as blob
   103→        const response = await fetch(url);
   104→        if (!response.ok) throw new Error('Failed to fetch');
   105→        
   106→        const blob = await response.blob();
   107→        const file = new File([blob], filename, { type: contentType || blob.type });
   108→        
   109→        if (navigator.canShare({ files: [file] })) {
   110→          await navigator.share({
   111→            files: [file],
   112→            title: 'Save Media',
   113→          });
   114→          return;
   115→        }
   116→      }
   117→    } catch (shareError) {
   118→      handleError(shareError, { context: 'downloadMedia', showToast: false });
   119→    }
   120→    
   121→    // Fallback: Open URL in new window - iOS will show its native preview
   122→    // which allows saving to Photos
   123→    try {
   124→      window.open(url, '_blank');
   125→      toast.info('Long press the image/video to save it');
   126→      return;
   127→    } catch (openError) {
   128→      handleError(openError, { context: 'downloadMedia', toastTitle: 'Unable to download. Try opening in Safari.' });
   129→      return;
   130→    }
   131→  }
   132→
   133→  try {
   134→    // Add timeout to prevent hanging downloads
   135→    const controller = new AbortController();
   136→    const timeoutId = setTimeout(() => {
   137→      controller.abort();
   138→    }, 15000); // 15 second timeout
   139→
   140→    const response = await fetch(url, {
   141→      signal: controller.signal
   142→    });
   143→    
   144→    clearTimeout(timeoutId);
   145→    
   146→    if (!response.ok) {
   147→      throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status}: ${response.statusText}`);
   148→    }
   149→
   150→    const blob = await response.blob();
   151→
   152→    const objectUrl = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
   153→
   154→    const link = document.createElement('a');
   155→    link.href = objectUrl;
   156→    link.download = filename;
   157→    document.body.appendChild(link);
   158→    
   159→    // Programmatic click to trigger download
   160→    link.click();
   161→
   162→    // Keep link in DOM briefly to allow download to initiate
   163→    setTimeout(() => {
   164→      if (document.body.contains(link)) {
   165→        document.body.removeChild(link);
   166→      }
   167→    }, 1500);
   168→    
   169→    // Delay object URL cleanup to avoid interrupting download (give browsers time)
   170→    setTimeout(() => {
   171→      try {
   172→        URL.revokeObjectURL(objectUrl);
   173→      } catch {}
   174→    }, 10000);
   175→
   176→  } catch (error: unknown) {
   177→    if (isAbortError(error)) {
   178→      handleError(error, { context: 'downloadMedia', toastTitle: 'Download timed out. Please try again.' });
   179→      return; // Don't try fallback for timeout
   180→    }
   181→
   182→    handleError(error, { context: 'downloadMedia', showToast: false });
   183→    
   184→    // Fallback 1: direct link with download attribute
   185→    try {
   186→      const link = document.createElement('a');
   187→      link.href = url;
   188→      link.download = filename;
   189→      link.target = '_blank';
   190→      document.body.appendChild(link);
   191→      link.click();
   192→      setTimeout(() => {
   193→        if (document.body.contains(link)) {
   194→          document.body.removeChild(link);
   195→        }
   196→      }, 1500);
   197→    } catch {}
   198→
   199→    // Fallback 2: window.open (some browsers block programmatic downloads)
   200→    try {
   201→      window.open(url, '_blank');
   202→    } catch {}
   203→  }
   204→};
   205→
   206→

    82→  11: 'grid-cols-3 sm:grid-cols-5 md:grid-cols-7 lg:grid-cols-8 xl:grid-cols-10 2xl:grid-cols-11',
    83→  12: 'grid-cols-4 sm:grid-cols-6 md:grid-cols-7 lg:grid-cols-9 xl:grid-cols-10 2xl:grid-cols-12',
    84→} as const;
    85→
    86→/**
    87→ * Skeleton column configs that match GRID_COLUMN_CLASSES for each columnsPerRow value.
    88→ * These must stay in sync with GRID_COLUMN_CLASSES to prevent layout shift during loading.
    89→ */
    90→export const SKELETON_COLUMNS = {
    91→  2: { base: 1, sm: 2, md: 2, lg: 2, xl: 2, '2xl': 2 },
    92→  3: { base: 1, md: 2, lg: 3, xl: 3, '2xl': 3 },
    93→  4: { base: 2, sm: 3, md: 4, lg: 4, xl: 4, '2xl': 4 },
    94→  5: { base: 2, sm: 3, md: 4, lg: 5, xl: 5, '2xl': 5 },
    95→  6: { base: 2, sm: 3, md: 4, lg: 5, xl: 6, '2xl': 6 },
    96→  7: { base: 3, sm: 4, md: 5, lg: 6, xl: 7, '2xl': 7 },
    97→  8: { base: 3, sm: 4, md: 5, lg: 6, xl: 7, '2xl': 8 },
    98→  9: { base: 3, sm: 5, md: 6, lg: 7, xl: 8, '2xl': 9 },
    99→  10: { base: 3, sm: 5, md: 6, lg: 8, xl: 9, '2xl': 10 },
   100→  11: { base: 3, sm: 5, md: 7, lg: 8, xl: 10, '2xl': 11 },
   101→  12: { base: 4, sm: 6, md: 7, lg: 9, xl: 10, '2xl': 12 },
   102→} as const;
   103→
   104→/**
   105→ * Parse an aspect ratio string (e.g., "16:9") into a numeric ratio (width/height)
   106→ */
   107→function parseAspectRatio(aspectRatioStr: string | undefined | null): number {
   108→  if (!aspectRatioStr) return 16 / 9; // Default to 16:9
   109→  const parts = aspectRatioStr.split(':');
   110→  if (parts.length !== 2) return 16 / 9;
   111→  const width = parseFloat(parts[0]);
   112→  const height = parseFloat(parts[1]);
   113→  if (isNaN(width) || isNaN(height) || height === 0) return 16 / 9;
   114→  return width / height;
   115→}
   116→
   117→/**
   118→ * Calculate the target image width.
   119→ *
   120→ * Uses a consistent target width regardless of aspect ratio.
   121→ * The actual displayed width depends on the grid column count,
   122→ * which is calculated from container width / target width.
   123→ */
   124→function getTargetImageWidth(_aspectRatio: number): number {
   125→  return TARGET_IMAGE_WIDTH.BASE;
   126→}
   127→
   128→/**
   129→ * Calculate optimal columns based on container width and image aspect ratio.
   130→ *
   131→ * @param containerWidth - The actual width of the gallery container in pixels
   132→ * @param aspectRatio - width/height ratio of images (e.g., 1.78 for 16:9)
   133→ * @returns Number of columns that fit, clamped to MIN/MAX range
   134→ */
   135→function calculateDynamicColumns(
   136→  containerWidth: number,
   137→  aspectRatio: number,
   138→  gap: number = 16
   139→): number {
   140→  if (!containerWidth || containerWidth <= 0) {
   141→    // Fallback to aspect-ratio-only calculation when container width unknown
   142→    return getColumnsForAspectRatio(aspectRatio);
   143→  }
   144→
   145→  const targetWidth = getTargetImageWidth(aspectRatio);
   146→  // Account for gaps: totalWidth = n*imageWidth + (n-1)*gap
   147→  // Solve for n: n = (containerWidth + gap) / (targetWidth + gap)
   148→  const effectiveWidth = targetWidth + gap;
   149→  const columns = Math.floor((containerWidth + gap) / effectiveWidth);
   150→
   151→  return Math.max(
   152→    TARGET_IMAGE_WIDTH.MIN_COLUMNS,
   153→    Math.min(TARGET_IMAGE_WIDTH.MAX_COLUMNS, columns)
   154→  );
   155→}
   156→
   157→/**
   158→ * Calculate optimal rows based on container dimensions and image aspect ratio.
   159→ *
   160→ * Uses the same logic as columns: given container height, how many rows fit?
   161→ * Row height is derived from column width (which comes from container width / columns)
   162→ * and the image aspect ratio.
   163→ *
   164→ * @param containerWidth - The width of the gallery container in pixels
   165→ * @param containerHeight - The available height for the gallery in pixels
   166→ * @param columns - Number of columns (already calculated)
   167→ * @param aspectRatio - width/height ratio of images (e.g., 1.78 for 16:9)
   168→ * @returns Number of rows that fit, clamped to MIN/MAX range
   169→ */
   170→function calculateDynamicRows(
   171→  containerWidth: number,
   172→  containerHeight: number,
   173→  columns: number,
   174→  aspectRatio: number,
   175→  gap: number = 16
   176→): number {
   177→  if (!containerWidth || containerWidth <= 0 || !containerHeight || containerHeight <= 0) {
   178→    return DEFAULT_ROWS_PER_PAGE.DESKTOP;
   179→  }
   180→
   181→  // Calculate actual image width based on container and columns
   182→  // containerWidth = columns * imageWidth + (columns - 1) * gap
   183→  // imageWidth = (containerWidth - (columns - 1) * gap) / columns
   184→  const totalGapWidth = (columns - 1) * gap;
   185→  const imageWidth = (containerWidth - totalGapWidth) / columns;
   186→
   187→  // Calculate image height from width and aspect ratio
   188→  // aspectRatio = width / height, so height = width / aspectRatio
   189→  const imageHeight = imageWidth / aspectRatio;
   190→
   191→  // Calculate how many rows fit in available height
   192→  // containerHeight = rows * imageHeight + (rows - 1) * gap
   193→  // Solve for rows: rows = (containerHeight + gap) / (imageHeight + gap)
   194→  // Subtract half a row height as safety margin so the last row isn't barely clipped
   195→  const effectiveHeight = imageHeight + gap;
   196→  const usableHeight = containerHeight - imageHeight * 0.5;
   197→  const rows = Math.floor((usableHeight + gap) / effectiveHeight);
   198→
   199→  const clamped = Math.max(
   200→    ROW_LIMITS.MIN_ROWS,
   201→    Math.min(ROW_LIMITS.MAX_ROWS, rows)
   202→  );
   203→
   204→  return clamped;
   205→}
   206→
   207→/**
   208→ * Calculate optimal columns per row based on aspect ratio.
   209→ *
   210→ * Wider images (16:9) → fewer columns (so each image isn't too wide)
   211→ * Taller images (9:16) → more columns (so each image isn't too tall)
   212→ *
   213→ * Uses sqrt for smoother scaling across the ratio range.
   214→ *
   215→ * @param aspectRatio - width/height ratio (e.g., 1.78 for 16:9, 0.56 for 9:16)
   216→ * @returns Number of columns (5-9 range)
   217→ */
   218→function getColumnsForAspectRatio(aspectRatio: number): number {
   219→  const BASE_COLUMNS = 5;
   220→  // Inverse relationship: wider = fewer columns, taller = more columns
   221→  // Add 2 to shift the range up (user requested +2 to all column counts)
   222→  const computed = Math.round(BASE_COLUMNS / Math.sqrt(aspectRatio)) + 2;
   223→  // Clamp to valid range (5-9)
   224→  return Math.max(5, Math.min(9, computed));
   225→}
   226→
   227→/**
   228→ * Get both columns and items per page based on aspect ratio and container dimensions.
   229→ * Convenience function that combines the above utilities.
   230→ *
   231→ * @param aspectRatioStr - Aspect ratio string (e.g., "16:9", "9:16")
   232→ * @param isMobile - Whether on mobile device
   233→ * @param containerWidth - Optional container width in pixels for dynamic column calculation
   234→ * @param containerHeight - Optional container height in pixels for dynamic row calculation
   235→ * @returns { columns, rows, itemsPerPage, skeletonColumns }
   236→ */
   237→export function getLayoutForAspectRatio(
   238→  aspectRatioStr: string | undefined | null,
   239→  isMobile: boolean,
   240→  containerWidth?: number,
   241→  containerHeight?: number,
   242→  reducedSpacing: boolean = false
   243→): {
   244→  columns: number;
   245→  rows: number;
   246→  itemsPerPage: number;
   247→  skeletonColumns: typeof SKELETON_COLUMNS[keyof typeof SKELETON_COLUMNS];
   248→  gridColumnClasses: string;
   249→} {
   250→  const ratio = parseAspectRatio(aspectRatioStr);
   251→  const gap = getEffectiveGap(reducedSpacing);
   252→
   253→  // Use dynamic calculation if container width is known, otherwise fall back to static
   254→  const rawColumns = containerWidth && containerWidth > 0
   255→    ? calculateDynamicColumns(containerWidth, ratio, gap)
   256→    : getColumnsForAspectRatio(ratio);
   257→
   258→  // Clamp to valid range for our predefined grid classes (3-12)
   259→  const clampedColumns = Math.max(3, Math.min(12, rawColumns)) as keyof typeof GRID_COLUMN_CLASSES;
   260→
   261→  // Use dynamic row calculation only on desktop when both width and height are known
   262→  // Mobile always uses fixed rows for consistent scrolling behavior
   263→  const rows = (!isMobile && containerWidth && containerWidth > 0 && containerHeight && containerHeight > 0)
   264→    ? calculateDynamicRows(containerWidth, containerHeight, rawColumns, ratio, gap)
   265→    : (isMobile ? DEFAULT_ROWS_PER_PAGE.MOBILE : DEFAULT_ROWS_PER_PAGE.DESKTOP);
   266→
   267→  const itemsPerPage = rawColumns * rows;
   268→  const skeletonColumns = SKELETON_COLUMNS[clampedColumns] || SKELETON_COLUMNS[5];
   269→  const gridColumnClasses = GRID_COLUMN_CLASSES[clampedColumns];
   270→
   271→  return { columns: rawColumns, rows, itemsPerPage, skeletonColumns, gridColumnClasses };
   272→}
   273→

1→/**
     2→ * Image Load Tracker
     3→ *
     4→ * Tracks which images have been loaded (preloaded or displayed).
     5→ * This is NOT a cache - it doesn't store image data, just tracks load status.
     6→ * The browser manages its own image cache; we just track what we've attempted to load.
     7→ *
     8→ * Used by:
     9→ * - Preloading system: marks images as loaded after preload completes
    10→ * - Progressive loading: checks if image was preloaded to skip animation delay
    11→ */
    12→
    13→import type { TrackableImage, TrackerLimits } from './types';
    14→
    15→// =============================================================================
    16→// CONFIGURATION
    17→// =============================================================================
    18→
    19→const getTrackerConfig = (): TrackerLimits => {
    20→  const isMobile = typeof window !== 'undefined' && window.innerWidth <= 768;
    21→  const hasLowMemory =
    22→    typeof navigator !== 'undefined' &&
    23→    'deviceMemory' in navigator &&
    24→    (navigator as { deviceMemory?: number }).deviceMemory !== undefined &&
    25→    (navigator as { deviceMemory: number }).deviceMemory <= 4;
    26→
    27→  if (isMobile || hasLowMemory) {
    28→    return { maxImages: 100, maxUrls: 150 };
    29→  }
    30→  return { maxImages: 300, maxUrls: 500 };
    31→};
    32→
    33→// =============================================================================
    34→// STATE
    35→// =============================================================================
    36→
    37→// Track loaded images by ID
    38→const loadedImagesById = new Map<string, boolean>();
    39→
    40→// Track loaded images by URL (for progressive loading)
    41→// Also stores element refs to prevent browser cache eviction
    42→const loadedImagesByUrl = new Map<
    43→  string,
    44→  { loadedAt: number; width?: number; height?: number; element?: HTMLImageElement }
    45→>();
    46→
    47→// =============================================================================
    48→// HELPERS
    49→// =============================================================================
    50→
    51→/**
    52→ * Evict oldest entries from a Map until it's under the limit.
    53→ * Maps maintain insertion order, so we delete from the beginning.
    54→ */
    55→const evictOldestEntries = <K, V>(
    56→  map: Map<K, V>,
    57→  maxSize: number,
    58→  name: string
    59→): number => {
    60→  if (map.size <= maxSize) return 0;
    61→
    62→  const toEvict = map.size - maxSize;
    63→  const keys = Array.from(map.keys()).slice(0, toEvict);
    64→
    65→  keys.forEach((key) => map.delete(key));
    66→
    67→  console.log(
    68→    `[ImageLoadTracker] Evicted ${toEvict} oldest entries from ${name}, new size: ${map.size}`
    69→  );
    70→  return toEvict;
    71→};
    72→
    73→// =============================================================================
    74→// PUBLIC API
    75→// =============================================================================
    76→
    77→/**
    78→ * Enforce tracker limits - call this periodically or after adding entries
    79→ */
    80→const enforceLoadTrackerLimits = (): void => {
    81→  const config = getTrackerConfig();
    82→  evictOldestEntries(loadedImagesById, config.maxImages, 'loadedImagesById');
    83→  evictOldestEntries(loadedImagesByUrl, config.maxUrls, 'loadedImagesByUrl');
    84→};
    85→
    86→/**
    87→ * Mark an image as loaded or not loaded
    88→ */
    89→export const setImageLoadStatus = (
    90→  image: TrackableImage,
    91→  isLoaded: boolean = true
    92→): void => {
    93→  const imageId = image.id;
    94→  if (!imageId) {
    95→    return;
    96→  }
    97→
    98→  // Update tracker
    99→  loadedImagesById.set(imageId, isLoaded);
   100→
   101→  // Update object property for backwards compatibility (will be phased out)
   102→  image.__memoryCached = isLoaded;
   103→
   104→  // Enforce limits after adding (debounced check - only every 50 entries)
   105→  if (isLoaded && loadedImagesById.size % 50 === 0) {
   106→    enforceLoadTrackerLimits();
   107→  }
   108→};
   109→
   110→/**
   111→ * Remove images from tracker (for cleanup when pages are evicted)
   112→ */
   113→const removeLoadedImages = (imageIds: string[]): number => {
   114→  let removedCount = 0;
   115→
   116→  imageIds.forEach((imageId) => {
   117→    if (loadedImagesById.has(imageId)) {
   118→      loadedImagesById.delete(imageId);
   119→      removedCount++;
   120→    }
   121→  });
   122→
   123→  return removedCount;
   124→};
   125→
   126→/**
   127→ * Clear load status for a set of images (used when evicting pages from cache)
   128→ */
   129→export const clearLoadedImages = (images: Array<{ id: string }>): number => {
   130→  const imageIds = images.map((img) => img.id).filter((id) => id);
   131→
   132→  return removeLoadedImages(imageIds);
   133→};
   134→
   135→/**
   136→ * Clear all tracked images (used on project switch)
   137→ */
   138→export const clearAllLoadedImages = (
   139→  reason: string = 'project switch'
   140→): number => {
   141→  const prevSize = loadedImagesById.size;
   142→  loadedImagesById.clear();
   143→  loadedImagesByUrl.clear();
   144→
   145→  console.log(
   146→    `[ImageLoadTracker] Cleared all for ${reason}, removed ${prevSize} entries`
   147→  );
   148→  return prevSize;
   149→};
   150→
   151→/**
   152→ * Check if an image has been loaded (by URL or image object)
   153→ */
   154→export const hasLoadedImage = (urlOrImage: string | TrackableImage): boolean => {
   155→  // URL string
   156→  if (typeof urlOrImage === 'string') {
   157→    return loadedImagesByUrl.has(urlOrImage);
   158→  }
   159→
   160→  // Image object
   161→  const imageId = urlOrImage?.id;
   162→  if (!imageId) {
   163→    return false;
   164→  }
   165→
   166→  const isLoaded = loadedImagesById.get(imageId) === true;
   167→
   168→  // Sync object property if needed (backwards compatibility)
   169→  if (isLoaded && urlOrImage.__memoryCached !== true) {
   170→    urlOrImage.__memoryCached = true;
   171→  }
   172→
   173→  return isLoaded;
   174→};
   175→
   176→/**
   177→ * Mark an image as loaded (by URL or image object)
   178→ * Optionally stores the HTMLImageElement ref to prevent browser cache eviction.
   179→ */
   180→export const markImageLoaded = (
   181→  urlOrImage: string | TrackableImage,
   182→  metadata?: { width?: number; height?: number; element?: HTMLImageElement }
   183→): void => {
   184→  // URL string
   185→  if (typeof urlOrImage === 'string') {
   186→    loadedImagesByUrl.set(urlOrImage, {
   187→      loadedAt: Date.now(),
   188→      ...metadata,
   189→    });
   190→    // Enforce limits after adding (debounced check - only every 50 entries)
   191→    if (loadedImagesByUrl.size % 50 === 0) {
   192→      enforceLoadTrackerLimits();
   193→    }
   194→    return;
   195→  }
   196→
   197→  // Image object
   198→  setImageLoadStatus(urlOrImage, true);
   199→};
   200→
   201→/**
   202→ * Get tracker statistics for debugging
   203→ */
   204→export const getLoadTrackerStats = (): {
   205→  byId: number;
   206→  byUrl: number;
   207→  limits: TrackerLimits;
   208→} => {
   209→  const config = getTrackerConfig();
   210→  return {
   211→    byId: loadedImagesById.size,
   212→    byUrl: loadedImagesByUrl.size,
   213→    limits: config,
   214→  };
   215→};
   216→
   217→/**
   218→ * Get the stored HTMLImageElement for a URL (if available).
   219→ * Used to verify browser cache status without creating a new Image.
   220→ */
   221→export const getImageElement = (url: string): HTMLImageElement | undefined => {
   222→  return loadedImagesByUrl.get(url)?.element;
   223→};
   224→
   225→

1→/**
     2→ * useMarkVariantViewed Hook
     3→ *
     4→ * Marks a variant as viewed in the database and invalidates all relevant queries.
     5→ * Used when user views a variant in the lightbox to remove the NEW badge.
     6→ *
     7→ * Now includes optimistic update support - the badge count is decremented immediately
     8→ * before the database update completes.
     9→ *
    10→ * Usage:
    11→ *   const { markViewed, markAllViewed } = useMarkVariantViewed();
    12→ *   markViewed({ variantId, generationId }); // generationId enables optimistic update
    13→ *   markAllViewed(generationId); // marks all unviewed variants for a generation
    14→ */

    16→import { useMutation, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';

    26→/**

    29→export const extractVideoMetadata = async (file: File): Promise<VideoMetadata> => {

   101→/**
   102→ * Uploads a video file to Supabase storage with real progress tracking,
   103→ * timeout, abort support, and stall detection.
   104→ *
   105→ * Note: projectId and shotId params are kept for backwards compatibility but
   106→ * are no longer used in the storage path (tracked in DB instead).
   107→ */
   108→export const uploadVideoToStorage = async (
   109→  file: File,
   110→  _projectId: string,
   111→  _shotId: string,
   112→  onProgressOrOptions?: ((progress: number) => void) | VideoUploadOptions,
   113→  maxRetriesParam: number = 3
   114→): Promise<string> => {
   115→  // Handle both old signature and new options object
   116→  let options: VideoUploadOptions;
   117→  if (typeof onProgressOrOptions === 'function') {
   118→    options = { onProgress: onProgressOrOptions, maxRetries: maxRetriesParam };
   119→  } else {
   120→    options = onProgressOrOptions || {};
   121→  }
   122→
   123→  const {
   124→    onProgress,
   125→    maxRetries = 3,
   126→    signal,
   127→    timeoutMs = DEFAULT_VIDEO_TIMEOUT_MS
   128→  } = options;
   129→
   130→  // Check if already aborted
   131→  if (signal?.aborted) {
   132→    throw new Error('Upload cancelled');
   133→  }
   134→
   135→  // Get session for auth and user ID (initial check)
   136→  const { data: initialSessionData } = await supabase.auth.getSession();
   137→  if (!initialSessionData?.session?.access_token || !initialSessionData?.session?.user?.id) {
   138→    throw new Error('No active session');
   139→  }
   140→  const userId = initialSessionData.session.user.id;
   141→
   142→  // Generate storage path using centralized utilities
   143→  const fileExt = getFileExtension(file.name, file.type, 'mp4');
   144→  const filename = generateUniqueFilename(fileExt);
   145→  const fileName = storagePaths.upload(userId, filename);
   146→
   147→  const fileSizeMB = (file.size / (1024 * 1024)).toFixed(2);
   148→
   149→  let lastError: Error | null = null;
   150→
   151→  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < maxRetries; attempt++) {
   152→    // Check abort before each attempt
   153→    if (signal?.aborted) {
   154→      throw new Error('Upload cancelled');
   155→    }
   156→
   157→    // Refresh session token before each attempt (tokens can expire during retries)
   158→    const { data: sessionData } = await supabase.auth.getSession();
   159→    const accessToken = sessionData?.session?.access_token;
   160→    if (!accessToken) {
   161→      throw new Error('Session expired - please sign in again');
   162→    }
   163→
   164→    try {
   165→
   166→      const bucketUrl = `${SUPABASE_URL}/storage/v1/object/${MEDIA_BUCKET}/${fileName}`;
   167→
   168→      // Upload with XMLHttpRequest to track progress, with timeout and stall detection
   169→      await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
   170→        const xhr = new XMLHttpRequest();
   171→        let lastProgressTime = Date.now();
   172→        let stallCheckInterval: ReturnType<typeof setInterval> | null = null;
   173→        let overallTimeout: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
   174→
   175→        const cleanup = () => {
   176→          if (stallCheckInterval) clearInterval(stallCheckInterval);
   177→          if (overallTimeout) clearTimeout(overallTimeout);
   178→        };
   179→
   180→        // Overall timeout
   181→        overallTimeout = setTimeout(() => {
   182→          cleanup();
   183→          xhr.abort();
   184→          reject(new Error(`Upload timed out after ${timeoutMs}ms`));
   185→        }, timeoutMs);
   186→
   187→        // Stall detection - check every 10 seconds if we've had progress
   188→        stallCheckInterval = setInterval(() => {
   189→          const timeSinceLastProgress = Date.now() - lastProgressTime;
   190→          if (timeSinceLastProgress > STALL_TIMEOUT_MS) {
   191→            cleanup();
   192→            xhr.abort();
   193→            reject(new Error(`Upload stalled - no progress for ${STALL_TIMEOUT_MS}ms`));
   194→          }
   195→        }, 10000);
   196→
   197→        // Handle abort signal
   198→        const abortHandler = () => {
   199→          cleanup();
   200→          xhr.abort();
   201→          reject(new Error('Upload cancelled'));
   202→        };
   203→        signal?.addEventListener('abort', abortHandler);
   204→
   205→        // Track upload progress
   206→        xhr.upload.addEventListener('progress', (e) => {
   207→          lastProgressTime = Date.now();
   208→          if (e.lengthComputable) {
   209→            const percentComplete = Math.round((e.loaded / e.total) * 100);
   210→            onProgress?.(percentComplete);
   211→          }

   213→
   214→        xhr.addEventListener('load', () => {

   220→          } else {

   222→          }
   223→        });
   224→
   225→        xhr.addEventListener('error', () => {

   227→          signal?.removeEventListener('abort', abortHandler);
   228→          reject(new Error('Network error during upload'));
   229→        });
   230→
   231→        xhr.addEventListener('abort', () => {
   232→          cleanup();

   234→          // Reject if not already rejected by timeout/stall/signal handlers
   235→          reject(new Error('Upload aborted'));

   252→
   253→    } catch (error) {

   255→      handleError(lastError, { context: 'VideoUploader', showToast: false });

   257→      // Don't retry for user cancellation

     3→ *
     4→ * Utilities for prefetching task data for generations.
     5→ * Used for hover prefetch in galleries and lightboxes.
     6→ *
     7→ * These hooks use immutable caching since generation→task mapping never changes once created.

    10→import { useCallback } from 'react';
    11→import { useQuery, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';
    12→import { supabase } from '@/integrations/supabase/client';

    16→/**

    18→ * Uses immutable caching since generation→task mapping never changes once created.
    19→ *
    20→ * @param generationId - The generation ID to get task data for
    21→ * @returns Query result with { taskId: string | null }
    22→ */
    23→export function useTaskFromUnifiedCache(generationId: string) {
    24→  const result = useQuery({
    25→    [REDACTED](generationId),
    26→    queryFn: async () => {
    27→      // Fetch task ID from generations table
    28→      // Note: React Query won't call this if data is cached (staleTime: Infinity)
    29→      const { data, error } = await supabase
    30→        .from('generations')
    31→        .select('tasks')
    32→        .eq('id', generationId)
    33→        .maybeSingle();
    34→
    35→      if (error) {
    36→        throw error;
    37→      }
    38→
    39→      // Return null taskId if generation doesn't exist or has no tasks
    40→      if (!data) {
    41→        return { taskId: null };
    42→      }
    43→
    44→      const taskId = Array.isArray(data?.tasks) && data.tasks.length > 0 ? data.tasks[0] : null;
    45→      return { taskId };
    46→    },
    47→    // Generation→task mapping is immutable - cache aggressively
    48→    staleTime: Infinity,
    49→    gcTime: 30 * 60 * 1000, // 30 minutes
    50→    refetchOnMount: false,
    51→    refetchOnWindowFocus: false,
    52→    refetchOnReconnect: false,
    53→    enabled: !!generationId,
    54→  });

    56→  return result;
