    43→  };
    44→}
    45→
    46→// Cached settings loader to prevent duplicate database calls  
    47→const loadUserSettingsCached = async (userId: string) => {
    48→  const cacheKey = `user_settings_${userId}`;
    49→  const cached = settingsCache.get(cacheKey);
    50→  
    51→  // Return fresh cached data
    52→  if (cached && (Date.now() - cached.timestamp) < CACHE_DURATION) {
    53→    return cached.data;
    54→  }
    55→  
    56→  // If there's already a loading request, wait for it
    57→  if (cached?.loading) {
    58→    return await cached.loading;
    59→  }
    60→  
    61→  // Make new database call and cache the promise
    62→  const loadingPromise = supabase
    63→    .from('users')
    64→    .select('settings')
    65→    .eq('id', userId)
    66→    .single()
    67→    .then(result => {
    68→      // Cache the result
    69→      settingsCache.set(cacheKey, {
    70→        data: result,
    71→        timestamp: Date.now(),
    72→        loading: null
    73→      });
    74→      return result;
    75→    })
    76→    .catch(error => {
    77→      // Remove loading state on error
    78→      settingsCache.delete(cacheKey);
    79→      throw error;
    80→    });
    81→  
    82→  // Cache the loading promise to prevent duplicate requests
    83→  settingsCache.set(cacheKey, {
    84→    data: cached?.data || null,
    85→    timestamp: cached?.timestamp || 0,
    86→    loading: loadingPromise
    87→  });
    88→  
    89→  return await loadingPromise;
    90→};
    91→
    92→/**
    93→ * Hook for user-scoped UI preferences (theme, pane locks, generation methods, etc.).
    94→ *
    95→ * Scope: user-only (stored in `users.settings.ui`).
    96→ * Auto-save: yes, 200ms debounce via the global settings write queue.
    97→ *
    98→ * Use this for preferences that follow the user across all projects/shots.
    99→ * For project/shot-scoped settings, use `useAutoSaveSettings` instead.
   100→ *
   101→ * @see docs/structure_detail/settings_system.md for the full settings hook decision tree
   102→ */
   103→export function useUserUIState<K extends keyof UISettings>(
   104→  key: K,
   105→  fallback: UISettings[K]
   106→) {
   107→  // Normalize logic specific to generationMethods to avoid ambiguous "both true" state.
   108→  // Allowed states:
   109→  // - inCloud: true, onComputer: false
   110→  // - inCloud: false, onComputer: true
   111→  // - inCloud: false, onComputer: false (explicitly disabled, used for warnings)
   112→  // Not allowed:
   113→  // - inCloud: true, onComputer: true → normalize to cloud by default
   114→  const normalizeIfGenerationMethods = (val: UISettings[K]): UISettings[K] => {
   115→    if ((key as string) !== 'generationMethods') return val;
   116→    if (!val || typeof val !== 'object') return val;
   117→    const valObj = val as unknown as Record<string, unknown>;
   118→    const inCloud = Boolean(valObj.inCloud);
   119→    const onComputer = Boolean(valObj.onComputer);
   120→    if (inCloud && onComputer) {
   121→      return { inCloud: true, onComputer: false } as UISettings[K];
   122→    }
   123→    return { inCloud, onComputer } as UISettings[K];
   124→  };
   125→  const [value, setValue] = useState<UISettings[K]>(fallback);
   126→  const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(true);
   127→  const userIdRef = useRef<string>();
   128→  const debounceRef = useRef<NodeJS.Timeout>();
   129→
   130→  // Helper function to save fallback values to database (preserves all existing settings)
   131→  // This automatically backfills existing users with default values when they first load the app
   132→  // IMPORTANT: Only runs when the key is completely missing from database (undefined)
   133→  // Does NOT override explicit user choices (including both options set to false)
   134→  const saveFallbackToDatabase = async (userId: string, _currentSettings: Record<string, unknown>) => {
   135→    try {
   136→      const fallbackToSave = normalizeIfGenerationMethods(fallback);
   137→      
   138→      // Use the global queue to save - it handles merging
   139→      await updateToolSettingsSupabase({
   140→        scope: 'user',
   141→        id: userId,
   142→        toolId: 'ui',
   143→        patch: { [key]: fallbackToSave },
   144→      }, undefined, 'immediate');
   145→      
   146→      // Invalidate cache so other components see the backfilled values
   147→      const cacheKey = `user_settings_${userId}`;
   148→      settingsCache.delete(cacheKey);
   149→      setValue(fallbackToSave); // Update local state after successful save
   150→    } catch (error) {
   151→      handleError(error, { context: 'useUserUIState.saveFallbackToDatabase', showToast: false });
   152→    }
   153→  };
   154→
   155→  // Load initial value from database
   156→  useEffect(() => {
   157→    const loadUserSettings = async () => {
   158→      try {
   159→        const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();
   160→        if (!user) {
   161→          // Skip loading for unauthenticated users (e.g., on public share pages)
   162→          setIsLoading(false);
   163→          return;
   164→        }
   165→
   166→        userIdRef.current = user.id;
   167→
   168→        const { data, error } = await loadUserSettingsCached(user.id);
   169→
   170→        if (error) {
   171→          handleError(error, { context: 'useUserUIState.loadSettings', showToast: false });
   172→          setIsLoading(false);
   173→          return;
   174→        }
   175→
   176→        const uiSettings = data?.settings?.ui;
   177→        const keyValue = uiSettings?.[key];
   178→        
   179→        if (keyValue !== undefined) {
   180→          // Key exists in database - merge with fallback to backfill any missing fields
   181→          const mergedValue = (typeof fallback === 'object' && fallback !== null)
   182→            ? ({ ...fallback, ...(keyValue as object) } as UISettings[K])
   183→            : (keyValue as UISettings[K]);
   184→
   185→          const normalizedValue = normalizeIfGenerationMethods(mergedValue);
   186→          setValue(normalizedValue);
   187→
   188→          // If any fields from the fallback are missing in the stored value OR
   189→          // normalization changed the value, backfill them in DB
   190→          if (
   191→            (typeof keyValue === 'object' && keyValue !== null &&
   192→            typeof fallback === 'object' && fallback !== null &&
   193→            Object.keys(fallback as object).some((k) => (keyValue as Record<string, unknown>)[k] === undefined)) ||
   194→            JSON.stringify(normalizedValue) !== JSON.stringify(keyValue)
   195→          ) {
   196→            // Use the global queue to save - it handles merging
   197→            updateToolSettingsSupabase({
   198→              scope: 'user',
   199→              id: user.id,
   200→              toolId: 'ui',
   201→              patch: { [key]: normalizedValue },
   202→            }, undefined, 'immediate').then(() => {
   203→              const cacheKey = `user_settings_${user.id}`;
   204→              settingsCache.delete(cacheKey);
   205→            }).catch(e => {
   206→              handleError(e, { context: 'useUserUIState.backfillFields', showToast: false });
   207→            });
   208→          }
   209→        } else {
   210→          // Key doesn't exist in database - this is an existing user who hasn't set preferences yet
   211→          // Save fallback values to backfill them (only runs when completely empty)
   212→          const normalizedFallback = normalizeIfGenerationMethods(fallback);
   213→          setValue(normalizedFallback); // Set normalized fallback immediately for responsive UI
   214→          
   215→          // Save to database in background (don't block loading)
   216→          saveFallbackToDatabase(user.id, data?.settings || {}).catch(error => {
   217→            handleError(error, { context: 'useUserUIState.saveFallback', showToast: false });
   218→          });
   219→        }
   220→        
   221→        setIsLoading(false);
   222→      } catch (error) {
   223→        handleError(error, { context: 'useUserUIState.loadUserSettings', showToast: false });
   224→        setIsLoading(false);
   225→      }
   226→    };
   227→
   228→    loadUserSettings();
   229→  }, [key]); // Remove fallback from deps to prevent unnecessary re-runs
   230→
   231→  // Debounced update function
   232→  // Uses the global settings write queue (via updateToolSettingsSupabase) to prevent
   233→  // race conditions with other hooks that write to users.settings (e.g., useToolSettings
   234→  // writing user-preferences). The write queue serializes writes and uses an atomic RPC.
   235→  const update = (patch: Partial<UISettings[K]>) => {
   236→    // Immediately update local state for responsive UI (with normalization)
   237→    const normalizedPatch = normalizeIfGenerationMethods({
   238→      ...(value as object),
   239→      ...(patch as object)
   240→    } as UISettings[K]);
   241→    setValue(normalizedPatch);
   242→
   243→    // Clear existing timeout
   244→    if (debounceRef.current) {
   245→      clearTimeout(debounceRef.current);
   246→    }
   247→
   248→    // Debounce the database write via the global settings write queue
   249→    debounceRef.current = setTimeout(async () => {
   250→      const userId = userIdRef.current;
   251→      if (!userId) return;
   252→
   253→      try {
   254→        // Use the write queue which handles atomic DB updates and merging.
   255→        // This prevents race conditions with other hooks writing to users.settings.
   256→        await updateToolSettingsSupabase({
   257→          scope: 'user',
   258→          id: userId,
   259→          toolId: 'ui',
   260→          patch: { [key]: normalizedPatch },
   261→        });
   262→
   263→        // Invalidate local cache so other useUserUIState instances see the update
   264→        const cacheKey = `user_settings_${userId}`;
   265→        settingsCache.delete(cacheKey);
   266→      } catch (error) {
   267→        handleError(error, { context: 'useUserUIState.update', showToast: false });
   268→      }
   269→    }, 200);
   270→  };
   271→
   272→  // Cleanup timeout on unmount
   273→  useEffect(() => {
   274→    return () => {
   275→      if (debounceRef.current) {
   276→        clearTimeout(debounceRef.current);
   277→      }
   278→    };
   279→  }, []);
   280→
   281→  return { 
   282→    value, 
   283→    update, 
   284→    isLoading 
   285→  };
   286→}

   323→            // Also invalidate without v2 for backwards compatibility
   324→            queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: [...queryKeys.resources.all, data.type] });
   325→            queryClient.invalidateQueries({ [REDACTED](data.type) });
   326→            // Invalidate specific-resources queries that include this resource ID
   327→            // Using predicate to find any query that contains this resource ID
   328→            queryClient.invalidateQueries({
   329→                predicate: (query) => {
   330→                    const key = query.queryKey;
   331→                    if (key[0] === 'specific-resources' && typeof key[1] === 'string') {
   332→                        return key[1].includes(data.id);
   333→                    }
   334→                    return false;
   335→                }
   336→            });
   337→        },
   338→        onError: (error) => {
   339→            handleError(error, { context: 'useUpdateResource', toastTitle: 'Failed to update resource' });
   340→        },
   341→    });
   342→};

   348→        mutationFn: async ({ id }) => {
   349→            const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();
   350→            if (!user) throw new Error('Not authenticated');
   351→
   352→            const { error } = await supabase

   365→            queryClient.invalidateQueries({ [REDACTED](variables.type) });

   369→        },
   370→    });

   107→  const [userHasManuallyInteracted, setUserHasManuallyInteracted] = useState(false);
   108→  const [lastSavedLoras, setLastSavedLoras] = useState<{ id: string; strength: number }[] | null>(null);
   109→
   110→  // Refs to hold current state for callbacks, preventing stale closures
   111→  const selectedLorasRef = useRef(selectedLoras);
   112→  useEffect(() => {
   113→    selectedLorasRef.current = selectedLoras;
   114→  }, [selectedLoras]);
   115→
   116→  // Track latest prompt value for trigger words

   118→
   119→  // Update ref when prompt changes
   120→  useEffect(() => {
   121→    latestPromptRef.current = currentPrompt;
   122→  }, [currentPrompt]);
   123→
   124→  // Universal persistence settings based on scope
   125→  const {
   126→    settings: persistenceSettings,
   127→    update: updatePersistenceSettings,
   128→    isUpdating: isSavingLoras
   129→  } = useToolSettings<{ 
   130→    loras?: { id: string; strength: number }[];
   131→    hasEverSetLoras?: boolean;
   132→  }>(
   133→    persistenceKey,
   134→    { 
   135→      projectId: persistenceScope === 'project' ? projectId : (enableProjectPersistence ? projectId : undefined),
   136→      shotId: persistenceScope === 'shot' ? shotId : undefined,
   137→      enabled: persistenceScope !== 'none' || enableProjectPersistence
   138→    }
   139→  );
   140→
   141→  // Legacy project LoRA settings for backward compatibility
   142→  const projectLoraSettings = enableProjectPersistence ? persistenceSettings : undefined;
   143→
   144→  // Universal mark as user set function
   145→  const markAsUserSet = useCallback(() => {
   146→    setHasEverSetLoras(true);
   147→    setUserHasManuallyInteracted(true);
   148→  }, []);
   149→
   150→  // Core handlers with universal user tracking
   151→  const handleAddLora = useCallback((loraToAdd: LoraModel, isManualAction = true, initialStrength?: number) => {
   152→    // Use the ref to ensure we are checking against the most up-to-date selection.
   153→    if (selectedLorasRef.current.find(sl => sl.id === loraToAdd["Model ID"])) {
   154→      return;
   155→    }
   156→
   157→    if (loraToAdd["Model Files"] && loraToAdd["Model Files"].length > 0) {
   158→      const loraName = loraToAdd.Name !== "N/A" ? loraToAdd.Name : loraToAdd["Model ID"];
   159→
   160→      // Determine if this is a multi-stage LoRA (has high_noise_url OR low_noise_url)
   161→      const hasHighNoise = !!loraToAdd.high_noise_url;
   162→      const hasLowNoise = !!loraToAdd.low_noise_url;
   163→      const isMultiStage = hasHighNoise || hasLowNoise;
   164→
   165→      // For multi-stage LoRAs, use high_noise_url as the primary path (if available)
   166→      // For single-stage, use the Model Files URL
   167→      const primaryPath = isMultiStage
   168→        ? (loraToAdd.high_noise_url || loraToAdd.low_noise_url) // Prefer high, fallback to low
   169→        : (loraToAdd["Model Files"][0].url || loraToAdd["Model Files"][0].path);
   170→
   171→      const newLora: ActiveLora = {
   172→        id: loraToAdd["Model ID"],
   173→        name: loraName,
   174→        path: hasHighNoise ? loraToAdd.high_noise_url : primaryPath, // High noise URL or single URL
   175→        strength: initialStrength || 1.0, // Use provided strength or default to 1.0
   176→        previewImageUrl: loraToAdd.Images && loraToAdd.Images.length > 0
   177→          ? loraToAdd.Images[0].url
   178→          : undefined,
   179→        trigger_word: loraToAdd.trigger_word,
   180→        // Multi-stage fields - store both even if one is undefined
   181→        lowNoisePath: hasLowNoise ? loraToAdd.low_noise_url : undefined,
   182→        isMultiStage,
   183→      };
   184→      setSelectedLoras(prev => [...prev, newLora]);
   185→      if (isManualAction) {

   187→      }
   188→    } else {
   189→      toast.error("Selected LoRA has no model file specified.");

   191→  }, [markAsUserSet]);
   192→
   193→  const handleRemoveLora = useCallback((loraIdToRemove: string, isManualAction = true) => {
   194→    const loraToRemove = selectedLoras.find(lora => lora.id === loraIdToRemove);

   196→      return;

   202→    }
   203→  }, [selectedLoras, markAsUserSet]);

   205→  const handleLoraStrengthChange = useCallback((loraId: string, newStrength: number) => {
   206→    setSelectedLoras(prev =>

   208→        lora.id === loraId ? { ...lora, strength: newStrength } : lora
   209→      )

   212→  }, [markAsUserSet]);

   214→  // Trigger word functionality
   215→  const handleAddTriggerWord = useCallback((triggerWord: string) => {

   218→    const currentPromptValue = latestPromptRef.current || '';

   223→    onPromptUpdate(newPrompt);

   227→
   228→  // Universal persistence functionality
   229→  const handleSaveProjectLoras = useCallback(async () => {

   231→      return;

   233→
   234→    // Trigger flash immediately when button is pressed

   236→
   237→    try {
   238→      const lorasToSave = selectedLorasRef.current.map(lora => ({
   239→        id: lora.id,
   240→        strength: lora.strength
   241→      }));
   242→
   243→      const settingsToSave = { 
   244→        loras: lorasToSave,
   245→        hasEverSetLoras: true
   246→      };
   247→
   248→      // Use universal persistence settings
   249→      await updatePersistenceSettings('project', settingsToSave);

   251→      // Update local cache of saved LoRAs for immediate tooltip update
   252→      setLastSavedLoras(lorasToSave);

   255→      // Only clear flash and show success after save completes

   257→      setSaveSuccess(true);
   258→      setTimeout(() => setSaveSuccess(false), 2000); // Clear success after 2 seconds
   259→    } catch (error) {
   260→      handleError(error, { context: 'useLoraManager', showToast: false });
   261→      setSaveFlash(false); // Clear flash on error too
   262→    }
   263→  }, [enableProjectPersistence, projectId, updatePersistenceSettings, markAsUserSet]);
   264→
   265→  const handleLoadProjectLoras = useCallback(async () => {
   266→    if (!enableProjectPersistence) return;
   267→
   268→    const savedLoras = projectLoraSettings?.loras;

   271→    }

   273→    try {

   279→      const currentLoraIds = new Set(currentLoras.map(lora => lora.id));

   281→      // Remove LoRAs that are not in the saved list
   282→      const lorasToRemove = currentLoras.filter(lora => !savedLoraIds.has(lora.id));

   284→
   285→      // Add LoRAs that are not currently selected
   286→      const lorasToAdd = savedLoras.filter(savedLora => !currentLoraIds.has(savedLora.id));
   287→
   288→      // Add missing LoRAs with correct strength immediately
   289→      for (const savedLora of lorasToAdd) {
   290→        const availableLora = availableLoras.find(lora => lora['Model ID'] === savedLora.id);

   299→      savedLoras.forEach(savedLora => {

   317→    handleLoraStrengthChange,

   320→
   321→  // Initialize user preference state from persistence

   356→    return true;

  "content": "import { describe, it, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';\nimport { renderHook, act } from '@testing-library/react';\nimport { useTimestampUpdater, useTimestampVisibility } from '../useTimestampUpdater';\n\ndescribe('useTimestampUpdater', () => {\n  beforeEach(() => {\n    vi.useFakeTimers();\n  });\n\n  afterEach(() => {\n    vi.useRealTimers();\n  });\n\n  it('returns initial state with a valid date', () => {\n    const { result } = renderHook(() =>\n      useTimestampUpdater({ date: new Date() })\n    );\n\n    expect(result.current.updateTrigger).toBe(0);\n    expect(result.current.date).toBeInstanceOf(Date);\n    expect(result.current.currentInterval).toBeTypeOf('number');\n  });\n\n  it('returns null currentInterval when date is null', () => {\n    const { result } = renderHook(() =>\n      useTimestampUpdater({ date: null })\n    );\n\n    expect(result.current.date).toBeNull();\n    expect(result.current.currentInterval).toBeNull();\n  });\n\n  it('accepts date strings', () => {\n    const dateStr = '2025-01-15T12:00:00Z';\n    const { result } = renderHook(() =>\n      useTimestampUpdater({ date: dateStr })\n    );\n\n    expect(result.current.date).toBeInstanceOf(Date);\n    expect(result.current.date?.toISOString()).toBe(new Date(dateStr).toISOString());\n  });\n\n  it('returns short interval for recent timestamps', () => {\n    const recentDate = new Date(Date.now() - 60 * 1000); // 1 minute ago\n    const { result } = renderHook(() =>\n      useTimestampUpdater({ date: recentDate })\n    );\n\n    // Less than 5 minutes old → 10 second interval\n    expect(result.current.currentInterval).toBe(10);\n  });\n\n  it('returns medium interval for older timestamps', () => {\n    const olderDate = new Date(Date.now() - 30 * 60 * 1000); // 30 minutes ago\n    const { result } = renderHook(() =>\n      useTimestampUpdater({ date: olderDate })\n    );\n\n    // Less than 1 hour old → 60 second interval\n    expect(result.current.currentInterval).toBe(60);\n  });\n\n  it('returns long interval for day-old timestamps', () => {\n    const dayOld = new Date(Date.now() - 12 * 60 * 60 * 1000); // 12 hours ago\n    const { result } = renderHook(() =>\n      useTimestampUpdater({ date: dayOld })\n    );\n\n    // Less than 1 day old → 300 second interval\n    expect(result.current.currentInterval).toBe(300);\n  });\n\n  it('returns longest interval for very old timestamps', () => {\n    const veryOld = new Date(Date.now() - 3 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000); // 3 days ago\n    const { result } = renderHook(() =>\n      useTimestampUpdater({ date: veryOld })\n    );\n\n    // Older than 1 day → 1800 second interval\n    expect(result.current.currentInterval).toBe(1800);\n  });\n\n  it('does not subscribe when disabled', () => {\n    const { result } = renderHook(() =>\n      useTimestampUpdater({ date: new Date(), disabled: true })\n    );\n\n    expect(result.current.updateTrigger).toBe(0);\n  });\n\n  it('does not subscribe when not visible', () => {\n    const { result } = renderHook(() =>\n      useTimestampUpdater({ date: new Date(), isVisible: false })\n    );\n\n    expect(result.current.updateTrigger).toBe(0);\n  });\n});\n\ndescribe('useTimestampVisibility', () => {\n  it('defaults to visible', () => {\n    const ref = { current: null } as React.RefObject<HTMLElement>;\n    const { result } = renderHook(() => useTimestampVisibility(ref));\n\n    expect(result.current).toBe(true);\n  });\n});\n"

The behavior is: when progressive is disabled, `displayImageUrl = getDisplayUrl(thumbUrl || imageUrl)`. So if `thumbUrl` is provided, it uses that first. The test expected `full.jpg` but the hook returns `thumb.jpg` when progressive is disabled and thumbUrl is set. The test assertion is wrong -- fix it.

    47→  } = options;

### Key patterns used across all tests

- **`vi.hoisted()`** for mock variables referenced inside `vi.mock()` factories (required because `vi.mock` is hoisted above variable declarations)
- **`vi.mock()`** before imports for all external dependencies (supabase, error handlers, storage paths, etc.)
- **DOM mocking** via `vi.spyOn(document, 'createElement')` for video/canvas elements with event simulation via `setTimeout`
- **Supabase mock chaining** with `.from().select().eq().single()` patterns using `mockReturnThis()`
- **XHR avoidance** in uploader tests - tests verify early-exit paths (null file, abort, no session) rather than triggering actual HTTP requests that jsdom cannot handle
